children.translated_text: The Preface (<s>Bhūmikā</s>).
Salutation to the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s>.
Salutation to the blessed <s>Nigamānta Mahādeśika</s>.

children.text:
śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthadeśikamaṇiprajñāsarittaraṅgaparamparāpariṇāmabhūtaṃ nyāyapariśuddhyabhidhānaṃ prabandharatnamidaṃ jayati jīvitamiva nyāyavistarasya vidyāsthānasya śrībhagavadrāmānujamunivarakṣuṇṇavartmano brahmamīmāṃsāśāstrasya ca /
anupajīvya cedaṃ vidyāsthānaṃ ko vibhavaḥ sapanditumapi śeṣasya vidyāsthānajātasya ? /
sarvameva hi loke śrutaṃ saṃśayaviparyayābhyāmāhitapāriplavaṃ vātyāspṛṣṭamiva tṛṇaśakalaṃ na kathañcidapi pratitiṣṭhati /
pramāṇaparīkṣayā tu yathāvadupapāditayā dṛṣadeva vyapoḍhavikṣobhaṃ niṣkampamavatiṣṭhate /
pramāṇaparīkṣaiva ca prathamāvatārapadavī nyāyavistarasya /
padavākyapramāṇabhedena hi tredhā vibhajanti śāstraṃ śāstravidaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the knowers of <s>śāstra</s> divide the sciences threefold according to the distinction of <s>pada</s> (word), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), and <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge).
Among these, <s>pada</s> refers to the science of grammar (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>) composed by <s>Pāṇini</s> and others.

And <s>vākya</s> refers to the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> system in both its divisions — dealing with ritual action (<s>karma</s>) and with <s>Brahman</s> — which takes the form of determining the meaning of Vedic sentences through critical investigation.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ tu---kvacidapyartheṣvanavagāḍhāvaṣṭambhāṃ svātmanyapyanupajātavisrambhāṃ ḍolāyamānāṃ buddhiṃ kareṇumiva tarkaśṛṅkhalābhirālānayanmananavyapadeśaṃ śāstram ; yasya saṃjñāntaraṃ nyāyavistaraḥ tarkaśāstram ityādi //
children.translated_text: While <s>pramāṇa</s> refers to the science called <s>manana</s> (reflection) — which, like chains restraining an elephant, steadies with the fetters of reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) the intellect that vacillates without firm grounding in any subject and has not yet developed confidence even in itself; the alternative names for this science are <s>Nyāyavistara</s>, <s>Tarkaśāstra</s>, and so forth.

This jewel of a treatise called <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, which is the culmination of the successive waves of the river of wisdom of the blessed <s>Veṅkaṭanātha Deśika</s>, is triumphant — it is like the very life-breath of the <s>Nyāyavistara</s> as a branch of learning, and of the science of <s>Brahmamīmāṃsā</s> whose path was trodden by the eminent sage, the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s>. Without drawing upon this branch of learning, what glory can the rest of the branches of knowledge possess, even in being studied? For indeed, everything that is heard in this world, beset by doubt and error, tossed about like a blade of grass touched by a whirlwind, cannot find any firm footing whatsoever. But when established through the proper examination of the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), it stands immovable, its agitation removed, like a rock. And the examination of the <s>pramāṇas</s> is indeed the very first step in the domain of <s>Nyāyavistara</s>.

children.text:
tadetat pramāṇapradhānamapi pramāṇagateḥ prameyasvarūpavivecanaparyavasānatayā prameyepi nyastapadaṃ pravṛttam /
itaretaravisaṃvādasaṃrabdhoddhurairāstikairnāstikaiśca bahudhā vādibhiḥ svasvacchandānurodhenānyathā cānyathā ca prameyaṃ pratipadyamānairitastataḥ parikṛṣyamāṇāni pramāṇānyapi parāvṛttarūpatayā lakṣaṇato durgrahāṇyabhūvan /
mānābhāsavyāmiśrāṇi hi mānāni na sukarāṇi vivektum /
children.translated_text: For <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge) that are intermixed with <s>mānābhāsa</s> (semblances of valid knowledge) are not easy to discriminate.

children.text: tadevaṃ śāstrameva paṅkilīkṛtaṃ cakṣuriva timiropasṛṣṭaṃ vigalitārthagrahaṇāpāṭava saṃvṛttam /
children.translated_text: Thus the science itself was muddied, like an eye afflicted by a film — it lost its capacity to apprehend its proper objects.

children.text: aviparyastalakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇavargaṃ parigṛhṇādbhirapi saugatārhatakāpilacārvākajaiminīyādibhiraṅgeṣvavāntarabhedeṣu canyūnātirekamāsthitairanekadhopayogādanekāntīkṛtamatayaḥ kṛtamatayopi svasvopadeśapāramparīpratyayādekatamaṃ pakṣamabhimanyamānāḥ sparigrahāvasādakātaratayā pakṣāntareṣu sābhyasūyāścirāyāpi garukuleṣu pariśramyālabdhabuddhiprasādā vibhrāmyanta evānubhūyante /
children.translated_text: Even those who grasp the correct definitions of the group of <s>pramāṇas</s> — such as the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists), <s>Ārhatas</s> (Jains), <s>Kāpilas</s> (Sāṃkhyas), <s>Cārvākas</s>, <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, and others — by maintaining deficiency or excess in the subsidiary divisions, rendered the science inconclusive through manifold applications; and even those who had formed conclusions, adhering to one particular position out of trust in the succession of their own teaching traditions, were observed to wander in confusion, their minds biased by partiality for their own side and disdainful toward rival positions, having labored long in the schools of teachers without attaining clarity of understanding.

children.text: ataḥ sarvopayogāya doṣaguṇahānopādānābhyāṃ śikṣaṇīyasyāsya nyāyavistarasya pṛthakprasthānaṃ nyāyadarśanaṃ nāma sūtrajātaṃ gautamena muninā prathamaṃ praṇītam ; yatra pramāṇāpramāṇādivivecanayā tattvanirṇayopāyāstatra ca saṃbhavanto guṇadoṣāḥ kathāsu ca grāhyāparihāryavibhāgāḥ saviśeṣaṃ pradarśitāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for universal benefit, through the rejection of faults and the adoption of merits, a separate system of this <s>Nyāyavistara</s> — a collection of <s>sūtras</s> called the <s>Nyāyadarśana</s> — was first composed by the sage <s>Gautama</s>; wherein the means of ascertaining truth through the discrimination of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge) and <s>apramāṇa</s> (invalid knowledge), the merits and faults arising therein, and the distinction between what is to be accepted and what is to be avoided in debates — all these were set forth in detail.

This science, though primarily concerned with <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), also extends its reach into <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), since the course of <s>pramāṇa</s> culminates in the discernment of the nature of <s>prameya</s>. Because fierce disputants — both <s>āstika</s> (orthodox) and <s>nāstika</s> (heterodox) — locked in mutual contradiction, each following their own whims, apprehend <s>prameya</s> now in one way and now in another, the <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves, being dragged hither and thither, assumed distorted forms and became difficult to grasp in terms of their defining characteristics.

children.text:
tacca nyāyadarśanaṃ prathamaṃ pramāṇaprameyādisūtreṇa ṣoḍaśadhā padārthān vibhajya tatparīkṣaṇena caritārthama /
tatra prameyatvasya kevalānvayinaḥ sarvapadārthasādhāraṇatayā vibhājakatvamanupapadyamānaṃ manyamānena kaṇādena muninā kṛtsnameva prameyajātaṃ dravyādisaptapadārthaparisaṃkhyānenāsaṃkīrṇaṃ vibhaktam /
tatra ca sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyābhāvān vitathamevāpadārthān padārthayatā tathāvidhameva cānyadanyadālapatā grāhyamagṛhṇatā tyājyaṃ cātyajatā kaṇabhakṣeṇa dūramapathīkṛtaḥ śāstrapatha iti brahmasūtrakārādibhiḥ pratikṣipto vaiśeṣikaḥ pakṣaḥ /
nyāyapakṣastu śaṅkyamānopasargopi kathañcidvyākhyānādheyasaṃskāratayā nātyarthaparivarjanīyaḥ iti manyamānāḥ katipayasaṃskārasaṃskṛtamimaṃ pakṣaṃ parigṛhya nibandhān nibabandhuḥ pūrve kecidācāryāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Nyāya</s> position, even though susceptible to objection, was considered by certain earlier <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) to be not entirely to be rejected, inasmuch as it was amenable to correction through proper interpretation; and so, having adopted this position after furnishing it with some emendations, they composed treatises upon it.

children.text: te ca nibandhā eṣu divaseṣu nāmnaiva kevalamavaśiṣyantotadyathā--śrīmannāthamunimiśrapraṇītaṃ nyāyatattvam, śrīmatparāśarabhaṭṭārakakṛtistattvaratnākaraḥ, śrībhagavadyāmunācāryāṇāmācāryaiḥ śrīmannāthamunicaraṇāśrayāṇāṃ śrīpuṇḍarīkākṣāṇāṃ śiṣyaiśca śrīrāmamiśragurubhirviracitaṃ vivaraṇaṃ ṣaḍarthasaṃkṣepaśceti granthadvayam, aviditaprabandhṛvyapadeśaṃ nyāyasudarśanaṃ prajñāparitrāṇāṃ ceti prabandhayugalam, śrīmannārāyaṇamuniviracitatvenācāryopāttaṃ nāmnā cānuddiṣṭaṃ kimapi prabandharatnam, asyaiva ca nyāyapariśuddhipraṇeturācāryasyācāryeṇa mātulena ca vādihaṃsāmbuvāhaḥ iti praśastināmāṅkitena ātreyarāmānujācāryeṇa kṛtaṃ svapratibhādraviṇanikṣepāyamāṇaṃ nyāyakuliśābhidhānaṃ cetyete nibandhāḥ nyāyapariśuddhikṛtaivācāryeṇa tatra tatra bhūyiṣṭhamudāhriyante /
children.translated_text: And those treatises in these days survive in name alone, namely: the <s>Nyāyatattvam</s> composed by the revered <s>Nāthamuni Miśra</s>; the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s> by the blessed <s>Parāśara Bhaṭṭāraka</s>; two works — the <s>Vivaraṇa</s> and the <s>Ṣaḍarthasaṃkṣepa</s> — composed by the revered <s>Rāmamiśra</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, himself a dependent of the feet of the blessed <s>Nāthamuni</s> and a teacher of the blessed <s>Yāmunācārya</s>; a pair of treatises called <s>Nyāyasudarśana</s> and <s>Prajñāparitrāṇa</s> whose authors' names are unknown; a certain jewel of a treatise received by the <s>Ācārya</s> as composed by the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇamuni</s>, though not referred to by name; and the work called <s>Nyāyakuliśa</s>, composed by <s>Ātreyarāmānuja Ācārya</s>, who bore the honorific title <s>Vādihaṃsāmbuvāha</s> and was the maternal uncle and teacher of this very <s>Ācārya</s>, the author of the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, and which served as a treasury for the deposit of his own intellectual wealth — all these treatises are frequently cited by the <s>Ācārya</s>, the author of the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in various places.

children.text: yadeva yāvadeva cācāryeṇa kvacit kvacidudāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ vākyakhaṇḍaṃ vā, tadatiriktaṃ kiyadapi ṭīkākṛtāmapi dṛṣṭiviṣayībhūtaṃ nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: Whatever sentence or sentence-fragment the <s>Ācārya</s> has cited anywhere, beyond that, nothing further is found to have come within the sight even of the commentators.

children.text: ayamatra hetuḥ pratibhāti---ācāryasaṃnihitakāleṣvapyanatisaṃkṣepavistararamaṇīyāni prasphuṭārthāni nityaprakāśānyācāryaśrīsūktiratnānyavamṛśya rasāsvādavādivijayaśiṣyapravacanādripravaṇeṣu uparyupari vyākhyānādipraṇayanairavistṛtya śāstraṃ vitathamevātipātitakāleṣu śiṣyapraśiṣyavargeṣu kumāravedāntācāryādiṣu, atīte ca gaṇarātre kaiścidarvācīnairāvirbhūtairgranthakṛdbhirajñātapūrvavṛttāntairyathākathañcidvyākhyānena kaścidupakāraḥ kṛta iti //
children.translated_text: The reason for this appears to be as follows: even during the time when the <s>Ācārya</s> was present, his sacred utterances — which were gems of neither too concise nor too elaborate beauty, luminous in meaning, and ever-radiant — were not elaborated upon by students and their students' students in those successive generations, including <s>Kumāra Vedāntācārya</s> and others, who were inclined toward commentarial compositions for the sake of victory in debate and instruction rather than savoring the aesthetic delight of the original; and after a long time had passed, certain later authors, unaware of the prior history, rendered some sort of service through their commentaries as best they could.

That <s>Nyāyadarśana</s> first divided the <s>padārthas</s> (categories) into sixteen through the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>prameya</s>, and so on, and fulfilled its purpose through their examination. There, the sage <s>Kaṇāda</s>, considering that <s>prameya-tva</s> (the property of being an object of knowledge), being a universal predicate common to all categories, cannot serve as a valid principle of division, divided the entire range of <s>prameya</s> distinctly through an enumeration of seven categories beginning with <s>dravya</s> (substance). But in doing so, by treating as genuine categories such non-categories as <s>sāmānya</s> (universality), <s>viśeṣa</s> (ultimate particularity), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and <s>abhāva</s> (absence), and by prattling on in the same erroneous vein about other things too — accepting what ought to be rejected and not rejecting what ought to be rejected — <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (Kaṇāda) led the path of the science far astray; hence the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> position was repudiated by the author of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> and others.

children.text:
hanta ! niḥśeṣakṣālitākhilakalaṅkasyāpyasya śrībhagavadrāmānujasiddhāntasyedamekaṃ śocanīyaṃ vaiśasam ; yat tāvadācāryapadābhiṣiktairapyarvācīnairbudhavaraiḥ kāṇādagautamīyādisāmānyaśāstrapariśrameṇa vyayitavayobhirantime vayasi kathañcidupajātavedāntatṛṣṇaiḥ śiṣyasaṃgrahaṇakṛtakṣaṇairavaśyopādeyopadeśaśrībhāṣyādikatipayagranthagrahaṇacaritārthairanādṛtāḥ prācāmācāryāṇāṃ vāgvistarā etarhi śrotumapi durlabhatāṃ gamitārḥ /
idṛśoyaṃ vidyāvadhaḥ kasya vā vidyāvyasanino na dūnoti mānasam ? /
athavā kṛtaṃ prācāṃ prabandhapraṇāśacintanena /
asyaivācāryasya vāṅmadhuniṣyando mudhaiva kiyān na visraṃsitaḥ /
sarvatantrasvatantrāṇāmācāryacaraṇānāṃ śatādhikāḥ prabandhā hāravimalāḥ prasiddhāḥ /
saṃskṛtaprākṛtadrāviḍabhāṣābhistrarauśikāni kāvyanāṭakastotrāṇi, lokaśāstravyavahāranirūḍhasaṃskṛtavyatikīrṇadrāviḍabhāṣāmayāni ca caturtharāśiniviṣṭānilaukikānāmapyanugrāhakāni parīkṣakāṇāmapi sugrahasāṃpradāyikatattvahitapuruṣārthānyādarśavimalāni maṇipravālaśabditāni niyataśrāvyatayā rahasyasaṃjñitāni siddhāntaniṣkarṣaṇedaṃparāṇi lokaśreyase jātāni granthajātāni /
tatra vedānte tāvat tattvaṭīkā nāma śrībhagavadrāmānujamunivaraviracitasya śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣyasya vivṛtirapūrvārthaviśeṣavinyāsaparibhūṣitā traikālyasaṃbhāvanīyānāmaśeṣākṣepāṇāmacalaniścayān parihārānupadarśayantī gaṅgena gaurīguroretasmādācāryavaryādāvirbhūtā /
sā ca prathamasūtramātramapi yāvadasamagropalabdhapracārā vedāntavidyāvicārakāṅkṣiṇāṃ cintāvyasanāyaiva khaṇḍabhūtā paridṛśyate /
vicitrāyodhanākuṇṭhaśaktau tejasvini svāṃ śakti samagramadarśayitvaiva niyatiyaiyātyenākasmāduparataṃ yodharatne taṭasthadṛṣṭe kasya vā vīradharmamanutiṣṭhato hṛdayaṃ na dūyeta /
soyamasya nibandharatnasya lope dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
kecinmanyeran ācāryaireva na samāpūritāyaṃ grantha iti, tadetat svopamānena sarvatra śaktiparicchedaṃ kalayatāṃ pralapitamatra na kramate /
trividhāḥ khalu loke prabandhakṛtaḥ---kecidgurukulacirapariśramairanekaśaḥ śrutān yathāśrutamarthān patreṣu viniveśya prakāśayanto lokamanugṛhṇanti /
athetare, ye punarjātyaiva sphaṭikāvadātabuddhayaḥ sattvaviśeṣāvirbhāvanistuṣāśayāḥ svataḥ svāntamukuratalasphuṭasaṃkrāntasarvārthapraticchandā api saṃpradāyaparirakṣaṇaśraddhalutayā gurūpadeśadarśitāṃ padavīmavarjayantaścittaghaṇṭāpatheṣu samasamayasaṃcaradakhilapramāṇatarkagurūpadeśasaṃpradāyaviśeṣā ekahelayā bhūyasorthānayatnena grahītuṃ praṇetumapyarhanti /
anye tu nirantarabhajanakṛtaprasadanena bhagavatā sarveśvareṇa dūrapratyūḍhapratyūhavipruṣo niḥśreyasāvadhīni kuśalajātānyanubhavituṃ nijacaraṇaśaraṇānapyanubhāvayituṃ cākuṇṭhaśaktayastṛtīyakakṣyāniviṣṭāḥ /
ta ete vyāsaparāśaravālmīkipramukhairmaharṣigaṇairapi gaṇanīyānubhāvā vilakṣaṇāḥ prabandhakṛtaḥ; yeṣāmekapratibhāsūtrasyūtāni prameyaratnāni punaḥ punaḥ pariśīlitānyapi navanavānīva prajñāvatāṃ hṛdayeṣu kamapi camatkāramāvahanti na ca kadācit purāṇacitravad vicchāyāni bhavanti /
nyāpariśuddhikṛdācāryastu dvitīyatṛtīyayorubhayorapri kakṣyayoḥ hārāvalyoriva nāyakamaṇiḥ prakāśata iti tattvavidāmaparokṣam /
prakṛtisiddhaṃ ca prakrāntasyāntagamanaṃ śaktimatām /
lokānugrahamātraphalā yeṣāṃ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ, tādṛśānāmayatnanirvartanīye lokopakārārthe samārambhe cikīrṣitavicchedaḥ kathamupapadyate ? /
children.translated_text: For those whose every activity has as its sole fruit the benefiting of the world — how can there be an abandonment of purpose in an undertaking for the welfare of the world that could be accomplished without effort?

children.text: evaṅguṇena cācāryacūḍāmaṇipavanā śiṣyabuddhiṃ prasādayitumārabdhā kṛtirasamāpya madhye apaviddhā bhavatīti ko nukhalu prabhāvavedī pratipattumarhati ? /
children.translated_text: And who, knowing the <s>Ācārya's</s> power, could accept that a work begun by this crown-jewel among masters, capable of bestowing clarity upon the minds of disciples, was cast aside unfinished in the middle?

Moreover, [the <s>Ācārya</s> himself states]: "The work that takes the form of refining the crest of the entire series of <s>Nigamas</s> (Vedas) is composed upon the palace terraces of aspiration for those of subtle minds;

It is the victory-banner for the twenty-eighth cycle of the exposition of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> of the Lord of ascetics (<s>Yatipati</s>, i.e., <s>Rāmānuja</s>), whose teachings have been heard and contemplated as they were delivered."

Alas! This is the one lamentable misfortune of the doctrine of the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s>, even though it has been cleansed of every stain — that the extensive discourses of the earlier <s>ācāryas</s> have been brought to such inaccessibility that they are now difficult even to hear; for the later learned authorities, though elevated to the seat of <s>ācārya</s>, had spent their youth in the general study of the <s>Kāṇāda</s> and <s>Gautamīya</s> systems and similar sciences, and only in their final years, having somehow developed a thirst for <s>Vedānta</s>, busied themselves with gathering disciples and, having fulfilled their duty by teaching a few essential texts such as the <s>Śrībhāṣya</s>, left the extensive discourses of the earlier <s>ācāryas</s> unattended. Who with a passion for learning would not be grieved by such a destruction of knowledge? But enough of lamenting the loss of the earlier masters' works. How much of this very <s>Ācārya's</s> own flowing nectar of speech has been needlessly lost! The blessed <s>Ācārya</s>, master of all systems (<s>sarvatantrasvatantra</s>), is renowned for more than a hundred treatises, radiant as garlands: poems, dramas, and hymns in Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Dravidian languages; and works in the mixed Sanskrit-Dravidian language known as <s>Maṇipravāla</s>, which are placed in a fourth category, which benefit even the uninitiated, which for discerning critics present the traditional truths beneficial for the supreme human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) in an easily graspable manner, and which, being designated as <s>Rahasya</s> (esoteric) due to their prescribed mode of transmission, are directed toward the extraction of doctrinal conclusions for the welfare of the world. Among these, in the field of <s>Vedānta</s>, the work called <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> — a commentary on the <s>Śārīraka Mīmāṃsā Bhāṣya</s> composed by the eminent sage, the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s> — adorned with the arrangement of unprecedented special meanings, demonstrating unshakeable refutations of every conceivable objection across all three times — was brought forth by this supreme <s>Ācārya</s>, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> from <s>Gaurī's</s> Lord. But even that work is seen in its extant fragmentary form to have circulated incompletely, covering barely even the first <s>sūtra</s>, thereby serving only to torment with longing those who desire to investigate the science of <s>Vedānta</s>. When a brilliant warrior of inexhaustible prowess on the wondrous battlefield, having not fully displayed his might, suddenly ceases through the force of destiny — what onlooker who upholds the warrior's code would not be pained at heart? That is the analogy for the loss of this jewel of a treatise. Some may think that the <s>Ācārya</s> himself did not complete this work; but this is merely the prattle of those who measure everyone's capacity by their own standard — it carries no weight here. For indeed, there are three kinds of authors in the world: some, through long toil in the schools of teachers, having heard the doctrines many times as taught, set them forth on paper just as they were heard, and thus benefit the world. Then there are others who, though naturally possessed of crystal-clear intellects, disposed by their very nature to manifest the excellence of <s>sattva</s>, and though all meanings of all subjects are clearly reflected in the mirror of their own minds, out of devotion to preserving the tradition do not abandon the path shown by the teacher's instruction, and along the pathways of their mental acuity — where the full range of <s>pramāṇas</s>, reasoning, teacher's instruction, and traditional learning simultaneously course — they are capable of grasping and also composing abundantly with effortless ease. And yet others, by the grace of the Lord of all, won through unceasing devotion — who has swept far away the spray of obstacles — are endowed with unimpeded power to experience and to cause others who take refuge at their feet to experience all forms of blessed good that culminate in the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>); these occupy the third and highest rank. Such are the extraordinary authors, worthy of being counted even among the great sages such as <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, and <s>Vālmīki</s>; the gems of doctrine strung on the single thread of their genius, even when examined again and again, appear ever fresh and produce an indescribable wonder in the hearts of the wise, and never fade like an old painting. And the <s>Ācārya</s>, the author of the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, shines as the central jewel in the double strand of both the second and third ranks — this is manifest to those who know the truth. And it is natural for those possessed of power to bring to completion what they have undertaken.

children.text: iti svakṛtasya bhāṣyapravacanasya aṣṭāviṃśyāmāvṛttau tattvaṭīkānibandhapraṇayanamācāryastattvaṭīkāprārambhe svayameva spaṣṭamāha /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Ācārya</s> himself clearly states at the beginning of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> that the composition of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> treatise was undertaken during the twenty-eighth cycle of his own exposition of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
And in the prologue of the <s>Saṃkalpasūryodaya</s>: "In his twentieth year, renowned for manifold learning, having expounded the <s>Śārīraka Bhāṣya</s> thirty times,

children.text: śreyaḥ śrīmān veṅkaṭanāthaḥ śrutipathyaṃ nāthaprītyai nāṭakamarthyaṃ vyadhitaitat" //
children.translated_text: the illustrious <s>Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, for the pleasure of <s>Nātha</s> (Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>), composed this drama, wholesome and faithful to the Vedic path."

children.text:
iti sūtradhāravācā śārīrakabhāṣyapravacanaṃ saṃkalpasūryodayanirmāṇakāle triṃśadvārakṛtaṃ prathayati /
tadānīmeva triṃśadvāraṃ śārīrakabhāṣyapravacanamāsīdyadi, tataḥ paścāt pravacanāvṛttayastatopi hi bhūyasyo bhavitumarhanti /
kṛṣṇamiśrasamāgamakālo hi saṃkalpasūryodayanirmāṇasamayaḥ /

children.translated_text: And therefore the composition of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> during the twenty-eighth cycle falls earlier than the encounter with <s>Kṛṣṇamiśra</s>.

children.text: śatadūṣaṇyāḥ samanantaraṃ tattvaṭīkā kṛteti ca pratīyate /
children.translated_text: And it is also understood that the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> was composed immediately after the <s>Śatadūṣaṇī</s>.

children.text: uktaṃ hi svayamevācāryaistattvaṭīkāṃ prakramamāṇaiḥ--- "śātitaḥ śatadūṣaṇyāṃ śaṅkarādimudhāgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Ācārya</s> himself, when commencing the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s>, states: "The foolish obstinacy of <s>Śaṅkara</s> and others has been demolished in the <s>Śatadūṣaṇī</s>;
now the body of the <s>Śārīraka</s> (<s>Brahmasūtra</s>) is herein clearly expounded."

Thus, through the voice of the <s>Sūtradhāra</s> (stage-director), he declares that at the time of composing the <s>Saṃkalpasūryodaya</s>, he had already expounded the <s>Śārīraka Bhāṣya</s> thirty times. If even then there had been only thirty cycles of expounding the <s>Śārīraka Bhāṣya</s>, then after that there must have been still more cycles of exposition. For the time of the encounter with <s>Kṛṣṇamiśra</s> is the time of the composition of the <s>Saṃkalpasūryodaya</s>.
Thus.
"He by whom the <s>Śrutaprakāśikā</s> was first preserved on earth

children.text: pravartitā ca pātreṣu tasmai śreṣṭhāya maṅgalam //
children.translated_text: and transmitted to worthy recipients — to that most excellent one, may there be auspiciousness!"

children.text:
" iti kumāravedāntācāryakṛtamaṅgalāśāsanaparāmarśane śrutaprakāśikāpravacanatatparatvamācāryāṇāṃ tattvaṭīkāpūraṇavighātāya jātaṃ syāditi cāpātaramaṇīyam /
śruprakāśikācāryasya himlecchabalopamardalagnasya nijagurusabrahmacāriṇo mumūrṣataḥ prārthanayā tadgrantharakṣaṇapravacanayoraṅgīkārepi naitāvatā svakīyaṃ mahīyāṃsaṃ prabandhapraṇayanaprayatnamācāryo vitathīkariṣyati /
na hmatratyamapūrvamarthajātaṃ granthāntareṇa caritārthaṃ bhavati /
tadidamācāryagranthe kṛtaśramāṇāṃ svata eva suvyaktam /
idānīmupalabhyamānaparyantepi tattvaṭīkāgranthakhaṇḍe ye viṣayāḥ pratipādyantu, naite śrutaprakāśikāyāmanyatra vā granthāntare pratipattuṃ sulabhāḥ /
kiñca svācāryairvādihaṃsāmbuvāhāryaiḥ praṇīte vidyamāna eva hi nyāyakuliśākhye nyāyanibandharatne nyāyapariśuddhimācāryaḥ svayaṃ nibabandha /
children.translated_text: Moreover, when the <s>Nyāyanibandharatna</s> named <s>Nyāyakuliśa</s>, composed by his own teacher <s>Vādihaṃsāmbuvāhārya</s> (also known as <s>Atreyarāmānuja</s>), was already in existence, the <s>Ācārya</s> himself composed the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>.

children.text: avaśyavaktavyeṣu cārtheṣu joṣaṃbhāvaḥ kathañcidapi śāsrācāryatāyāḥ sadṛśo na bhavati /
children.translated_text: And silence on matters that must necessarily be stated is in no way befitting of the status of a teacher of <s>śāstra</s>.
Nor is the disclosure of ever-new meanings by later [teachers] a disparagement of earlier <s>Ācāryas</s>.
Moreover: "That which has the form of the crown-ornament of all the series of <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Nigamas</s>) is established upon the terrace-grounds of the hope-palace of those of subtle minds."

—thus the remark regarding the auspicious benedictions composed by <s>Kumāra Vedāntācārya</s> — [the suggestion] that the <s>Ācāryas</s>' devotedness to expounding the <s>Śrutaprakāśikā</s> was born in order to obstruct the completion of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> — is only superficially appealing.
For the <s>Śrutaprakāśikā-Ācārya</s>, even though he was engaged in repelling the oppression of barbarian forces, accepted the task of protecting and expounding that work at the request of his dying co-disciple (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>) of his own teacher — yet by that much the <s>Ācārya</s> would not have abandoned his own greater effort of composing his own treatise.
For the unprecedented collection of meanings contained herein is not rendered redundant by any other work.
This is self-evident to those who have labored over the <s>Ācārya</s>'s works.
Even within the sections of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> that can be found at present, the subjects treated therein are not easy to learn either from the <s>Śrutaprakāśikā</s> or from any other work.

children.text:
iti prabandhopakramapratijñānameva pradarśayati granthāntarairacaritārthasya sarvavedāntārthasaṃskārasya mahāmatibhirapi sarvajñasakāśāt śuśrūṣitasya pratipādanārthamapūrvāyāḥ kṛteḥ samārambha iti /
sa kathaṃ na paripūryeta ? /
kiñca nijanibandhasya śrutaprakāśikārakṣaṇāṅgīkārasamaya eva labdhaprasaratāmanusmṛtya parakīyagranthapravacanamaṅgīkṛtamācāryairiti śakyamabhyūhitum /
tathāca sati tattvaṭīkāgranthalopanidānamarvācāmācāryāṇāṃ tatrāpariśīlanameva, na tu granthāparisamāptiḥ /
yathāhi nyāyasiddhāñjanamapi jaḍadravyaparicche denaiva paryavasitaṃ sāṃprataṃ paridṛśyate, adravyaparicchedastu patita eva /
children.translated_text: For just as even the <s>Nyāyasiddhāñjana</s> is now seen to conclude only with the section on non-sentient matter (<s>jaḍadravyapariccheda</s>), while the section on non-material [entities] (<s>adravyapariccheda</s>) has simply been lost.
And its completion by others is impossible.

children.text: itthamamumarthaṃ śrīraṅgarāmānujagurureva nyāyasiddhāñjanavyākhyāne "na kvāpyataḥ paramadṛsyata kośaśeṣa- staccheṣapūraṇakṛtiḥ parihāsahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: In this way, the revered <s>Śrīraṅgarāmānuja Guru</s> himself, in his commentary on the <s>Nyāyasiddhāñjana</s>, states and concludes [thus]: "Nowhere beyond this is the remainder of the text seen;

children.text: jñātavyamanyadapi tairniraṇāyi samya- ggranthāntareṣviti na kiñcidihāsti cintyam" //
children.translated_text: an attempt to complete that remainder would be a laughing-stock. / What else was to be known has been properly determined by them in other works — therefore there is nothing to be pondered here." //

This very opening declaration of the treatise shows that the commencement of an unprecedented work is for the purpose of demonstrating the refinement of the meaning of all <s>Vedānta</s> — which has not been accomplished by other works, which must be reverently learned from the Omniscient One even by great intellects.
How then could it not be completed?
Moreover, it can be surmised that the <s>Ācārya</s> accepted the exposition of another's work, having recalled that his own treatise had already attained currency, at the very time when he accepted the task of protecting the <s>Śrutaprakāśikā</s>.
This being so, the cause of the disappearance of the <s>Tattvaṭīkā</s> text is merely the lack of study of it by later <s>Ācāryas</s>, not the non-completion of the work.

children.text:
iti nigamayannivedayati /
śatadūṣaṇyapi hi na samagrā dṛśyate /
ṣaṭṣaṣṭireva vādā loke pracaranti /
śeṣe tu mithyaiva kimapyaitihyaṃ kalpayitvā katipaye prajalpanti /
yattāvat dvaitamatakhaṇḍanaparaḥ śeṣo granthaḥ madhvamatasthena kenacidyatinā bhikṣāmaṭatā savinayamupasṛtya prārthitoyamācāryaḥ taṃ tasya bhikṣārthe prāyacchiditi, tadapi na vicārakṣamam /
na hyācāryagrantheṣu kvacidapi madhvamataṃ nirasyate /
tattvaviplavābhāvāt, avāntareṣu cārtheṣu naiyāyikavaiśeṣikādipratipāditasyaiva dvaitasyānuvādāt, anatipracuratayā tasya matasya lokaviplavaprasaṃgābhāvāccānāsthaivācāryāṇāṃ tatra syāt /

children.translated_text: Therefore, that thirty-four arguments are devoted to refuting the <s>Madhva</s> doctrine is mere rumor.

children.text: śatadūṣaṇī ca śaṅkādikṛtasūtravyākhyānādinirāsārthameva pravṛtteti ca tadgranthamukha eva sphuṭībhavati /
children.translated_text: And that the <s>Śatadūṣaṇī</s> is undertaken solely for the purpose of refuting the commentaries on the <s>Sūtras</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara</s> and others — this becomes clear from the very opening of that work.

children.text: tatra hi ---- "prācīmupetya padavīṃ yatirājadṛṣṭāṃ tatsaṃnikṛṣṭamapi vā matamāśrayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: For therein: "Having approached the ancient path seen by <s>Yatirāja</s> (<s>Rāmānuja</s>), or adopting even a doctrine close to his—

children.text: prājñā yathoditamidaṃ śukavat paṭhantaḥ pracchannabauddhavijaye parito yatadhvam" //
children.translated_text: O wise ones, reciting this as stated, like parrots, strive everywhere for the conquest of the crypto-Buddhists." //

— thus he indicates.
Even the <s>Śatadūṣaṇī</s> is not seen in its complete form. Only sixty-six arguments circulate in the world. Regarding the rest, some prattle having fabricated some mere tradition.
As for [the claim that] the remainder of the work, devoted to refuting the <s>Dvaita</s> (dualist) doctrine, was given by the <s>Ācārya</s> — who was approached respectfully by some <s>Madhva</s> monk wandering for alms, who requested it — to that [monk] for the purpose of alms — this too does not withstand scrutiny.
For nowhere in the <s>Ācārya</s>'s works is the <s>Madhva</s> doctrine refuted.
Because there is no deviation from truth [in it requiring refutation]; and because in subsidiary matters, it is merely the dualism propounded by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, and others that is being restated; and because, due to its not being overly widespread, there would be no danger of it misleading the world — therefore the <s>Ācāryas</s> would have no concern regarding it.

children.text: atra 'tatsaṃnikṛṣṭamapi vā matamāśrayantaḥ' ityanena dvaitinaḥ svapakṣīkriyante /
children.translated_text: Here, by the phrase 'or adopting even a doctrine close to his,' the dualists (<s>Dvaitins</s>) are made allies.
And that the refutation of <s>Advaita</s> (non-dualism) alone is the purpose of the work's composition — this too is shown.

children.text: tathā ca---vidyāraṇyākṣobhyamunivivāde nirṇayaṃ bruvadbhirācāryeḥ "asinā tattvamasinā parajīvaprabhedinā /
children.translated_text: And accordingly — when the <s>Ācārya</s>, pronouncing judgment in the debate between <s>Vidyāraṇya</s> and <s>Akṣobhyamuni</s>, stated: "With the sword 'Thou art That' (<s>Tattvamasi</s>), which distinguishes the individual soul from the other—
<s>Akṣobhyamuni</s> cut down the great forest of <s>Vidyāraṇya</s>." //
— thus it is declared.
— thus it was said.
And in [the verse] 'The stubborn delusion of <s>Śaṅkara</s> and others was slain in the <s>Śatadūṣaṇī</s>'

children.text: ' ityatra tu śaṅkarādītyādipadaṃ yādavabhāskarayoḥ saṃgrahāyeti sthitam /
children.translated_text: — there the word 'and others' (<s>ādi</s>) in '<s>Śaṅkarādi</s>' is established as being for the inclusion of <s>Yādava</s> and <s>Bhāskara</s>.
Therefore, this is clear: the non-availability of the complete work, due to the interruption of exposition by later <s>Ācāryas</s>, is the cause of the loss of the treatise.

children.text:
atra prasaktānuprasaktamācāryasya kṛṣṇamiśrasamāgamacaritaṃ kiñcidupanyasyate---kṛṣṇamiśro hi gauḍadeśīyaḥ paṇḍitacūḍāmaṇiḥ sarvāsu vidyāsu kalāsu ca saviśeṣakṛtaśramaḥ kaviśca brahmādvaitaṃ siddhantamātiṣṭhamāno vādakutūhalitayā sarvā diśaḥ paryaṭan jitakāśī krameṇa dakṣiṇāndiśamācakrāma /
tatra śrīraṅgaṃ divyakṣetraṃ viduṣāmāvāsamākarṇya devasevāpadeśena vādasamaramarthayamānaḥ śrīraṅgarājasya bhavagataḥ prāsādamāsadāda /
tadānīṃ tatra bhāṣāmayīrgāthāḥ sarāgatālaṃ gīyamānā niśamya tatkartṝṇāṃ ca kavīnāṃ varṇāvarāṇāmapi pratimāstasmin devālaye devopacārairārādhyamānā viditvā tatra sevāsamavetān jñānavṛddhān śrīvaiṣṇavānāmantrya 'bhoḥ prājñāḥ, bhavatāmanenāpabhraṃśapāṭhena varṇāvarapūjanena ca dūrāpoḍhaṃ veṣṇavaṃ tejaḥ /
kimanenārādhanena ? /
anthathākṛtamakṛtaṃ hi bhavati' iti sākṣepaṃ papraccha /
yadā tairmilitairapi na kiñcidākṣepasadṛśamuttaraṃ pratipannaṃ, tadā tadātanāya taddeśādhipataye tamarthamāvedya, pratiṣṭhāprabhṛti sarva evālayasaṃskāraḥ kāryaḥ pratyagra eva iti ca niyamya taṃ divyālayaṃ gāḍhaghaṭitārgaladvāraṃ parityaktāśeṣapūjotsavaṃ ca kārayāmāsa /
lokācāryaprabhṛtayaśca bahavastatra darśanaguravastādṛśaṃ vaiśasamacintitopanatamanusmṛtya durante duḥkhasāgare nimagnāstaṃ ca prativādinaṃ sarvavidyāviśāradaṃ vādāhavanavaśūramaprakampyamākalayantaḥ sabhāmabhinavāṃ kāmapi saṃgamayya tasyānarthasya kiñcidapi pratividhānaṃ cintayāmāsuḥ /
tasmin mahati sadasi viduṣāṃ saṃpradāyācāryaḥ śrīmān lokācāryaḥ sarveṣāṃ sabhāsadāmavadheyavacanaḥ samarthāmabhyarhitāṃ vācamādade--- "bhoḥ bhāgavatapradhānāḥ, balavantaṃ paripanthinaṃ parāṅmukhīkartumupāyaḥ kaścidatra me pratibhāti /
sa tāvaducyamāno bhavadbhiranumanyatām /
asti kila kāñcyāṃ nagaryāṃ veṅkaṭanāthāryo nāma viduṣāṃ prathamaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is, it is said, in the city of <s>Kāñcī</s> (Kanchipuram), one named <s>Veṅkaṭanāthārya</s>, the foremost among the learned.

children.text: sa hi vṛṣaśailanāthasya ghaṇṭāṃśa evāvatīrṇaḥ iti tattvavidāṃ grahaṇam /
children.translated_text: He is indeed an incarnation of the bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) of the Lord of <s>Vṛṣaśaila</s> (<s>Tirupati</s>) — such is the understanding of the knowers of truth.

children.text: soyaṃ pañcavarṣadeśīyaḥ śiśureva san nijamātulena vādihaṃsāmbuvāhenātreyarāmānujācāryeṇa śārīrakabhāṣyagrahaṇāya varadagurusakāśaṃ gacchatā priyabhāgineyena nītastatra bhāṣyaviṣaye prasaktān bahūn saṃdehaśṛṅkhalāgranthīn visraṃsayaṃstayā tatrasamavetayā prajñāvṛddhapariṣadā apūrvaprasādavismayacitritacittayā sabahumānamavalokitaḥ śrīmatā ca varadaguruṇā śrībhagavadrāmānujasiddhāntasya daivāt saṃprati saṃjātamavalambanamiti baddhāśvāsena, 'pratiṣṭhāpitavedāntaḥ pratikṣaptabahirmataḥ /
children.translated_text: This one, being merely about five years old, while still a child, was brought by his own maternal uncle, <s>Vādihaṃsāmbuvāha</s> — also known as <s>Atreyarāmānujācārya</s> — who was going to the presence of <s>Varadaguru</s> for the study of the <s>Śārīrakabhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Brahmasūtras), taking along his beloved nephew. There [the child], untying many knots in the chain of doubts that had arisen regarding the subject of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, was looked upon with great respect by the assembly of elders rich in wisdom who had gathered there, their minds painted with wonder at [his] unprecedented clarity. And the blessed <s>Varadaguru</s>, assured that 'by divine providence a support has now arisen for the doctrine of the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s>,' bestowing the benediction: 'May you, the establisher of <s>Vedānta</s>, the refuter of external doctrines,
become the honored bearer of the threefold [Vedic] learning, a vessel of abundant auspiciousness!' //

Here, as something incidentally relevant, the account of the <s>Ācārya</s>'s encounter with <s>Kṛṣṇamiśra</s> is briefly narrated: <s>Kṛṣṇamiśra</s> was a native of the <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal) region, a crown-jewel among scholars, one who had especially exerted himself in all sciences and arts, a poet, adhering to the doctrine of <s>Brahmādvaita</s> (non-duality of Brahman), and wandering in all directions out of eagerness for debate. Having conquered <s>Kāśī</s> (Varanasi), he gradually proceeded to the southern direction. There, hearing that <s>Śrīraṅgam</s>, the divine sacred site, was the abode of scholars, he reached the temple of <s>Śrīraṅgarāja</s>, seeking an opportunity for debate under the pretext of worshipping the deity. At that time, hearing songs being sung there in the vernacular language with percussion, and learning that the statues of those poets — its composers, even those of low castes — were being worshipped with divine honors in that very temple, he summoned the knowledgeable senior <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> assembled there for worship and asked them reproachfully: 'O wise ones! By this recitation in a corrupt language and by this worship of low-caste persons, the glory of <s>Vaiṣṇavism</s> has been driven far away. What is the use of such worship? For what is done otherwise than properly is as if undone.' When even they, assembled together, could not give a fitting reply to his challenge, he then reported the matter to the local ruler of that time, and having ordained that all temple rituals — from the consecration onward — should be [re-]done entirely anew, he caused that divine temple to have its doors firmly bolted shut and all worship-festivals abandoned. And <s>Lokācārya</s> and many other teachers of that school, remembering this unprecedented calamity that had befallen them through the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s machination, and sunk in a terrible ocean of grief, and reckoning that disputant — accomplished in all sciences and unshakable as a warrior in the battle of debate — to be insurmountable, assembled in some new gathering and deliberated on some remedy for that disaster. In that great assembly, <s>Śrīmān Lokācārya</s>, the traditional teacher, whose words commanded the attention of all those assembled, spoke a fit and respected word: 'O foremost among devotees! A means occurs to me for turning away this powerful adversary. Let it, when stated, be approved by you.

children.text:
' ityāśiṣaṃ prayuñjānena 'asya kumārasya svataḥ pratibhātasamastaśāstrārthasārasya vidyāsaṃskāramātraphalo gurūpadeśo bhaviṣyati /
na tu jñāne kaścidapi śaktileśa ādheyo bhavati /
bhagavānapi hi devakīnandanaḥ vidyāgrahaṇāya sāṃdīpinerācāryasya sakāśe gurukulavāsamagrahīt /
kiṃ cāsya śaiśava evāyaṃ prajñāprakarṣo dāśaratheriva vikramatiśayo janmasiddhaḥ /
nāsau puruṣāntaradṛṣṭiviṣayaṃ prāpayituṃ yuktam /
sābhyasūyāḥ savismāyā vā dṛśo nāsmin bālavayasi patitumarhanti /
children.translated_text: Neither envious nor astonished gazes should be allowed to fall upon him at this young age.

children.text: dṛṣṭidoṣairhi viṣānalairiva prasaradbhistarava ivāvalāḍhāḥ kati nāma mahāguṇāḥ puruṣāḥ svaguṇairlokamanupakṛtyaivāstaṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: For how many great men of great qualities, scorched by the spreading poisons and fires of evil glances like trees [scorched by fire], have set without benefiting the world with their qualities!
You alone are fit to make him accomplished in all <s>śāstras</s>.

children.text: śrībhagavadrāmānujasiddhāntasyaiṣa jayadhvajaḥ samucchrīyatām' iyādiśya śiśurasau nijamātule vādihaṃsāmbudācārye nyāsīkṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Let this victory-banner of the blessed Lord <s>Rāmānuja</s>'s doctrine be raised aloft!'—having thus instructed, that child was entrusted to his maternal uncle, <s>Vādihaṃsāmbuvāha Ācārya</s>.

—and declaring: 'For this prince, whose inherent mastery of the essence of all <s>śāstras</s> is self-manifest, the teacher's instruction will bear fruit only in the form of formal academic refinement. No trace of capacity needs to be imparted regarding knowledge. For even the Blessed <s>Lord Devakīnandana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) undertook residence in the <s>gurukula</s> (teacher's house) of his <s>Ācārya Sāndīpani</s> for the purpose of studying. Moreover, this preeminence of intellect even in childhood is inborn, like the extraordinary valor of [Lord] <s>Rāma</s> son of <s>Daśaratha</s>. It is not proper to bring it within the gaze of ordinary men.

children.text: athāsau vayasā viṃśativarṣadeśīya eva san sarvatomukhaprasṛtaprabodhatayā pareṣāmanabhibhavanīyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, being merely about twenty years of age, became invincible to others through the spread of his awakened intelligence in all directions.

children.text: evamakṣayyapratibhādraviṇena sarveṣvapi ca tantreṣu nirāmayaṃ panthānamavagantuṃ prasādayituṃ cālaṅkarmīṇena cācāryeṇā sārdhaṃ kadācit kāñcīnagare devadevasya bhagavataḥ śrīdevarājasya vaiśākhamāsike yātrāmahotsave vidvatsaṃvādakutūhalitayā samāgataḥ sarvapathīnavaiduṣīvibhavaḥ prabandharatnapraṇetā cākhilaśāstreṣu vidyāraṇya iti kṛtapraśastināmadheyo mādhavācāryo nāma vedabhāṣyakṛt vādāhave lagno niraṅkuśaniśitatarkaśarāsāravarṣiṇaḥ ācāryasyāgrataḥ pratyavasthātumakṣamo vismayabahumānabharitamanā vijayanagaraṃ prayātaḥ svaśiṣyasya rājñastamarthaṃ yathāvṛttamāvedya tathāvidhavidvadratnadarśanotkaṇṭhātvaritasya prabhoḥ prārthanayā chatracāmaraprabhṛtisamastarājaparibarhaparibṛṃhitaṃ rājaupavāhyapuraḥsaraṃ pradhānasacivahastārpitasabahumānasamāhvānalekhaṃ ca caturaṅgabalaṃ praṇīyaḥ prārthito vairāgyapañcakaṃ tasya pratyuttarayāñcakāra /
children.translated_text: Thus, with inexhaustible wealth of genius and being capable of traversing and illuminating the unerring path in all systems of thought — once, in the city of <s>Kāñcī</s>, at the great festival of the <s>Vaiśākha</s>-month procession of the god of gods, the blessed <s>Śrī Devarāja</s> — <s>Mādhavācārya</s>, who was the renowned <s>Vidyāraṇya</s>, author of the <s>Prabandharatna</s>, endowed with scholarly distinction in all schools, composer of the <s>Vedabhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Vedas), had come out of curiosity for scholarly discourse; [but] being unable to withstand before the <s>Ācārya</s>, who was showering a torrent of sharpest dialectical arrows, and his mind filled with wonder and respect, he departed for <s>Vijayanagara</s> and reported the matter as it happened to his disciple the king. At the king's request, who was eager with curiosity to see such a jewel among scholars, [<s>Mādhavācārya</s>] dispatched a four-branched army embellished with all royal paraphernalia of umbrella, <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk), and the rest, preceded by a royal conveyance, with a letter of respectful invitation placed in the hand of the chief minister, to invite [the <s>Ācārya</s>]. But he, being invited, sent as reply the five verses on renunciation (<s>Vairāgyapañcaka</s>).

children.text: tena ca mādhavācāryeṇa svīye sarvadarśanasaṃgrahe rāmānujadarśanamupakṣipatā--- 'taduktaṃ veṅkaṭanāthena tattvamuktākakalāpe' ityupakramya, // śrīḥ //
children.translated_text: And by that <s>Mādhavācārya</s>, while introducing the <s>Rāmānuja</s> system in his own <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s> — beginning with 'Thus said <s>Veṅkaṭanātha</s> in the <s>Tattvamuktākalāpa</s>' — // <s>Śrīḥ</s> //
// Salutation to the blessed <s>Hayavadana</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>! //
// Salutation to the blessed <s>Rāmānuja</s>! //
// Salutation to the blessed <s>Nigamānta Mahādeśika</s>! //

children.text:
śrīmāna veṅkaṭanāthārthaḥ kavitārkikakesarī /
vedāntācāryavaryo me saṃnidhattāṃ sadā hṛdi
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the lion among poets and logicians (<s>Kavitārkikakesarī</s>), / the foremost among <s>Vedānta Ācāryas</s> — may he ever be present in my heart.

children.text: nyā. pa. pra. 1 patyuḥ saṃyamināṃ praṇamya caraṇau tatpādakoṭīrayoḥ saṃbandhena samidhyamānavibhavān dhanyāṃstathānyān gurūn /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa. Pra.</s> 1. Having bowed at the feet of the Lord of the self-controlled, and to those other blessed teachers whose glory is ignited by their connection with the rays of His lotus-feet,

children.text: śuddhaṃ saṃśritabādarāyaṇatanornārāyaṇasyoktibhaḥ śrīmān veṅkaṭanāyakaḥ sthitipadaṃ nirmāti nīteḥ śubham //
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Veṅkaṭanāyaka</s>, whose utterances are the pure radiance of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as expounded by <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, constructs the auspicious ground of firm establishment for [the science of] reasoning. //
Among the righteous fields of knowledge, the <s>Nyāyavistara</s> (the detailed system of logic) is counted [as important].
And that has been distorted by various [thinkers]; therefore here it is being purified. //
<s>Nyā. Pa. Pra.</s> 2.
The thesis of excluding <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>Sūtras</s>.

children.text: yadyapi kathañcidākṣapādaṃ satpakṣe nikṣeptu śakyam; na ca kaṇabhakṣapakṣanikṣepavat kleśaḥ; nāpi tatkartā gautamastāmaseṣu paripaṭhyate; nāpi ca vipralambhakatvakhyātiḥ; tathāpi brahmasūtrakārādibahiṣkṛtatvānnātīva vayamādriyāmahe /
children.translated_text: Although it is possible somehow to place <s>Ākṣapāda</s> (<s>Gautama</s>) on the correct side, and though there is not as much difficulty as in placing the <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s>) position [on the correct side], and though its author <s>Gautama</s> is not reckoned among the <s>tāmasa</s> (those of the quality of darkness), nor is he known for deception — nevertheless, because he was excluded by the author of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> and others, we do not overly esteem [his system].
Not indeed is esteem for it [warranted] merely because of its being composed by a sage and the like, since that would lead to an unwanted over-extension.

children.text: prājñānāṃ prathamenaiva guruṇā hi svayaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: For by the very first teacher (<s>Brahmā</s>), indeed, of old, / the materialist (<s>Lokāyata</s>) doctrine was expounded — a cause of the world's destruction. //

Or rather, the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>) himself is the authority here, who taught the materialist doctrine to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>. Similarly, <s>Gautama</s> too may be regarded [in that light].

children.text:
athavā pitāmaha evātra pramāṇam, ya indravirocanāyoścārvākamatamupadiṣṭavān /
tathā gautamo 'pi saṃbhāvyate /

children.translated_text: [from the <s>Smṛti</s>:] "By the <s>Kāṇāda</s> (followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s>), the <s>Śākya</s> (Buddhist), and heretical doctrines, the <s>dharma</s> of the three <s>Vedas</s> was destroyed;
[but] formerly by <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing the triple staff (<s>tridaṇḍa</s>), the three <s>Vedas</s> were protected." //
— from this <s>Smṛti</s>,
Moreover,
[and from the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:] "Many persons, O king, are followers of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> investigation;
they do not accept a single <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), O scion of the <s>Kuru</s> race. //
But <s>Vyāsa</s> stated in summary the oneness of <s>Puruṣa</s>."
//[end of section]

children.text: iha tu na tatheti cenna, tulyanyāyatayā vacanasyopalakṣaṇārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: If it be objected that here (in the case of Nyāya) it is not so, we say no, because the statement serves as a mere indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) due to the parity of reasoning.
Indeed, there is no distinction between 'that one' and 'one of that kind.'

children.text: yadyapi kāśakuśāvalambanyāyena pakṣāntarādādhikyamasya pakṣasya, athāpi na tadvedāntasaṃnidhau; na khalumaśakādbaliṣṭho 'pi mātaṅgaḥ kaṇṭhīravamuparuṇaddhi //
children.translated_text: Although by the maxim of grasping at reeds and grass (<s>kāśakuśāvalambinyāya</s>) this position has superiority over other positions, nevertheless that does not hold in the proximity of <s>Vedānta</s>; for indeed, even an elephant (<s>mātaṅga</s>) mightier than a fly does not obstruct a lion (<s>kaṇṭhīrava</s>).
— from this statement of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the exclusion of those respective [systems] is justified.

children.text: "yadakṣapādaḥ pravaro munīnāṃ śamāya śāstraṃ jagato jagāda /
children.translated_text: "That which <s>Akṣapāda</s>, foremost among sages, proclaimed as a <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) for the tranquility of the world,
a composition (<s>nibandha</s>) thereof shall be made by me, which will be the cause of removing the ignorance of false reasoners (<s>kutārkika</s>)."
This statement should not be regarded as spoken out of partiality toward the school of <s>Akṣapāda</s>.
And it has been said by the earlier teachers (<s>pūrvācārya</s>):
"Whether it be the <s>Kāṇāda</s> (Vaiśeṣika), <s>Ākṣapāda</s> (Nyāya), or <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṃkhya) system,
all these systems are not [truly independent] systems when one examines the self (<s>ātman</s>)."
Thus.

children.text: ata eva hi "etena śiṣṭāparigrahā api vyākhyātāḥ" iti sūtre bhāṣitam---"etena---vedāparigṛhītasāṃkhyapakṣakṣapaṇena, śiṣṭāśca vedāparigṛhītāḥ kaṇabhakṣākṣapādakṣapaṇakabhipakṣāḥ kṣapitā veditavyāḥ" iti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>sūtra</s> "By this, those not accepted by the learned are also explained," the <s>Bhāṣya</s> states: "By this—by the refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position not accepted by the <s>Veda</s>—the learned positions not accepted by the <s>Veda</s>, namely those of <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (Kaṇāda), <s>Akṣapāda</s>, and <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> (Jaina), should be understood as refuted."

children.text: na ca sūtranibaddhaṃ sarvaṃ vidyāsthānamiti niyamo dṛṣṭaḥ; na caika evaikasya vidyāsthānasya sūtrakṛdityapi vā ṛṣirityeva vā rājājñā, anyairapi ca tatkaraṇadarśanāt //
children.translated_text: Nor is there any rule observed that every domain of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>) must be set forth in <s>sūtras</s>; nor is there a royal decree that there be only one <s>sūtra</s>-maker for each domain of knowledge, or that he must be a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), since others too are seen to have composed such works.

children.text:
pramāṇaśabdasya bhāve karaṇe ca vyutpattiḥ /
1 evaṃ ca pramaiva pramāṇamityeke /
2 pramākaraṇamevetyapare /
3 tayoranyataradityanye /
4 yathāvasthitavyavahārānuguṇaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇam /
5 yadajñānāt saṃsāro yajjñānāt tannivṛttistat prameyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ prakarṣeṇa meyatvāt /
6 taddvividhaṃ dravyādravyabhedāt /
7 sāmānyato vā pramāviṣayaḥ prameyam /
8 āgantukadharmāśrayo dravayam /
9 atathābhūtamadravyam /
10 dravyaṃ dvedhā jaḍamajaḍamiti /
11 jaḍaṃ ca dvedhā prakṛtiḥ kāla iti /
12 ajaḍaṃ ca tathā pratyak parāgiti /
13 pratyagapi dvividhaṃ jīvar iśvara iti /
14 parāgapi tathā dharmabhūtajñānaṃ nityavibhūtiśceti /
15 athavā dravyaṃ dvividhamātmānātmabhedāt /
16 tredhā vā bhoktṛbhogyaniyantṛśrutyanusārāt /
17 ṣoḍhā vā triguṇakālajīveśvaraśuddhasattvamatibhedāt /
18 asvayaṃprakāṃśaṃ jaḍam /
19 svayaṃprakāśamajaḍam /
20 miśrasattvāśrayaḥ prakṛtiḥ /
21 kālaḥ kṣaṇalavādivyavahārahetuḥ /
22 svasmai bhāsamānaṃ pratyak /
23 parasmai bhāsamānaṃ parāk /
24 paratantracetano jīvaḥ /
25 svatantrar iśvaraḥ /
26 arthaprakāśo buddhiḥ /
27 prakṛtivyatiriktatve sati sattvāśrayo nityavibhūtiḥ /
28 adravyamanekadhā sattvaśabdādivaicitryāt /
29 ekaṃ vetaraviśiṣṭaṃ prādhānyataḥ prameyaṃ paraṃ brahma /
30 itareṣāṃ svaniṣṭhabrahmaikaniṣṭhatvāt /
31 tasyaiva ca tathātvena mumukṣubhiḥ prakarṣeṇa meyatvaśruteḥ /
32 avyavasthitavyavahārakāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ /
33 ayathāvyavahārakāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ viparyayaḥ /
34 saṃskāramātrajaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ /
35 tadvyatiriktaṃ jñānamanubhavaḥ /
36 puruṣapravṛttyuddeśyaṃ prayojanam /
37 vyāptyadhigamasthānaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
38 prāmāṇikatvābhimataiḥ parigṛhītor'thaḥ siddhāntaḥ /
39 parārthapramāṇaprayogavākyāvāntaravākyānyavayavāḥ /
40 vyāpyāṅgīkāreṇa vyāpakāniṣṭaprasañjanaṃ tarkaḥ /
41 tarkānugṛhītapramāṇapūrvakatattvāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ /
42 vītarāgakathā vādaḥ /
43 pakṣadvayasādhanavatī vijigīṣukathā jalpaḥ /
44 pratipakṣasthāpanahīnā tu sā vitaṇḍā /
45 hetvaṅgaikadeśavikalā hetvābhāsāḥ /
46 avivakṣitaśabdārthāropeṇa dūṣaṇaṃ chalam /
47 svavyāpidūṣaṇaṃ jātiḥ /
48 kathakāśaktiliṅgaṃ nigrahasthānam /
49 ityetādṛśāni vākyāni kiṃ na sūtrāṇi syuḥ ? tadiha saṃkṣiptaṃ lakṣaṇādivākyaṃ sūtram; tadudāharaṇādivākyaṃ tu bhāṣyādikamiti vibhāvya saṃtoṣṭavyam /
na ca pūrvaprābalyavyavasthā, tatpūrvasaṃbhavāt vārtikasya cānavatāraprasaṅgāt vyākaraṇādiṣvanyathākaraṇasvīkārācca /
na ca jaimineḥ pramāṇalakṣaṇādiṣvaudāsīnyamātreṇa gautamokteṣu kāśyapokteṣu vā niḥśeṣānumatisiddhiriti mantavyam, anyaparatayā lokaprasiddhopajīvanāt, parakalpitataṭākopajīvanavat /
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that merely because <s>Jaimini</s> was indifferent regarding the definitions of <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth, there is a complete endorsement of what <s>Gautama</s> or <s>Kaśyapa</s> (Kaṇāda) stated, since [<s>Jaimini</s>] relied upon what is well-known in the world for a different purpose, just as one makes use of a tank constructed by another.

children.text: karmakāṇḍavṛttikārādayo 'pi hi losiddhāṃ pramāṇādivyavasthāṃ yathāyathamanyathā saṃjagṛhuḥ /
children.translated_text: For even the commentators on the <s>Karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion of the Veda) appropriated the commonly known system of <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth, each modifying it as they saw fit.

children.text: ato yāvadiha yuktiyuktaṃ tāvadupajīvyate; na khalu taṭākasthaḥpaṅko 'pyapaṅkilabuddhibhistatadavagāhibhirupajīvyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever is supported by reason here is made use of; for indeed, even the mud in a tank is not made use of by those of unpolluted intellect who draw from it.

children.text: ataḥ siṃhavanaguptinyāyena yathāvasthitanyāyānugṛhītaṃ vedaṃ vedānumataṃ ca nyāyamanusarāmaḥ, na punarnyāyamātram //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the maxim of <s>Siṃhavanaguptā</s>, we follow the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Nyāya</s> (reasoning) that is approved by the <s>Veda</s> as properly established, but not mere <s>Nyāya</s> (reasoning) alone.

The word <s>pramāṇa</s> has etymological derivation both in the sense of the state (of valid cognition) and of the instrument (of valid cognition).
1. Thus, some hold that valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) itself is <s>pramāṇa</s>.
2. Others hold that only the instrument of valid cognition (<s>pramākaraṇa</s>) is <s>pramāṇa</s>.
3. Yet others hold that it is either of the two.
4. <s>Pramāṇa</s> is cognition that accords with well-established practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>).
5. That from ignorance of which there is <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth), and from knowledge of which there is its cessation—that is <s>prameya</s> (the knowable) for seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), because it is to be known preeminently.
6. That is twofold, due to the distinction between <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>adravya</s> (non-substance).
7. Or, in general, the object of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is <s>prameya</s>.
8. <s>Dravya</s> (substance) is the substratum of adventitious attributes (<s>āgantukadharma</s>).
9. That which is not of such nature is <s>adravya</s> (non-substance).
10. <s>Dravya</s> is twofold: <s>jaḍa</s> (non-sentient) and <s>ajaḍa</s> (sentient).
11. <s>Jaḍa</s> is also twofold: <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Kāla</s> (time).
12. <s>Ajaḍa</s> is likewise twofold: <s>pratyak</s> (self-luminous/subjective) and <s>parāk</s> (other-luminous/objective).
13. <s>Pratyak</s> is also twofold: <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).
14. <s>Parāk</s> is likewise twofold: <s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s> (attributive knowledge) and <s>nityavibhūti</s> (eternal glory).
15. Alternatively, <s>dravya</s> is twofold due to the distinction between <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>anātman</s> (non-self).
16. Or threefold, following the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) regarding the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), the enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>), and the controller (<s>niyantṛ</s>).
17. Or sixfold, due to the distinctions of <s>triguṇa</s> (the three-guṇa entity, i.e. Prakṛti), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), <s>śuddhasattva</s> (pure sattva), and <s>mati</s> (cognition/attributive knowledge).
18. That which does not shine by itself is <s>jaḍa</s> (non-sentient).
19. That which is self-luminous (<s>svayaṃprakāśa</s>) is <s>ajaḍa</s> (sentient).
20. <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter) is the substratum of mixed <s>sattva</s> (<s>miśrasattva</s>).
21. <s>Kāla</s> (time) is the cause of practical distinctions such as moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>), interval (<s>lava</s>), and so forth.
22. That which shines for itself is <s>pratyak</s> (subjective/self-aware).
23. That which shines for another is <s>parāk</s> (objective/other-directed).
24. The dependent sentient being is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).
25. The independent one is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).
26. The illumination of objects is <s>buddhi</s> (cognition/attributive knowledge).
27. That which is distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s> and yet is a substratum of <s>sattva</s> is <s>nityavibhūti</s> (eternal glory).
28. <s>Adravya</s> (non-substance) is manifold, due to the variety of <s>sattva</s>, <s>śabda</s> (sound), and so forth.
29. One entity, qualified by the rest, is preeminently the <s>prameya</s>—the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
30. Because all the others have their ultimate ground in <s>Brahman</s> alone.
31. And because scripture declares that it is He alone who is to be known preeminently by seekers of liberation.
32. <s>Saṃśaya</s> (doubt) is cognition that causes unsettled practical activity.
33. <s>Viparyaya</s> (error) is cognition that causes incorrect practical activity.
34. <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) is cognition born solely from mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
35. <s>Anubhava</s> (experience) is cognition other than that (i.e. other than memory).
36. <s>Prayojana</s> (purpose) is that which is the aim of a person's activity.
37. <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is the locus for the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance).
38. <s>Siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) is a proposition accepted by those deemed authoritative.
39. <s>Avayavas</s> (members of a syllogism) are the sub-statements of the statement that constitutes a demonstration (<s>parārthapramāṇaprayoga</s>) for others.
40. <s>Tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is the derivation of an undesired consequence regarding the <s>vyāpaka</s> (pervader) through the acceptance of the <s>vyāpya</s> (pervaded).
41. <s>Nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment) is the definitive determination of reality preceded by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) aided by <s>tarka</s>.
42. <s>Vāda</s> (debate) is discussion free from passion.
43. <s>Jalpa</s> (wrangling) is a disputatious discussion aimed at victory, employing arguments for both sides.
44. <s>Vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) is that same (disputation) devoid of the establishment of one's own counter-position.
45. <s>Hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) are those deficient in one or more components of a valid reason (<s>hetu</s>).
46. <s>Chala</s> (quibble) is a refutation by attributing an unintended meaning to a word.
47. <s>Jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) is a refutation that is vitiated by the same fault as one's own (position).
48. <s>Nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) is the indication of a debater's incapacity.
49. Could not such statements as these themselves be <s>sūtras</s>? Here, a concise definitional statement is a <s>sūtra</s>; a statement providing illustrations and so forth is <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) and the like—one should be satisfied having discerned this distinction.
Nor is the rule that the earlier [formulation] takes precedence [valid here], because such a prior [formulation as this] is possible, and because a <s>vārtika</s> (supplementary work) would then have no occasion to appear, and because in grammar and other disciplines the acceptance of alternative formulations is observed.

children.text:
yattu "jñātasaṃbandhasya" ityādigranthamupādāyānantaramuktaṃ śrīviṣṇucitteḥ---- "vyāptidhīgarbhānubhavo 'numānamityarthaḥ /
nyāyaśāstre tu tadviśeṣanirṇayaḥ" iti, tadapi tannirūpaṇādhikṛtavidyāsthānakhyāpanaparam /
pramāṇādisūtramupādāya vyācakṣāṇaistatpakṣaniṣṭhairapi pūrvaiḥ kvacit sūtrāṇi nirākṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Even the earlier authorities who were adherents of that (Nyāya) school, while expounding by taking up the <s>sūtras</s> on <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth, have in certain places rejected [some of those] <s>sūtras</s>.
The reasoning of that [Nyāya] system is for us neither a snake-killing (something to fear) nor a warding off of punishment (something that constrains us).

children.text: tataśca, yathālokaṃ yathāvedaṃ laukike vaidike 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in accordance with common experience and in accordance with the <s>Veda</s>, in both the secular and the Vedic domains,

children.text: yo vaktā sa parigrāhyaḥ prāktano 'dyatano 'pi vā //
children.translated_text: whoever speaks [truly] is to be accepted, whether ancient or modern.

As for what <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> said, taking up the passage beginning with "of one who knows the relation" and then stating: "Experience containing the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference)—this is the meaning. But the detailed determination thereof belongs to the <s>Nyāya</s> treatise"—that too is merely aimed at indicating the domain of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>) in which that analysis is undertaken.

children.text: vivakṣitārthāvaiśadyaṃ vyākulatvamapūrṇatā ullokatetyamī doṣā guṇakoṭau jaḍaiḥ kṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: Lack of clarity in the intended meaning, confusion, and incompleteness are flaws that dull minds (<s>jaḍa</s>) have placed in the category of merits.
By the venerable <s>Nārthamuni</s> (i.e. <s>Nāthamuni</s>), the path of <s>Nyāya</s> named <s>Nyāyatattva</s>,
was composed, setting aside the [systems of] <s>Akṣapāda</s> and others.
By later teachers who adopted whatever doctrines they preferred,
the investigation of <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth was carried out in many ways by various [thinkers].
Thus, this is the position of exclusion (of Nyāya as an independent authority), which is established in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself.
<s>Nyā. Pa. Pra.</s> 3 (Nyāyapariśuddhi, section 3).
The position of accepting the <s>sūtras</s> of <s>Gautama</s>.
For those who desire acceptance, even the <s>Ākṣapādīya</s> (Nyāya system) will stand in the manner exclusively stated by us; we shall establish it precisely thus.

children.text: ato vayamapi mahatāmayuktārthatātparyakalpanena nāparādhyema, nyūnādhikaviruddhavyapadeśādīnāmalakṣaṇalakṣaṇoktīnāṃ cādhyāhārānyaparyāmyāṃ tadbhakterapi nirvāhāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we too would not offend the great ones by attributing to them an intent toward unreasonable doctrines, since even devotion to them can be maintained through the supplying of what is deficient, excess, contradictory designations, and statements of non-definitional definitions where no other interpretation is possible.

children.text: tathāsmin yatra sphuṭaḥ śrutismṛtiśārīrakavirodhaḥ, sa uddeśato niruhyate //
children.translated_text: Thus, wherever in this [Nyāya system] there is a manifest contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> (revelation), <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), and the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtras), that is refuted in the appropriate place.

children.text: yattāvatsūtritaṃ prathamādhyāye --- "ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakchrotrāṇīndriyāṇi bhūtebhyaḥ" iti; atra jñānendriyapañkopādānaṃ nendriyāntarapratikṣepārtham, manasaḥ pṛthakprameyatayā uddeśāt anantarameva ca "yugapajjñānānutpattirmanaso liṅgam" iti lakṣaṇakaraṇāt abhyupagamasiddhāntanyāyena ca tadindriyatvaparīkṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: First, what is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> of the first chapter: "Nose, tongue, eye, skin, and ears are the sense organs, [arising] from the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>)"—here, the mention of only five cognitive sense organs (<s>jñānendriya</s>) is not meant to exclude other sense organs, since <s>manas</s> (mind) is separately listed as a <s>prameya</s> (knowable), and immediately after, its definition is given as "Non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the mark of <s>manas</s>," and since by the principle of a commonly accepted doctrine (<s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>), its status as a sense organ is examined.

children.text: ataścoktena samānayogakṣemayuktipramāṇakaḥ karmendriyavarga upalakṣaṇīyaḥ, "pravṛttirvāgbuddhiśarīrārambhaḥ" iti sūtre vācaḥ kaṇṭhokteḥ pāṇyādicatuṣṭayasya śārīravyāpārakaraṇatayā sūcanāditi //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the reasoning and authority that share the same standing as what has been stated, the group of motor sense organs (<s>karmendriya</s>) should be understood as indicated by implication, since in the <s>sūtra</s> "Activity is the initiation of speech, intellect, and body," speech (<s>vāc</s>) is explicitly mentioned, and the four organs beginning with the hands (<s>pāṇi</s>) are suggested as instruments of bodily activity.

children.text:
śarīrake tu "saptagaterviśeṣitatvācca" iti pūrvapakṣamupakṣipyāsādhayacca hastādīnāmapīndriyatvaṃ bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ--- "hastādayastu sthite 'to naivam" iti /
"bhūtebhyaḥ" iti ca nopādānābhiprāyam, ahaṅkāropāttānāmāpyāyakabhūtavivakṣayāpi tadupapatteḥ /
tathā ca vedārthasaṃgrahe---"evamāhaṅkārikāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ bhūtaiścāpyāyanaṃ mahābhārata ucyate" iti /

children.translated_text: This reconciliation is for the purpose of maintaining the consistency of statements by other sages (<s>ṛṣi</s>) that follow the same principle.

children.text: parasparaviruddhapramāṇavākyeṣu tātparyaviśeṣaparikalpanayā parihāra eva hi paṇḍitakṛtyam /
children.translated_text: For in the case of mutually contradictory authoritative statements, reconciliation through determining the specific purport (<s>tātparya</s>) is indeed the proper task of the learned.

children.text: anityamanovādibhirapi hi "annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ"--- iti śrutirāpyāyanaparatayaiva yojyā /
children.translated_text: For even by those who hold the mind to be non-eternal and so forth, the <s>śruti</s> "The mind, O <s>Somya</s>, is indeed made of food" must be construed as having its purport in nourishment (<s>āpyāyana</s>).
This applies equally elsewhere as well.

In the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtras), however, the venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, having raised as a preliminary objection "because the seven [sense organs] are distinguished by [their] movement" and having then refuted the sense-organ status of the hands and so forth, [stated]: "But the hands and so forth, since this is established, are not so."
The phrase "from the elements (<s>bhūtebhyaḥ</s>)" is not meant in the sense of material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), since it can be explained by the intended meaning that the sense organs produced from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) are nourished (<s>āpyāyana</s>) by the elements.
Thus in the <s>Vedārthasaṃgraha</s>: "Thus, the nourishment of the sense organs produced from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> by the elements is stated in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>."

children.text: yattu---"bādhanālakṣaṇaṃ duḥkham" "tadatyantavimokṣo 'pavargaḥ" iti, tatra duḥkhātyantanivṛtterapavargatvaṃ sarvāṅgīkṛtam /
na ca tatrānandaḥ śrautaḥ kaṇṭhoktyāḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: And the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) taught by <s>śruti</s> (scripture) is not denied therein by explicit statement.

children.text: tadabhiprāye cānanyathāsiddhaṃ kimapi na liṅgaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the intended view of that [Nyāya system], we see no inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that is not otherwise explicable [to support the denial of bliss in liberation].

For this very reason, in the view of [<s>Nyāya</s>] <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Udayana</s>'s <s>Nyāyakusumāñjali</s> or a related work), the connection with the experience of eternal bliss (<s>nityasukhasaṃvedana</s>) has been established in <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).
By this, the statement of the fourth chapter "Therefore, the absolute release from all suffering is <s>apavarga</s>" is also resolved, since there too there is no denial of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss).

As for [the Nyāya statements]: "Pain (<s>duḥkha</s>) is that which has the characteristic of affliction (<s>bādhana</s>)" and "The absolute release from that is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation)"—here, the status of <s>apavarga</s> as the absolute cessation of suffering is accepted by all.

children.text:
yacca śārīrakadvitīyādhyāyaviruddhamiha dvitīyādhyāye avayavisamarthanamivābhāti, tadapi tadekārthaṃ yojayituṃ śakyam /
tathā hi---"na caikadeśopalabdhiravayavisadbhāvāt /
sādhyatvādavayavini saṃdehaḥ /
sarvāgrahaṇamavayavyasiddheḥ /
dhāraṇākarṣaṇopapatteśca /
senāvanavadgrahaṇamiti cennātīndriyatvādaṇūnām /
" ityetāni hi tatsūtrāṇi; na tāni virudhyante, senāvanādivyāvṛttāvayavyārambhakatayā tadasamavāyikāraṇatvābhimatāvasthāviśeṣāpannaḥ saṃghātaviśeṣa evāvayaviśabdena nirdiṃśyata ityavirodhāt tāvataiva upalambhavyavahāraviśeṣādeścaritārthatvāt /

children.translated_text: The statement about atoms being beyond the senses is also not contradictory, since it is accepted that even sensible things, like the parts of a lamp-flame, become imperceptible in certain states—just as [the atoms become imperceptible] through a particular state.
For the scripturally-minded (<s>āgamika</s>) hold that the three-<s>guṇa</s> substance, which is indeed unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), becomes manifest through a particular state.

Even for things that are individually imperceptible, the variation in perceptibility and its gradations due to differences of state in the form of special aggregations (<s>saṃhativiśeṣa</s>) is well-established in the world in cases of snow-powder, heaps, and the like, where no [separate] whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is produced.

As for the defense of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), this has been resolved by those who accept only a part of the <s>Nyāya</s> system, as being aimed merely at rejecting the subsumption of <s>upamāna</s> under <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

And as for what appears in the second chapter [of the Nyāyasūtras] to be a defense of <s>avayavin</s> (the whole as distinct from parts), which seems to contradict the second chapter of the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtras)—that too can be construed as having the same purport.
For the <s>sūtras</s> there are: "Not from the perception of one part, because the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) exists. Doubt regarding the whole, because it is to be proved. Non-apprehension of all [parts simultaneously] is due to the non-establishment of the whole. And because of the possibility of support and attraction. If it be said that apprehension is like that of an army or a forest, [we say] no, because atoms are beyond the senses."
These <s>sūtras</s> are not contradictory [to Vedānta], because there is no conflict if the word <s>avayavin</s> (whole) is understood to designate a special configuration (<s>saṃghātaviśeṣa</s>)—a state attained by a particular arrangement—which is distinct from the whole as conceived in the army-and-forest analogy, and which serves as the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) as maintained [by the Nyāya school], and because the particular modes of perception and practical activity are fully accounted for by just this much.

And where [in the Nyāyasūtras], having raised the objection "because filling, burning, and splitting are not perceived, there is no relation [between word and meaning]" regarding the absence of a relation between word and meaning, the resolution is given: "There is no prohibition, because of the settled convention between word and meaning (<s>śabdārthavyavasthāna</s>)."

children.text: "na sāmayikatvācchabdādarthe pratyayasya" ityādinā sāmayikatvamuktam; tadapi saṃpratipannasāmayikatvadvārā anumānādivilakṣaṇasaṃbandhaviśeṣakhyāpanārthamiti yojyam, anādinidhanāvicchinnasaṃpradāyavedavartināṃ padānāṃ manvādivacanaviruddhasāṃketikatvopapādanakḷptyasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: The statement "The cognition from a word regarding its object is not conventional (<s>sāmayika</s>)" and so forth, asserting conventionality—this too should be construed as aimed at revealing a special type of relation (<s>saṃbandhaviśeṣa</s>) distinct from <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and the like, through the acknowledged conventionality, since it is impossible to devise an explanation that would establish a merely stipulated (<s>sāṃketika</s>) character—contradicting the statements of <s>Manu</s> and others—for words that belong to the <s>Veda</s>, whose tradition is beginningless and endless and unbroken.

children.text: yacca "mantrāyurvedaprāmāṇyavacca tatprāmāṇyamāptaprāmāṇyāt" iti, etadapyanādinidhanasyaiva vedasya pratikalpamīśvareṇāptatamena yathāpūrvaṃ pravartanamabhisaṃdhāyeti sugamam //
children.translated_text: And the [Nyāya] statement "The authority of <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s> is like that [of the Veda], due to the authority of trustworthy persons (<s>āpta</s>)"—this too is easily understood as having in view the promulgation of the <s>Veda</s> itself, which is beginningless and endless, by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the most trustworthy, in each cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>) in accordance with its prior form.
The discussion of the non-eternality of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) is not contradictory to <s>śruti</s> and other authorities; rather, it is actually favorable.

children.text: śārīrakadevatādhikaraṇe varṇānityatvamabhyupagamyaiva hi "ata eka ca nityatvam" "samānanāmarūpatvāccāvṛttāvapyavirodho darśanāt smṛteśca" iti vedanityatvaṃ sādhitam //
children.translated_text: In the <s>devatādhikaraṇa</s> (section on deities) of the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtras), it is precisely by accepting the non-eternality of phonemes that the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is established [through the sūtras]: "Therefore, one and eternality" and "Because of the sameness of name and form, there is no contradiction even in [cosmic] repetition, as is seen and as <s>smṛti</s> states."

children.text: yattu jaiminīye śabdādhikaraṇe varṇanityatvasamarthanaṃ vyācakhyuḥ; sa tu vyākhyātṝṇāmevāparādhaḥ, asāṃketikavācakākāranityatvaparatvenānyaparatvāttasyādhikaraṇasya //
children.translated_text: As for the defense of the eternality of phonemes in the <s>Śabdādhikaraṇa</s> (section on word) of the <s>Jaiminīya</s> (Mīmāṃsāsūtras) as expounded by the commentators—that is the fault of the commentators themselves, since that <s>adhikaraṇa</s> has a different purport, namely the eternality of the form (<s>ākāra</s>) of words as non-conventional designators.

children.text:
yacca dvitīyādhyāyānte "vyaktyākṛtijātayastu padārthaḥ"ityuktam, tatrāpi na vaiśeṣikābhyupagatajātisvīkāre liṅgaṃ paśyāmaḥ; nahyatra dravyaguṇādipadārthaparisaṃkhyānaṃ kriyate, "te vibhaktyantāḥ padam" iti pratipāditapadavācyapradarśanaparatvāt /
anantaraṃ catisṛṇāmeva lakṣaṇamāha---"vyaktirguṇaviśeṣāśrayo mūrtiḥ""ākṛtirjātiliṅgākhyā" "samānaprasavātmikā jātiḥ" iti /

children.translated_text: Here, however, this should be construed as appropriate in terms of the nature of the real entity (<s>vastusvarūpa</s>), the distinguishing attribute whose nature is determined by that entity (<s>svarūpanirūpitasvarūpaviśeṣakadharma</s>), and the attribute that determines that distinguishing attribute (<s>svarūpanirūpakadharma</s>).
Therefore, even in the second chapter there is no contradiction with <s>Vedānta</s>.

In the third [<s>adhyāya</s>], the passage beginning with "from the apprehension of a single object by sight and touch" and the examination of external and internal <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) and so forth is extremely useful.

children.text: na ca manonityatvādikaṃ tatra sūtritam; yena tadutpattyādiśrutikopaḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor is the eternality of <s>manas</s> (mind) and such matters taught in those <s>sūtras</s>; so there is no conflict with the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) teaching its origination and so forth.

And the statement at the end of the second chapter, "<s>Vyakti</s> (individual), <s>ākṛti</s> (form/configuration), and <s>jāti</s> (universal) are the meaning of a word"—here too we see no inferential mark for accepting the <s>jāti</s> (universal) as conceived by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>; for here there is no enumeration of categories (<s>padārtha</s>) such as substance, quality, and so forth, since the purpose is to indicate the denotata of words as established in the statement "Those ending in case-suffixes are words (<s>pada</s>)."
Immediately after, the definitions of only these three are given: "<s>Vyakti</s> (individual) is a corporeal entity (<s>mūrti</s>) that is the substratum of particular qualities," "<s>Ākṛti</s> (form) is that called <s>jātiliṅga</s> (the mark of the universal)," and "<s>Jāti</s> (universal) is that whose nature is [producing] similar offspring (<s>samānaprasava</s>)."

children.text: yaccātroktam---"gandhakledapākavyūhāvakāśadānebhyaḥ pāñcabhautikaṃ śrutiprāmāṇyācca" iti, etadeva yathāśrutaṃ siddhāntatayā svīkāryam /
yadapi "gandharasarūpasparśaśabdānāṃ sparśaparyantāḥ pṛthivyāḥ" "aptejovāyūnāṃ pūrvapūrvamapohyākāśasyottaraḥ" iti guṇavyavasthāpanam, tatra tu tathaivābhyupagame 'pi na vastvantaravirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Also, the determination of qualities—"of earth, [the qualities are] smell, taste, color, touch, and sound, up to touch" and "of water, fire, air, each preceding [quality] is removed, and of <s>ākāśa</s> (space), the last"—even if accepted exactly as stated, there is no contradiction with any other reality.

children.text: tathāpyākāśādiṣu śabdāderekadvitricatuṣpañcakrameṇa purāṇeṣu pāṭhāt, ākāśānupraveśādanyatra śabda iti nirvāhe vārūvādyanupraveśāduttarottareṣu sparśādiriti nirvoḍhuṃ śakyatvāt, upalambhānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vyavasthāpanasyāpi samatvāt, gandhādisūtraṃ pṛthivyāste santyevetyayogavyavacchedena nirvāhyam /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, since in the <s>Purāṇas</s> there is the reading that in <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest, sound and so forth occur in a sequence of one, two, three, four, and five; and since in the resolution that sound exists in other [elements] due to the interpenetration of <s>ākāśa</s>, it is possible to explain that touch and the rest exist in each successive [element] due to the interpenetration of water and so forth; and since the establishment [of qualities] by the co-presence and co-absence of perception is equally [applicable], the <s>sūtra</s> on smell and so forth should be resolved by exclusive attribution (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>), meaning that earth possesses these [qualities].
In the passage "of <s>ākāśa</s>, the last," [the resolution is] by inclusive attribution (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>), meaning that that [quality] belongs to it alone.

children.text: kati kati caivaṃ sūtrāṇi kliṣṭāni parairapi niruhyante //
children.translated_text: How many such <s>sūtras</s> are laboriously explained even by others!
