Moreover: In the eternal [<s>Veda</s>], there is no dependence on the qualities of a cause, just as there is no cognition of a Lord [as author]. If [you say] there is no defect because there is no cause —
then for us too [there is no defect], because there is no speaker [of the <s>Veda</s>]. Just as cognition that is uncaused attains the status of being a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramātva</s>),
so too a statement that is uncaused is intrinsically a cause of valid cognition.
— [that is the position].
If invalidity would follow from the absence of qualities in the cause,
then this [consequence] is unavoidable for you too, even with respect to the valid cognition of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 17 athaiva brūṣe---kāraṇaguṇadoṣayorabhāve tatprayojyayoḥ prāmāṇyāprāmāṇyayordvayorapyasaṃbhavādraśyantarāyogācca niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ vedaśabdajanyajñānānāṃ syāditi; idamapi tulyamīśvarajñāne /
hetunivṛttistatkāryaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ nivartayet, na tu nityamiti cet, aprāmāṇyahetunivṛttirapi tathaiva /
ato viruddhasvabhāvayogaḥ ubhayaparityāgānniḥsvabhāvaitava vā syāt /
evamanīśvaravādināṃ saugatādīnāṃ śuddhasaṃvitsantānādiṣvadhipatisahakāryādikāraṇatadguṇāderasaṃbhavāt svārasikasvātmagocaraprāmāṇyasya cābhyupagamāt samāścarcāḥ /
yadyapi pūrvapratyayasyakāraṇatvamiṣṭam, tathāpi tasyāpavargadaśāsthasya guṇadoṣādirūpasamastasaṃskārapratyarthitayā na tajjanyasya guṇahetuteti /
yacca, prāmāṇyaṃ parato jñāyate, iti prayuktam, tatra jñānāntareṇa jñānāntarasvabhāvavedanābhyupagamāt siddhasādhanatā /
parata eveti vivakṣāyāmīdṛśaṃ jñānaṃ prameti lakṣaṇataḥ sarvapramāsaṅgrāhiṇi jñāne pārameśvare ca vijñāne tadasaṃbhavaḥ; na hi tābhyāṃ svapramātvaṃ na gṛhītam, lakṣaṇāvyāptikiñcijjñatvādiprasaṅgāt /
atonyatra parata eveti niyama iti cet, tadapi na, taddṛṣṭāntenaiva pratiprayoktuṃ śakyatvāt-vigītaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ svādhāreṇa jñāyate, prāmāṇyarūpatvāt, riśvarajñānādiprāmāṇyavat iti /
kathaṃ tarhi idaṃ pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ veti saṃśayāvakāśaḥ ? iti cenna, viśeṣato gṛhyamāṇeṣvapi saṃśayotpattidarśanāt /
bhavati muhuḥ śuktikārajatamohādandhīkṛtadhiyaḥ kaladhautepi tathopalabhyamāne yathopalambhamidaṃ rajatameva vā pūrvavacchuktirajataṃ veti purataḥ /
tathātrāpi gṛhyamāṇepi prāmāṇye kimidaṃ pramāṇameva sat pramāṇatayopalambhate ? uta, bādhāt pūrvabhramavadapramāṇaṃ sat ? iti saṃśayo yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly here too, even when validity is grasped, the doubt is reasonable: 'Is this really valid and apprehended as valid? Or is it, like the previous error, actually invalid due to subsequent sublation (<s>bādha</s>)?'

children.text: tathāpi sandehasahena kiṃ svatograhaṇena ? niścayastu parādhīna eveti cet, kimasmadapekṣayā grahaṇamagrahaṇaṃ vā niyantuṃ śakyam ? siddho hi grahaṇaprakāraḥ parīkṣakairanusaraṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, what is the use of apprehension that is intrinsic yet accompanied by doubt? If [you say] certainty is dependent on something else alone — [we reply:] can apprehension or non-apprehension be regulated at our will? For the mode of apprehension that is established must be followed by investigators.

children.text: siddhireva svataḥ kathamiti cet, ittham---jñānaṃ svālambanaṃ prakāśayat svayamapi jñānāntaranirapekṣaṃ prakāśate, iti tāvat sarvavedāntisaṃmatam /
children.translated_text: If [you ask] 'How is the establishment itself intrinsic?' — [we answer] thus: A cognition, while illuminating its own object, itself also becomes manifest without depending on another cognition — this much is accepted by all <s>Vedāntins</s>.

Even on the view that [cognition] is not self-luminous, the cognitive act (<s>vyavasāya</s>), being illuminated by the apperceptive cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) that grasps it, is seen as itself free from doubt.

<s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 17. Now if you say: 'In the absence of both qualities and defects of the cause, since both validity and invalidity — which are produced by those [qualities and defects] — are impossible, and since no other alternative is available, the cognitions produced by Vedic words would be without any nature' — this too applies equally to the cognition of the Lord.
If [you say] the cessation of the cause would remove its effect, namely validity, but not [what is] permanent — [we reply:] the cessation of the cause of invalidity would equally [fail to affect what is permanent].
Therefore, [you face] the combination of contradictory natures, or else both would be abandoned, resulting in your [cognitions] being without any nature.
Thus the same considerations apply equally to those who do not accept a Lord — the <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists) and others — since in the pure stream of consciousness (<s>śuddha-saṃvit-santāna</s>) and the like, causes such as governing conditions (<s>adhipati</s>) and cooperative factors (<s>sahakārin</s>), and the qualities of such causes, are impossible, and yet they accept intrinsic validity with respect to their own objects.
Even though the preceding cognition is accepted as a cause, still, since in the state of final liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) that [preceding cognition] has counteracted all impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) in the form of qualities and defects, the [cognition] produced by it does not have a cause of qualities.
And as for the assertion that 'validity is known from another [cognition]' (<s>parato jñāyate</s>) — there, since it is accepted that one cognition cognizes the nature of another cognition, there is the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).
If the intended meaning is 'only from another' — then such a cognition 'this cognition is valid,' being a comprehensive grasp of all valid cognitions through their definition, and also divine cognition, cannot [itself be known from another]; for their own validity is not ungrasped by them, since otherwise there would follow non-pervasion of the definition, partial knowledge, and the like.
If [you say] 'the restriction that [validity is known] only from another applies elsewhere [but not to these]' — that too is not [tenable], because it can be counter-argued by the very same example: 'Contested validity is known through its own substrate, because it has the nature of validity — like the validity of the Lord's cognition and the like.'
If [you ask] 'How then is there room for doubt of the form "Is this a valid means of knowledge or not?"' — [we reply:] this is not [a problem], because the arising of doubt is observed even regarding things that are grasped in their specific form.
Indeed, one whose intellect has been blinded by the delusion of shell-silver often [thinks], even when gold is perceived just as it is: 'Is this really silver, or is it shell-silver as before?' — directly.

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 18 smṛtyaprāmāṇyavādepyapūrvārthagocaratayā smṛtivilakṣaṇaścāviparyayātmā cābādhātmā ca, vādhādeḥ pūrvaṃ tatprasaṅgābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 18. Even on the view that memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is not a valid means of knowledge, [the initial cognitive act] is distinct from memory insofar as it has a novel object (<s>apūrvārthagocaratā</s>), is of the nature of non-error (<s>aviparyaya</s>), and is of the nature of non-sublation (<s>abādha</s>), since prior to sublation there is no occasion for [attributing] that [defect].

children.text: tataśca yadviṣayatayāyaṃ vyavasāyaḥ prathamaṃ pratibhātaḥ, tadviṣayatayaiva parasparaparikṣodāt paścādapi /
children.translated_text: And therefore, the object with respect to which this cognitive act first appeared — it is with respect to that very object that [it continues to appear] even subsequently, through the mutual corroboration [of cognitions].

children.text: ato yat tadviṣayatvalakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ paścāt tenaiva vyavasthāpyate, tadādāveva gṛhītamiti svataḥ prāmāṇyagrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that validity which has the nature of having that object, and which is subsequently established by that very [cognition] — that was already grasped at the very beginning. Thus, the apprehension of validity is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇyagrahaḥ</s>).

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 19 nanvevaṃ saṃśayatvādilakṣaṇamaprāmāṇyamapi svayaṃprakāśenānuvyavasāyena vā prathamamave grahītuṃ śakyam; tathāpi viparyayatvalakṣaṇaṃ na tathā, gṛhyamāṇavaiparītyasya svena svagrāhiṇā vā prathamamagrahaṇāt, tasminnaṃśe ca vaidikānāmavivādāt, tatremamaṃśamādāyaiva cāntataḥ pasvataḥ prāmāṇyasamarthanapravṛtteḥ, tatra doṣābhāvādevādāvaprāmāṇyānutpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 19. Now, [if you object:] in this way, invalidity too, characterized by doubt and the like, could be grasped at the very beginning through the self-luminous [cognition] or through apperception (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>). Nevertheless, invalidity characterized by erroneousness (<s>viparyayatva</s>) is not [grasped] in that way, because the erroneousness that is being grasped is not grasped at the beginning by [the cognition] itself or by what grasps it, and on this point there is no dispute among the <s>Vaidikas</s>. And it is only by accepting this aspect that the effort to establish intrinsic validity ultimately proceeds. [This is] because, in the absence of defects, invalidity does not arise at the beginning.

children.text: tata eva cāprāmāṇyapramityasaṃbhavāt, svata eva ca prāmāṇyapramiterabādhācca ityucyate, iti //
children.translated_text: And for that very reason, because the cognition of invalidity is impossible [at the beginning], and because the cognition of validity is intrinsically unsublated — thus it is stated.

children.text: iti kavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu nyāyapariśuddhau śabdādhyāye prathamamāhnikam
children.translated_text: Thus, in the works of <s>Kavitārkikasiṃha</s> (the lion among poets and logicians), <s>Sarvatantrasvatantra</s> (master of all systems), the blessed <s>Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the <s>Vedāntācārya</s> — in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in the chapter on <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony), the first session (<s>āhnika</s>).
Salutation to the blessed <s>Nigamānta Mahādeśika</s>.
The second session (<s>āhnika</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 20 atha pauruṣeyāpauruṣeyavibhāga evānupapannaḥ, sarvasyāpi vākyasya pauruṣeyatve vākyatvādiliṅgasadbhāvāt---sarvajñapraṇītā vedāḥ, vedatvāt, iti vyatirekisaṃbhavāt; "mantrakṛdbhyaḥ" "tasya ha vā etasya mahato bhūtasya niśvasitametadyadṛgvedaḥ" "ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire /
chandāṃsi jajñire tasmāt /
yajustasmādajāyata" ityādiśravaṇāt, "pratimanvantaraṃ caiṣā śrutiranyā vidhīyate" ityādismṛteśca;"adhikṛtya kṛte granthe" iti pāṇinismṛtisiddhārthakāṭhakakālāpakādisamākhyāviśeṣayogāt; kādācitkakathāviśeṣasaṃdṛṣṭeḥ, anityayogāt, tatpūrvottarakālayostadananvayāpatteḥ, śabdasya bhūtaguṇasya naśvaratvāt, iti cet, tanna, vākyatvānumānasya vipakṣe bādhakābhāvāt /
akāraṇakāryotpattiprasaṅgaḥ, iti cenna, kāryatvasyaiva sādhyamānatvāt, akāraṇatvamātrasyāpādyamāna syeṣṭatvāt /
kramaviśeṣeṇānuccāryamāṇānāṃ varṇānāṃ kathaṃ padatvaṃ vākyatvaṃ veti cenna, parakṛtaprabandhapāṭhavadakartṛbhiruccāraṇepi tatsiddheḥ /
ādimamuccāraṇaṃ kartrabhāve kathaṃ syāditi cenna, ādimattvasyaivāsiddheḥ, darśanānuguṇyena adyatvavadeva sarvadā paratantroccāraṇasyaivābhyupagantumucitatvāt, tataśca sarvadoccārayitṛpuruṣāpekṣatvepi pūrvapūrvādhītaprakārasyānusaraṇādanāditvasiddheḥ /
apauruṣeyatve ghuṇakṣatākṣaravadūbodhakatvepyabhiprāyavirahādarthaparatvaṃ na syāditi cenna, pratipanne nirbādhe cārthe pradhāne bodhakatvasyaiva tātparyarūpatvāt, prādhānyāderlaukikavākyavadākhyātādisvabhāvādeva siddheḥ, asmadiṣṭe ca seśvaramīmāṃsāpakṣe nityeśvarābhiprāyasaṃbhavāt /
svayameva hyāha--- "śrutiḥ smṛtirmamaivājñā" iti /
tathā bhāṣyam--- "svaśāsanāvabodhi śāstramiti nityaṃ śrutyaiva niyuṅkte paraḥ" iti /
nityāpi sā tadājñā /
gītādirapi śrutyarthopadeśarūpatayā pravartate /
sākṣāttu śrutistadādośaḥ /
tadanuvidhānācca smṛtirapi /
ajñātakartṛkatve gandharvabhāṣitādivadāptakartṛkatvaniścayābhāvādaprāmāṇyaśaṅkā syāditi cenna, doṣābhāvaniścayādeva tannivṛtteḥ /

children.translated_text: If [you ask:] 'When there is doubt about [the <s>Veda</s>] having an untrustworthy author, how can there be certainty of the absence of defects?' — [we reply:] no [problem], because the doubt of an untrustworthy authorship is uprooted by the very acceptance of the great community (<s>mahājana</s>).

children.text: bāhyāgamaparigrahavat kiṃ nasyāt ? iti cenna, bahujanaparigrahādimātrasya mahājanaparigrahatvenāvivakṣitatvāt, tatpariprahaviśeṣasyaiva vivakṣitatvācca /
children.translated_text: If [you say:] 'Would not the same apply to the acceptance of heterodox scriptures (<s>bāhyāgama</s>)?' — [we reply:] no, because the mere acceptance by many people is not what is intended by 'acceptance of the great community,' but rather a specific kind of acceptance is intended.

children.text: tayoḥ ko vā viśeṣaḥ ? iti cenna, hetudarśanādarśanābhyāṃ viśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: If [you ask:] 'What then is the distinction between the two?' — [we reply:] the distinction lies in the observation or non-observation of [ulterior] motives.

children.text: ananyagatikaiḥ svairarasikaiḥ sukhajīvikārthibhiḥ kuhakavañcitairvā tatparigrahaḥ, iha tu na tathā, tadvaiparītyasya suprasiddhatvāt, iti //
children.translated_text: The acceptance of those [heterodox scriptures] is by those who have no other recourse, by those driven by personal taste, by those seeking easy livelihood, or by those deceived by charlatans. But here [with the <s>Veda</s>] it is not so, because the opposite [of all these conditions] is well-established.

<s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 20. Now, the very distinction between authored (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) and authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) [scripture] is untenable — since all statements have the status of being authored, given the presence of indicators such as being-a-statement; and since an argument by negative concomitance is possible: 'The <s>Vedas</s> are composed by an omniscient being, because they are <s>Vedas</s>'; and because of scriptural passages such as 'From the seers of the <s>mantras</s>,' 'Indeed, of this great being, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the exhalation,' and '<s>Ṛc</s> verses and <s>Sāman</s> chants were born, metres were born from that, and the <s>Yajus</s> was born from that'; and because of <s>smṛtis</s> such as 'In every <s>Manvantara</s>, a different <s>Śruti</s> is ordained'; and because of the specific names like <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and <s>Kālāpa</s>, whose meaning is established by the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule 'When a work is composed with reference to [someone]' (<s>adhikṛtya kṛte granthe</s>); because of the observation of particular occasional narratives; because of [the <s>Veda</s>'s] connection with impermanence; because of the impossibility of its continuity in the times before and after [the cosmic dissolution]; and because sound, being a quality of the element [air], is perishable — if [all this is argued], it is not so, because the inference from being-a-statement lacks a counter-positive that would serve as a defeater.
The undesirable consequence of an effect arising without a cause [would follow] — if [you say] this, [we reply:] no, because being-an-effect is itself what is being established, and because the mere absence of a cause is acceptable for what is being argued.
If [you ask] how phonemes that are not uttered in a specific sequence can have word-hood or sentence-hood — [we reply:] no [problem], because this is established even in the recitation by those who are not authors, just as in the reading of a text composed by someone else.
If [you ask] how there could be a first utterance in the absence of an author — [we reply:] no [problem], because the very existence of a 'first [utterance]' is unestablished; and because, just as with the present [utterance], it is appropriate to accept that utterance has always been dependent [on prior tradition], in accordance with what is observed. And therefore, even though utterance at all times depends on human [agents], the authorlessness (<s>anāditva</s>) is established because [each generation] follows the manner of study of its predecessors.
If [you say] that even granting authorlessness, since [the <s>Veda</s>] would be unintelligible — like letters eaten by bookworms — and since there is no [author's] intention, there could be no purposive meaning (<s>arthaparatva</s>) — [we reply:] no, because intelligibility itself constitutes intentionality (<s>tātparya</s>) when the meaning that is understood is uncontradicted and primary; because primacy and the like are established from the very nature of verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>) and so forth, just as in ordinary speech; and because on our accepted position of theistic <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, the intention of the eternal Lord is possible.
For He Himself declares: 'Scripture and <s>Smṛti</s> are My very command.' Likewise the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [states]: 'The Supreme [Lord] enjoins through scripture alone, [which is] a teaching that conveys His own command.' Even though eternal, that [scripture] is His command.
Even the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> and the like operate as instruction in the meaning of scripture.
But scripture directly [conveys His command] — hence no fault.
And <s>Smṛti</s> too, because it follows [scripture].
If [you say] that when the author is unknown, there would be a doubt about validity, as with the speech of <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial beings) and the like, since there is no certainty of a trustworthy author — [we reply:] no, because that [doubt] is removed by the very certainty of the absence of defects.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 21 api ca bāhyāgamapratibandiḥ kiṃ vadeprāmāṇyamāptaprāmāṇyanibandhanamitīcchadbhirvaiśeṣikādibhirucyate ? uta saugatādyāgamaprāmāṇyamicchadbhiḥ ? atha vā parityaktāśeṣapāralaukikāgamairlokāyatikaiḥ ? iti /
nādyaḥ, riśvarakṛtatvepi vedasyaivaṃvidhaparigrahaviśeṣamantareṇādyatanarebāhyāgamebhyo (?) vivekasyāśakyatvāt, sarvajñapraṇītatvādyabhimānasya tadanumānaprakriyāyāśca sarvatra durvāratvāt /

children.translated_text: Not the second — because the same consequence would apply to their own scripture whose validity they accept.

children.text: dṛṣṭaphalasaṃvādasya visaṃvādānyathāsiddheśca sarvatra samacarcatvāt, asmaduktasya nirupādhikaparigrahasya svamate durvacatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the considerations regarding agreement with observed results, and the otherwise-explicability of disagreement, apply equally everywhere; and because the unconditional acceptance that we have described is difficult to maintain in their own system.

children.text: ata eva na tṛtīyaḥ, prāmāṇyasya parokṣaprāmāṇyasya vākyaprāmāṇyasya ca sthāpitatvena vaidikavākye hyautsargike prāmāṇye prāpte nirupādhikaprekṣāvadanantapuruṣaparigrahādevānāptakartṛkatvaśaṅkonmūlane ca vaktṛdoṣaśaṅkānutthānāt, vacasi casvataḥ kācādivaddoṣādarśanāt /
children.translated_text: For the same reason, not the third either — because, since the validity of knowledge (<s>prāmāṇya</s>), the validity of testimony regarding imperceptible matters, and the validity of statements have all been established, when the general-rule validity of Vedic statements has been obtained, and when the doubt of an untrustworthy author has been uprooted by the unconditional acceptance of innumerable discerning persons (<s>prekṣāvat</s>), no suspicion of the speaker's defect arises; and because in the statement itself, no defect is observed — like [defects in] crystal and the like — intrinsically.
Even in the absence of a trustworthy author, the general-rule validity [of the <s>Veda</s>] remains unsublated.

<s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 21. Moreover, is the objection against the validity of heterodox scripture being raised by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others who hold that the invalidity of the <s>Veda</s> depends on the validity of a trustworthy person? Or by those who desire to establish the validity of Buddhist and other scriptures? Or by the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (Materialists) who have abandoned all supramundane scripture? Not the first — because even if the <s>Veda</s> is made by the Lord, without this specific kind of acceptance [by the great community], there is no way to distinguish it today from heterodox scriptures; and because the claim of composition by an omniscient being, and the inferential procedure for it, are equally irresistible everywhere.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 22 ata eva hi prekṣāvantaraścoditeṣu bahuvittavyayāyāsasādhyeṣu niśaṅkaṃ pravartante, pratiṣiddheṣu ca sukhatareṣvapi viṣasaṃsṛṣṭānnabhojanādivannivartante /
prayogaśca---pāralaukikī mahājanapravṛttiḥ saphalā, prekṣāvatpravṛttitvāt, kṛṣyādipravṛttivat; na hyanantaiḥprekṣāvadbhiravisaṃvādenāphalamanuṣṭhīyate iti śaṅkituṃ śakyam /
duḥkharūphaladarśanena siddhasādhanateti cenna, anabhipretopālambhāt, pravṛttiduḥkhādadhikapuruṣārthaparyavasānasya siṣādhayiṣitatvāt /
tathāpi lābhapūjākhyātirūpadṛṣṭaprayojanenaiva sārthateti cet, tadapyasat, ataduddeśena teṣāṃ pravṛttidarśanāt, taduddeśena pravṛtteśca ḍāmbhikatvena śāstraistanniṣṭhaiśca vigarhaṇāt /
ye ca taduddeśena pravartante, tepyataduddeśena pravṛttānāmanukurvāṇā eva khyātyādi prāpnuvanti, anyathā khyātilābhapūjādernirnimittatvaprasaṅgāt /
na hi yatkiñcidanena kṛtamiti matvā kaścit kṛcchrasaṃpāditān dhanādīn dadāti, pūjayati, guṇānvā āropya stauti; api tu kutaścit pramāṇāt siddhaṃ praśastācaraṇamabhimatyaiva /
samarasāmarthyādimūlalābha jādikamapyantatorthaśāstrādimūlapraśastapravṛttiprasūtam /
ataḥ sanmaryādāpravṛttān dānamānādibhirabhyarcayantoṣpadṛṣṭabuddhyaiva pravartante /
janarañjanārthameva dānādi, jano dātari mānayitari ca rajyate, "janānurāgaprabhavāśca saṃpadaḥ" iti prasiddheḥ, iti cenna, pratyupakārādyanarhapravrajitatapasvijaḍāndhabadhiradīnānāthādiṣu dānamānādibhiranurañjiteṣvapi tanmūladṛṣṭasaṃpatprasaṅgābhāvāt; ata eva hi nītinarmasaciveṣveva tadarthadānādivyavasthāpanam /

children.translated_text: If [you say] 'They are deceived by Vedic practitioners who are skilled in deception, and therefore honor them' — [we reply:] no.

children.text: kiṃ te svātmānamapi pratārayanti? ye nāma samastabhogāvimukhā yāvajjīvamātmānaṃ parikleśayanti; yaiśca paṭuprajñāḥ sarve lokāḥ pratāritāḥ, te kathaṃ lokottaraprajñena tvayā pratārakā ityunnītāḥ /
children.translated_text: Do they deceive even themselves? — those who, averse to all enjoyments, torment themselves throughout life. And those by whom all the clever people of the world have been 'deceived' — how have they been exposed as deceivers by you, whose wisdom is supposedly beyond the world?

children.text: andhaparamparākalpastarhyayamanuṣṭhānapravāhaḥ iti cenna, pramāṇasvarūpaphalayorabādhasya ca pratyakṣatvāt dharmabuddhyaiva ca nirupādhikaparigrahasya tvaduktyaiva siddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'Then this stream of [religious] practice is like a blind tradition following the blind' — [we reply:] no, because the nature and result of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) are directly perceptible, and because the unconditional acceptance [of the <s>Veda</s>] is motivated by the conviction of <s>dharma</s> — as is established by your own statement.

children.text: anādinidhanesminnāmnāyamūle anuṣṭhāne pravahati prakriyāntaramāśritya pratārakairīśvarairarvācīnaiśca praticchandapravartanā śrutismṛtisiddhā yuktimatī cetyeṣā dik //
children.translated_text: In this authoritative tradition (<s>āmnāya</s>) that is without beginning or end, while the stream of practice flows on, the establishment — based on alternative procedure — of [the right of] the Lords (<s>Īśvaras</s>) and later [teachers] who are deceivers acting according to their own whims, is [itself] established by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, and is supported by reasoning — this is the direction [of our argument].

<s>Nyā. Pa.</s> Section 22. For this very reason, discerning persons (<s>prekṣāvat</s>) engage without hesitation in prescribed actions that require the expenditure of much wealth and effort, and they abstain even from very pleasant prohibited things — like [abstaining from] food mixed with poison.
And the argument [is as follows]: Supramundane activity by the great community is fruitful (<s>saphala</s>), because it is the activity of discerning persons — like activity in agriculture and the like. For it cannot be doubted that innumerable discerning persons would engage fruitlessly without [experiencing] any contradiction.
If [you say] this proves what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), since the observation of suffering as a result [is already available] — [we reply:] no, because [suffering] is apprehended as unintended, and because [the practitioners] intend to establish that [the result] culminates in a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) greater than the suffering involved in the practice.
If [you say] that even so, [the activity] is fully explained by visible purposes alone such as gain, honor, and fame — that too is wrong, because those [practitioners] are observed to engage without any such intention, and because engagement with such an intention is censured as hypocrisy (<s>ḍāmbhika</s>) by the scriptures and by those devoted to them.
And those who do engage with such an intention — they too obtain fame and the like only by imitating those who engage without such intention; otherwise, fame, gain, and honor would be without any basis. For no one gives away wealth acquired with difficulty, or honors, or praises by attributing virtues, merely thinking 'this person did something or other'; rather, [they do so] only by esteeming praiseworthy conduct that is established from some valid source of knowledge.
Even gain and the like that are rooted in natural ability and similar [qualities] ultimately originate from praiseworthy conduct rooted in the treatises on <s>artha</s> and the like.
Therefore, those who honor the adherents of good conduct with gifts, respect, and the like, act only with the understanding that this is beneficial as seen [in valid sources].
If [you say] gift-giving and the like are merely for pleasing people, and people are pleased with givers and those who honor them — as it is well known that 'prosperities arise from the affection of the people' — [we reply:] no, because even when beggars, ascetics who have renounced [all], the dull, the blind, the deaf, the destitute, and the orphaned are pleased by gifts and honor, there is no occasion for visible prosperity arising from that. And for this very reason, the giving and honoring for such purpose is prescribed [only] with respect to counselors skilled in politics and entertainment.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 23 vedānityatvānumānānāṃ pratiprayogāśca---parvāparakalpāḥ etadvedasandarbhapāṭhavantaḥ, kalpatvāt, adyatanakalpavat /
aiśvaraṃ vedapravartanamapracyutaprācīnasandarbham, āptakartṛkavedapravartanarūpatvāt, adyatananipuṇopādhyāyavedapravartanavat; na cāśrayādyasiddhiḥ, pauruṣeyatvepi prāmāṇyamicchatastata eva tatsiddheḥ /
aprāmāṇyamicchatopi mahājanaparigrahānyathānupapattyaiva prāmāṇyaṃ prasādhya tata eva tatsādhanāt /
na cāsti vedapravartanasya sārasvatapāṭhenānaikāntyam, tathaiva tatpravāhasya tattacchākhāpraṇayanavadanāditvāt, mantrabrāhmaṇādivākyasvarūpavaiyākulīvirahācceti /
evaṃvipakṣe bādhakābhāvādeva kevalavyatirekyapi nirastaḥ, anumānādhyāye tasya sāmānyato dūṣitatvācca /
tvanmatepyāyurvedādisapakṣasadbhāvena tasyāsādhāraṇyam; nahi tebhyo vyāvṛttamapauruṣeyatvādilakṣaṇaṃ vedatvaṃ tvayābhyupagamyate /
vedaśabdaprayogaviṣayatāmātreṇa teṣāmapi pakṣīkāre svecchāgṛhītarūpasyeśvarasya tattadavatārasaṃvyavahārā vedavyatiriktāḥ santi sapakṣāḥ /
na ca te tvayāpi neṣyante, vedatayā vā svīkriyante, gītādiṣu bhagavaduktyaṃśānāṃ śrīviṣṇusmṛtiprabhṛtīnāṃ ca vedatvānabhyupagamāt /
dharmaśāstratayaiva hi vaiṣṇavasmṛtyādiprasiddhiḥ /
avaktṛkasandarbhā vedāḥ, vedatvāt, yaḥ sakartṛkasandarbhaḥ, nāsau vedaḥ, iti pratihetuśca siddhaḥ /
aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatvādicodyaṃ tviha na tvayā smartavyam /
sandarbhaḥ kathamavavatṛkaḥ syāditi cenna, varṇakramaniyamamātraviśeṣasya sandarbhaśabdena grahaṇāt,tasya ca prāguktanayena yathāpūrvapravartanamātreṇāpi vyavasthānāt /
mābhūdavītahetuḥ /
vītastu syāt vigītaṃ vākyaṃ sarvajñapraṇītaṃ, pramāṇatve satyalaukikārthaviṣayavākyatvāt, "na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsam" ityādivākyavat, iti cenna, vedārthaviṣayaiḥ kalpasūtrakārādivākyairasmadādivākyaireva vānaikāntyāt /
atīvakartṛkatve satīti viśeṣayiṣyāmaḥ iti cenna, tathāpi yathāpūrvapraṇayanamātreṇāpi tatpraṇītatvasiddhau siddhasādhanāt /
yathāpūrvameva hi viśvamīśvaraḥ sṛjati; yathā adhīmahe--- "sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat" iti /
evaṃ tarhitulyayogakṣematayā vedavajjagatopyakartṛkatvaṃ prasaktamiti cenna, yathāpūrvaṃ ghaṭādinirmāṇe kulālakuvindādeḥ kartṛtvasiddheḥ; hanta ! vedasya evaṃ syāditi cet, hanta ! syādeva /
children.translated_text: If it is objected that in that case, since the <s>Veda</s> and the world would be in the same position, the absence of an author would apply to the world as well — no, because the authorship of the potter, weaver, and such is established in the making of pots and so forth as before. If one says: 'Well then, let it be so for the <s>Veda</s> too!' — well then, let it indeed be so!

children.text: na hi kalpāntaravarṇavyaktisamudāyamevedānīntanavedarāśiṃ brūmaḥ, api tu tādṛkkramayogitāmātram /
children.translated_text: For we do not claim that the present corpus of <s>Vedas</s> is the very same collection of particular phoneme-instances from another <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle); rather, [we claim] merely the possession of the same sequential arrangement.

children.text: sarvatra vākyeṣu yatheṣṭakramakalpane puruṣasya svātantryoktiḥ, na punaryathāpuroccāraṇe, iti kāvyādiṣvapi prasiddham /
children.translated_text: The autonomy of a person is spoken of in composing sentences in whatever order one wishes, not in uttering them as before — this is well-known even in poetry and such [literary compositions].

children.text: yadi tvayā ayathāpurapraṇītatvaṃ sādhyeta, tatra yathāpurapraṇayane kamiva doṣāmālakṣyaivaṃ viśeṣayasi ? mantrādiṣu kramabhaṅgānupapattiśca kalpāntarepi tacchaktyanapāyādeva, tathātvepi vā yathāpūrvoccāraṇepi tadanapāyāt, anyathā kalpanāgauravāt, iti //
children.translated_text: If you were to prove that [the Veda] was composed not-as-before, then what fault do you perceive in composition-as-before that you make such a qualification? And the impossibility of disruption of sequence in <s>mantras</s> and such [follows] because even in another <s>kalpa</s> their potency does not depart; or even granting that [disruption], because even in utterance-as-before that [potency] does not depart; otherwise, there would be the fault of excessive postulation. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 23. Counter-arguments (<s>pratiprayoga</s>) to the inferences for the non-eternality of the <s>Veda</s> — The previous and subsequent <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles) possess the same textual arrangement of this <s>Veda</s>, because they are <s>kalpas</s>, just like the present <s>kalpa</s>. / The divine promulgation of the <s>Veda</s> preserves the ancient arrangement without deviation, because it has the nature of promulgation of the <s>Veda</s> by a reliable author, just like the promulgation of the <s>Veda</s> by a skilled teacher today; nor is there the defect of unestablished substratum and so forth, because even for one who accepts authoritativeness despite accepting human authorship, that [divine existence] is established from that very [authoritativeness]. / Even for one who denies authoritativeness, since authoritativeness is first established through the impossibility of otherwise explaining the acceptance by great persons, that [divine existence] is established from that very [authoritativeness]. / Nor is there indeterminacy (<s>anaikāntya</s>) in the promulgation of the <s>Veda</s> due to <s>Sārasvata</s> recitation and the like, because the tradition-stream of that [Veda] itself is beginningless just like the composition of its various branches, and because there is no disturbance to the essential form of <s>mantra</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and other sentences. / Since there is no defeater in the opposing side, the purely negative inference (<s>kevala-vyatirekin</s>) is also refuted, and because it has been generally refuted in the chapter on inference. / Even in your own position, due to the existence of positive instances such as <s>Āyurveda</s> and the like, that [inference] is not exclusive (<s>asādhāraṇya</s>); for you do not accept <s>Veda</s>-hood characterized by being non-human-authored and so forth as distinct from those [texts]. / If those [texts] too are made objects of dispute merely by being referred to by the word '<s>Veda</s>,' then when <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) whose form is assumed at will takes various incarnations, those transactions are positive instances distinct from the <s>Veda</s>. / Nor are they denied even by you, nor accepted as <s>Veda</s>, since the portions spoken by the Lord in the <s>Gītā</s> and such, as well as the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Smṛti</s> and the like, are not accepted as <s>Veda</s>. / For the <s>Vaiṣṇava Smṛtis</s> and such are well-known only as <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (texts of law). / The <s>Vedas</s> are authorless compositions, because they are <s>Vedas</s>; whatever is an authored composition, that is not a <s>Veda</s> — this counter-reason (<s>pratihetu</s>) is also established. / But the objection of unestablished qualifier and the like should not be raised by you here. / If asked how a composition can be without an author — it is because the word 'composition' (<s>sandarbha</s>) grasps merely the specific arrangement of the sequence of phonemes, and because that [arrangement] is maintained merely through promulgation as before, according to the principle stated earlier. / Let there not be a defeated reason. / But if one says: a defeated [counter-argument] would be — 'A sentence composed by an omniscient being is authoritative, because it is a sentence about non-worldly matters while being authoritative, just like the sentence "Never indeed was I not" and such' — no, because of indeterminacy with sentences of <s>Kalpasūtra</s> authors and such, or with our own sentences regarding Vedic matters. / If one says 'we shall qualify it: when there is supreme authorship' — even so, since authorship by that [omniscient being] is established merely by composing as before, this is proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). / For <s>Īśvara</s> creates the universe exactly as before; as we learn — '<s>Dhātā</s> (the Creator) fashioned the sun and moon as before.'

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 24 tathāpi sargapralayasaṃbhavāt saṃpradāyavicchede sarvavedocchedāt paścādīśvarastatsraṣṭā syāt /
na syāt, tathāpi prācīnavedasākṣātkāriṇastasya tatpravartanamātraucityāt, śaktasyāpi tajjātīyavedāntarakalpane gauravāt, śaktāvapi siddhopajīvanasyāsmadādiṣu dṛṣṭeḥ, eṣāmeva ca mantrāṇāṃ kalpāntarepi mantratvāvirodhāt /
evaṃ mantranityatve ca tulyanyāyatayā brāhmaṇanityatvasyāpi dustyajatvāt, taddṛṣṭāntena vā tannityatvasādhanāt /
sārasvatapāṭhādāvapi mantrādisvarūpabhedābhāvasyoktatvāt /
"yā brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vai vedāṃśca prahiṇoti tasmai /
" "vācāvirūpanityayā""pūrve pūrvebhyo vaca etadūcuḥ" "ajān ha vai praśnīṃstapasyamānāt brahma svayaṃ bhyabhyānar ṣat ta ṛṣayobhavan tadṛṣīṇāmṛṣitvam" "anādinidhanā hyeṣā vāgutsṛṣṭā svayaṃbhuvā" "vyasya vedaṃ sanātanam" ityādibhirīśvarasyāpyanīśvaravadvedapravartanamātrasiddheḥ kutaśca sargapralayasiddhiḥ ? viśvasantatiratyantamucchidyate, santatitvāt, pradīpasantativat /
viśvasantānoyaṃ dṛśyasantānahīnaiḥ samavāyibhirārabdhaḥ, santānatvāt, āraṇeyāgnisantānavat /
vartamānabrahmāṇḍaparamāṇavaḥ pūrvamutpāditasajātīyasantānāntarāḥ, nityatve sati tadārambhakatvāt, pradīpaparamāṇuvat /

children.translated_text: Even mountains will be pulverized, because they have parts, like a pot.

children.text: samudrā api śoṣamupayāsyanti, jalāśayatvāt, palvalavat ityādyanumānataḥ, iti cenna, keṣāṃ cinnityasaṃsārapakṣe prathamasya hetostathā tatpratipādakairāgamairaṃśato bādhaḥ, tadvahiṣkāre ca anaikāntaḥ; sarveṣāṃ ca śrutiśatasiddhairnityavibhūtiniṣṭhairīśvaranityavigrahādibhistaistairanekāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even oceans will dry up, because they are reservoirs of water, like a puddle — if such inferences [are offered against eternality], no; for those who hold the position of eternal <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), the first reason is partially contradicted (<s>bādha</s>) by the scriptures that establish it; and if those [scriptures] are excluded, there is indeterminacy (<s>anaikāntya</s>). And for all of them, there is indeterminacy through the various [entities] established by hundreds of <s>śrutis</s> (Vedic texts) that pertain to the eternal realm — <s>Īśvara's</s> eternal body and so forth.
Nor can those be made objects of the thesis (<s>pakṣīkāra</s>), because one would fall into either contradiction (<s>bādha</s>) or the already-established (<s>siddhi</s>).

children.text: pratiprayogāśca---gaṇitaviśeṣādisiddhadvipārārdhasaṃkhyāpūrvottarakālo na lokaśūnyaḥ, kālatvāt, adyatanakālavat, ityādayaḥ svayamūhyāḥ //
children.translated_text: And the counter-arguments: The time extending over eons measured by the number <s>dvīparārdha</s> (half the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>), established through specific mathematical calculations, both before and after, is not devoid of a world, because it is time, just like the present time — such and similar [counter-arguments] should be formulated by oneself. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 24. Even so, since creation and dissolution occur, when the tradition is broken and all <s>Vedas</s> are destroyed, <s>Īśvara</s> would thereafter be their creator. / He would not be; even then, because it is fitting that He, who directly perceives the ancient <s>Veda</s>, merely promulgates it; because even when capable, there is the fault of unnecessarily creating a different <s>Veda</s> of the same kind; because even when capable, we observe [Him] relying on what already exists, as in our own case; and because these very <s>mantras</s> being <s>mantras</s> even in another <s>kalpa</s> is not contradictory. / And since, when the eternality of <s>mantras</s> is thus established, the eternality of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [texts] too is difficult to abandon by the same reasoning, or because the eternality of the latter is established by the former as an example. / Because the absence of essential difference in <s>mantras</s> and such even in <s>Sārasvata</s> recitation and the like has been stated. / '<s>Yā Brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvam, yo vai Vedāṃśca prahiṇoti tasmai</s>' ('She who creates <s>Brahmā</s> first, He who sends forth the <s>Vedas</s> to him'), '<s>Vācā virūpa nityayā</s>' ('By eternal speech, O <s>Virūpa</s>'), '<s>Pūrve pūrvebhyo vaca etad ūcuḥ</s>' ('The ancients spoke this speech to their ancients'), '<s>Ajān ha vai praśnīṃs tapasyamānāt brahma svayaṃbhyabhyānarṣat, ta ṛṣayo 'bhavan, tad ṛṣīṇām ṛṣitvam</s>' ('To the unborn ones engaged in inquiry and austerity, <s>Brahman</s> itself flowed forth of its own accord; they became <s>ṛṣis</s> — that is the <s>ṛṣi</s>-hood of the <s>ṛṣis</s>'), '<s>Anādinidhanā hy eṣā vāg utsṛṣṭā svayaṃbhuvā</s>' ('For this speech, beginningless and endless, was sent forth by the Self-born'), '<s>Vyasya Vedaṃ sanātanam</s>' ('Having divided the eternal <s>Veda</s>') — from such [texts], since it is established that even <s>Īśvara</s> merely promulgates the <s>Veda</s> as one who is not its originator. And whence is the establishment of creation and dissolution? The continuity of the universe is never completely cut off, because it is a continuum, like the continuum of a lamp. / This world-continuum is begun by constituent causes that lack a visible break in continuity, because it is a continuum, like the continuum of fire from fire-sticks. / The atoms of the present universe are of the same kind as those produced previously, belonging to another continuum, because while being eternal they are the cause of that [universe], like the atoms of a lamp.

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 25 vipakṣe bādhakaṃ na samyagdṛśyate /
yaccāgamānugraha eṣāṃ balamityabhimatam, tadāgamapramāṇatvopajīvanam, tathā cāgamata eva pralayādisiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And as for the claim that these [inferences for non-eternality] have their strength in the support of scripture (<s>āgama</s>) — that relies on the authoritativeness of scripture, and thus the establishment of dissolution and so forth comes from scripture alone.
And therefore, from scripture alone the eternality of scripture is established.

children.text: uktaṃ ca prajñāparitrāṇe--- "vedataḥ pauruṣeyatvaśaṅkā vede na śāmyati /
children.translated_text: And it has been said in the <s>Prajñāparitrāṇa</s> — 'The doubt of human authorship regarding the <s>Veda</s> does not subside in the <s>Veda</s>;
arising from one set of reasons, it is dispelled by another set of reasons.' //
<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 25. The defeater (<s>bādhaka</s>) against the opposing side is not properly discerned.
Thus.

And the manner of the acceptance of the <s>Veda</s> at the beginning of creation has been explained thus — 'Since there are no persons engaged in ordinary usage, and since the comprehension of words is impossible,

children.text: vedārtho naiva śakyeta boddhuṃ tasyeti cenna tat //
children.translated_text: the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> could not be understood by him [<s>Brahmā</s>] — if this is said, it is not so. //
There indeed exist many who are engaged in the usage of words and their meanings —
the liberated souls and others, or the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), or because of the assumption of manifold forms [by the Lord]. //
Or, for this Creator (<s>Vedhas</s>), through the continuation of the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of knowledge from the previous [cycle],
the knowledge of all words and their meanings would arise, like one awakened from sleep. //
For them there is no [passage through] dwelling in the womb, nor stages of age and the like;
they are created endowed with all knowledge — thus the understanding of the <s>Veda</s> [is explained]. //
By the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) '<s>Yo Brahmāṇam</s>' ('He who [creates] <s>Brahmā</s>'), <s>Īśvara</s>, having created <s>Brahmā</s>,
gave the <s>Vedas</s> to him — does not this understanding arise? //
The giving of the <s>Veda</s> to one who knows words and their meanings would be meaningful;
otherwise it would be purposeless — therefore, by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), [<s>Brahmā</s>'s] knowledge of words and their meanings [is established].' //
Thus. //

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 26 sūtrakāṇḍamantrakṛttvajanmādivākyānāmapi prathamadraṣṭṛtvasmartṛtvasaṃpradāyapravartanādibhireva nirvāhaḥ /
idamapyāgamānurodhādeva siddham /
"svayaṃbhvabhyānarṣat" ityādi hi śrūyate /
prajāpatiniyogācca tadāhitamahimāno maharṣayonadhītāneva vedabhāgān paśyanti /
tannniyogaśca tattadṛṣikatvenānusandhānādeḥ karmaupayikatvāt /

children.translated_text: Since even their [the <s>ṛṣis</s>'] tradition-stream is beginningless, there is no defect of non-eternal conjunction and the like.

children.text: "yadvai kiñca manuravadat" ityādau pravāhānāditvaṃ parairuktam; tadupākhyānāntarādiṣvapi tulyam /
children.translated_text: In passages such as '<s>Yad vai kiñca Manur avadat</s>' ('Whatever <s>Manu</s> said'), the beginninglessness of the tradition-stream has been stated by the opponents themselves; the same applies to the sub-narratives and so forth therein.

children.text: uktaṃ ca bhagavatā vyāsena--- "yugāntentarhitān vedān setihāsān maharṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it has been said by the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> — 'The great <s>ṛṣis</s>, at the end of the <s>yuga</s> (cosmic age), having lost [access to] the <s>Vedas</s> together with the <s>itihāsas</s> (histories),
obtained them again through austerity, being authorized by the Self-born (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>).' //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 26. Even for the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>Sūtras</s>) and the statements about the creatorship of <s>mantras</s>, birth, and so forth — the explanation is through being the first seer, the recollector, and the initiator of the tradition, and so on. / This too is established only in accordance with scripture. / For the <s>śruti</s> says: '<s>Svayaṃbhvabhyānarṣat</s>' ('It flowed forth from the Self-born of its own accord'). / And by the command of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the great <s>ṛṣis</s>, endowed with glory through that [command], see the portions of the <s>Veda</s> that they have not [formally] studied. / And that command [of <s>Prajāpati</s>] is because the investigation [of mantras] as authored by the respective <s>ṛṣis</s> and the like is useful for ritual purposes.
Thus. //
Here, '<s>itihāsa</s>' means the respective historical accounts.
And it has been said by the same [<s>Vyāsa</s>] in the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> as well — 'They call the <s>Veda</s>, an uncreated mass of texts, the root of <s>dharma</s>;
and [also] the <s>smṛti</s> and conduct of those who know it, and virtuous custom dear to the heart.' //
Thus.

And the arrangement of the branches (<s>śākhā-praṇayana</s>) [of the <s>Veda</s>] at the end of <s>Dvāpara</s> [yuga] is the extraction of a portion of the tree of the <s>Veda</s>, due to the decline of the powers of future persons.
By this, the designation [of the <s>Veda</s> as '<s>pravacana</s>' (that which is taught)] is explained, because it is an object of teaching. //

children.text: idaṃ ca sarvaṃ prasādhitaṃ prajñāparitrāṇe--- "yādṛkprabhāvāḥ śrūyante ṛṣyādyā vedarāśiṣu /
children.translated_text: And all this has been established in the <s>Prajñāparitrāṇa</s> — 'The <s>ṛṣis</s> and others are created by the Self-born (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>) with exactly the same powers as are heard of in the Vedic corpus;

children.text: tādṛśā eva sṛjyante vedān dṛṣṭvā svayaṃbhuvā //
children.translated_text: having seen the <s>Vedas</s>, [they are created] by the Self-born. //
Therefore, since the <s>Veda</s> existed prior to them, the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> [is established],
because of [the <s>ṛṣis</s>] being manifesters of the <s>Vedas</s> without having studied them. //
Through austerity, from [the awakening of latent] impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the possibility of their being <s>sūktas</s> (hymns) and so forth arises;
through the power of austerity, from the refinement of the <s>mantras</s> by the seers' vision, //
a certain capacity is acquired, just as for us [it comes] from study;
but the capacity to convey meaning belongs to the word by its own power, like any other word. //
Even for one who has not studied, through the seer's vision, another capacity arises;
this would be helpful for the accomplishment of unprecedented results (<s>apūrva</s>). //
This alone is the reason for the designations such as <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and the like,
or else the distinguished teaching [is the reason] — thus the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is established.' //
Thus. //

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 27 varṇānityatvaṃ kramānityatā vā nābhimatavedanityatvavirodhi /
na ca varṇanityatvaṃ vedanityatvahetuḥ, kāvyādiṣvapi tulyatvāt /

children.translated_text: And we do not accept the <s>Śabdādhikaraṇa</s> (the section on word [in the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>]) as being about the irrelevant eternality of phonemes.

children.text: śārīrakadevatānadhikaraṇe ca--- "śabda iti cenna, ataḥ prabhavāt pratyakṣānumānābhyām /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Bhāṣya], in the <s>Devatānadhikaraṇa</s> (the section on the deity) — '<s>Śabda iti cenna, ataḥ prabhavāt pratyakṣānumānābhyām</s>' ('If it be said [that <s>Brahman</s> is not the cause] because of [the Vedic] word, [we say] no, because the origination [of the world] from that [<s>Brahman</s>] is [established] by perception and inference');
'And from this very [fact] follows [its] eternality';

children.text: samānanāmarūpatvācca, āvṛttāvapyavirodho darśanāt, smṛteśca" iti sūtrairidaṃ sarvaṃ samarthitam //
children.translated_text: 'And because of the sameness of names and forms, there is no contradiction even in recurrence, as is seen [in scripture] and from <s>smṛti</s>' — by these <s>sūtras</s>, all this has been substantiated. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 27. The non-eternality of phonemes or the non-eternality of sequence does not contradict the accepted eternality of the <s>Veda</s>. / Nor is the eternality of phonemes a reason for the eternality of the <s>Veda</s>, since the same would apply to poetry and such.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 28 vedārthasaṅgahe tu---vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ cet, vidhyarthavādamantrāgataṃ sarvamapūrvamarthajātaṃ yathāvasthitameva bodhayanti /
prāmāṇyaṃ ca vedānām 'autpattikastu śabdasyārtthena saṃbandhaḥ' ityuktam" iti mantrārthavādayorapi yāthārthyaṃ prakramya, śabdaśakterasāṅketikatvam, tata eva śabdānumānavivekaḥ pauruṣeyāpauruṣeyādivibhāgādikaṃ ca vyaktaṃ pradarśitam /
tathāhi---yathā agnijalādīnāmauṣṇyādiśaktiyogaḥ svābhāvikaḥ; yathā cakṣurādīnāmindriyāṇāṃ buddhijanakatvaśaktiḥ svābhāvikī, tathā śabdasyāpi bodhakatvaśaktiḥ svābhāvikī /
na ca hastaceṣṭādivat saṅketamūlaṃ śabdasya bodhakatvamiti vaktuṃ yuktam, avanādyanusandhānāvicchedepi saṅketayitṛpuruṣājñānāt /
yāni saṅketamūlāni, tāni sarvāṇi sākṣādvā paramparayā vā vijñāyante /
children.translated_text: Those [significatory devices] that are based on convention are all known either directly or through a chain of transmission.

children.text: na ca devadattādiśabdavat kalpayituṃ yuktam; teṣu sākṣādvā paramparayāṃ vā saṃketo jñāyate /
children.translated_text: Nor is it proper to treat [common words] like the word '<s>Devadatta</s>' and such [proper names]; for in those cases, the convention is known either directly or through tradition.

children.text: gavādiśabdānāṃ tu anādyamusandhānāvicchedepi saṃketājñānādeva bodhakatvaśaktiḥ svābhāvikī /
children.translated_text: But for words like '<s>go</s>' (cow) and such, even though there is no break in the beginningless tradition, it is precisely because the convention is unknown that the capacity to produce knowledge is natural —
like the power of heat and so forth in fire and such, and like the capacity of the sense organs to produce knowledge, the capacity of words too to produce knowledge must necessarily be accepted. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 28. In the <s>Vedārthasaṅgraha</s>, however — 'If the <s>Vedas</s> are authoritative, then they convey the entire body of unprecedented meanings (<s>apūrva arthajāta</s>) found in injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>), explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), and <s>mantras</s>, just as they actually are. / And the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedas</s> has been stated [by <s>Jaimini</s>]: "The relation of the word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>)." ' Thus, having introduced the veridicality of <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> as well, the non-conventional nature of word-power (<s>śabdaśakti</s>), and from that the distinction between verbal testimony and inference, and the classification into human-authored and non-human-authored and so forth — [all this] has been clearly demonstrated. / Namely — just as the connection of fire, water, and such with powers like heat and so forth is natural; and just as the capacity of the sense organs such as the eye and so forth to produce cognition is natural; so too the capacity of words to produce knowledge is natural. / Nor is it proper to say that the capacity of words to produce knowledge is based on convention (<s>saṅketa</s>), like hand-gestures and so forth, because even when there is no break in the tradition from the beginningless [past], the person who established the convention is not known.

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 29 nanu ca indriyavacchabdasyāpi bodhakatvaṃ svābhāvikaṃ cet, saṃbandhagrahaṃ bodhakatvāya kimityapekṣate ?; liṅgavadityucyate; yathā jñātasaṃbandhaniyamaṃ dhūmādi agnyādibuddhijanakam, tathā jñātasaṃbandhaniyamaḥ śabdopyarthaviśeṣabuddhijanakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 29. But if, like the sense organs, the capacity of words to produce knowledge is also natural, why does it require the apprehension of a relation [between word and meaning] for producing knowledge? It is said: like an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>); just as smoke and such, when their invariable relation is known, produce the cognition of fire and so forth, so too a word, when its invariable relation is known, produces the cognition of a specific meaning.

children.text: evaṃ tarhi śabdopyarthaviśeṣasya liṅgamityanumānameva syāt; maivam; śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho bodhyabodhakabhāva eva /
children.translated_text: If so, then a word too would be an inferential mark for a specific meaning, and [verbal testimony] would be nothing but inference. Not so; for the relation between word and meaning is precisely that of what is to be conveyed and what conveys it (<s>bodhya-bodhaka-bhāva</s>).

children.text: dhūmādīnāṃ tu saṃbandhāntaramiti, tasya saṃbandhasya jñāpanadvāreṇa buddhijanakatvamiti viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for smoke and such, the relation is of a different kind [namely, the relation of effect to cause and so forth], and it is through the cognition of that relation that [smoke] produces knowledge — this is the distinction.

children.text: evaṃ gṛhītasaṃbandhasya bodhakatvadarśanādanādyanusaṃdhānāvicchedepi saṃṅketājñānāt bodhakatvavaṃ śaktireveti niścīyate //
children.translated_text: Thus, since we observe that one who has apprehended the relation [between word and meaning] has the capacity to produce knowledge, even when there is no break in the beginningless tradition, because the convention is unknown, it is ascertained that the capacity to produce knowledge is indeed a [natural] power (<s>śakti</s>). //

children.text: evaṃ bodhakānāṃ padasaṃghātānāṃ saṃsargaviśeṣabodhakatvena vākyaśabdābhidheyānāmuccāraṇakramo yatra puruṣabuddhipūrvakaḥ, te pauruṣeyāḥ śabdāḥ ityucyante /
children.translated_text: Thus, among those [words] that produce knowledge, the collections of words (<s>padasaṃghāta</s>) whose utterance-sequence is preceded by human intention, which convey specific relations [among meanings] in the capacity of sentences (<s>vākya</s>) — those are called '<s>pauruṣeya</s>' (human-authored) verbal expressions.

children.text: yatra tūccāraṇakramaḥ pūrvapūrvoccāraṇakramajanitasaṃskārapūrvakaḥ sarvadā, apauruṣeyāste vedāḥ ityucyante /
children.translated_text: Where, however, the order of utterance is always preceded by impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by the prior sequence of utterance, those are called the authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: etadeva vedānāmapauruṣeyatvaṃ nityatvaṃ ca, yat pūrvoccāraṇakramajanitasaṃskāreṇa kramaviśeṣaṃ smṛtvā tenaiva krameṇoccāryatvam /
children.translated_text: This alone is the <s>apauruṣeyatva</s> (authorlessness) and <s>nityatva</s> (eternality) of the <s>Vedas</s> — namely, that they are uttered in that very same sequence, having recalled the particular order through the impression generated by the prior sequence of utterance.

children.text: tenānupūrvīviśeṣeṇa tameva saṃsthitā akṣararāśayo vedā ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvabhedena bhinnāḥ anantaśākhā vartanta iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, established in that very fixed sequence (<s>anupūrvī</s>), those collections of syllables constitute the <s>Vedas</s>, which are divided according to the distinctions of <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s>, and subsist in infinite branches (<s>śākhās</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 30 atrāṅgirasānuktiratharvānupraveśavivakṣayā /
evaṃ trivedīvyapadeśepi vivakṣābhedo grāhyaḥ /
sarvopyasau punarmantrārthavādādirūpeṇa trividhaḥ /
tatra prāmāṇikamantravyavahāraviṣayo mantraḥ /
sa cānuṣṭheyārthaprakāśanādinopakāroti /
na cedameva tallakṣaṇam, "vasantāya" ityevamādyavyāpteḥ /
"vasantāya kapiñjalānālabhante" ityādayastu mantrā api vidhiparā eva mīmāṃsitāḥ /
sakila mantraḥ kriyamāṇānuvādistotraśastrajapyādibhedabhinnaḥ /
paiśācamāgadhāditattadbhāṣāmantrāṇāṃ phalapradatve tattadbījajātyādikaṃ nidānam /
śraddheyadevatānāmāṅkamātraṃ tu na tadakṣaraśaktipratibandhakam; kṣiprakṣudraphalaprakāśanena vipralambhārthaṃ tathaiveśvarādibhiḥ sṛṣṭam /
garuḍādināmāṅkabhāṣāmantreṣu tu tattaddevatāsmṛtyupakārakatvamapyasti /
etena mantravyākaraṇaṃ nirvyūḍham /
ye tu saptakoṭayo mahāmantrāḥ ityāptaśāstrapratiṣṭhitāḥ, te tu praṇavayogāyogādibhirvaidikāḥ tāntrikāḥ iti vibhajyante /
tatra śūdrādhikāratvasidhyarthaṃ tāntrikaparibhāṣā; na punaravaidikatayā, śrautasmārtādibhedavyapadeśavat pramāṇasiddhatvāviśeṣāt /
sarveṣāṃ ca mantrāṇāṃ sadvārakamadvārakaṃ ca paramātmaiva pratipādyaḥ phalapradaśca /
children.translated_text: And for all <s>mantras</s>, <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self) alone is the one to be conveyed and the bestower of results, whether mediately or immediately.
In the case of those that operate mediately, the culmination is in <s>Brahman</s> in various ways due to the differences in ritual application (<s>viniyoga</s>).
Because [each deity] is the body of the respective god, and because [each] abides as a part of that [Supreme],
by the principle established in the <s>Aindra</s> and similar [<s>adhikaraṇas</s>], all of these have their abode in <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 30. Here, the non-mention of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s> is with the intention of their inclusion within the <s>Atharva</s>. Similarly, even in the designation 'triple <s>Veda</s>' (<s>trivedī</s>), a difference in intention is to be understood. All of this [Vedic corpus] is also threefold in the form of <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages), and the like. Among these, a <s>mantra</s> is that which is the subject of authoritative usage as <s>mantra</s>. And it serves by illuminating the meaning of what is to be performed, and so forth. But this alone is not its definition, because it would fail to apply to passages such as "for <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring)" and the like. Passages such as "they offer <s>kapiñjala</s> birds for <s>Vasanta</s>" — even though they are <s>mantras</s> — have been determined [by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>] to be injunction-oriented. For indeed, a <s>mantra</s> is divided into the sub-types of <s>anuvādi</s> (reiterative), <s>stotra</s> (hymn of praise), <s>śastra</s> (recitation), <s>japya</s> (to be muttered), and others, according to the action being performed. As for the efficacy of <s>mantras</s> in <s>Paiśāca</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and other such languages, the cause is their respective seed-syllables (<s>bīja</s>), class, and the like. The mere stamp of the name of a trustworthy deity does not obstruct the power of those syllables; rather, such [mantras in other languages] were created by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and others precisely for the purpose of deception, through the display of quick and trivial results. But in the case of <s>mantras</s> in regional languages bearing the names of <s>Garuḍa</s> and other deities, there is also the function of aiding the recollection of the respective deities. By this, the grammar of <s>mantras</s> has been dealt with. Now, those seventy million great <s>mantras</s> (<s>saptakoṭi mahāmantrāḥ</s>) that are established in authoritative scriptures — they are classified as Vedic (<s>vaidika</s>) or Tantric (<s>tāntrika</s>) based on whether they incorporate the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) or not, and so forth. There, the designation 'Tantric' is for the purpose of establishing the eligibility of <s>Śūdras</s>; it does not imply non-Vedic status, just as the designations 'Śrauta' (pertaining to Śruti) and 'Smārta' (pertaining to Smṛti) do not imply a difference in validity as <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 31 vidhyadhīnapravṛttyuttambhakavākyaviśeṣo hyarthavādaḥ /
so 'pi pratyakṣādyaviruddhe svārthe pramāṇam, svataḥ prāmāṇyasyānapāyāt /
yatra virodhadhīḥ, tatrāpyaviruddhārthopacāreṇa tatprāmāṇyam /
sa ca kvācid vidhyekavākyatayā pramāṇībhavatītyarthavādādhikaraṇādiṣu sthāpitam /
svataḥ prayojanabhūtārthaviśeṣaviṣayastu svatantratayāpi prāmāṇyaṃ prāpnotīti samanvayasūtrasiddham /
tatprāptyabhilāṣe tu tadupāyavākyapravṛttiḥ /
sa caturdhā---nindāpraśaṃsāparakṛtipurākalpabhedāt /

children.translated_text: <s>Nindā</s> (censure) here is the statement of the fault of what is prohibited and so forth, which serves as ancillary to a prohibition.
<s>Praśaṃsā</s> (praise) is the statement of the merit of what is enjoined and so forth, which serves as ancillary to an injunction.
<s>Parakṛti</s> (precedent of another) is a particular narrative connected to a single [injunction].
While <s>purākalpa</s> (ancient practice) is connected to multiple [injunctions].

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 31. An <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) is indeed a particular type of sentence that bolsters the activity that is dependent on an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>). It too is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding its own meaning when not contradicted by perception and other [means of knowledge], since its self-validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) remains undiminished. Where there is apprehension of contradiction, even there its validity holds through figurative interpretation (<s>upacāra</s>) of a non-contradictory meaning. And in some cases it becomes a valid means of knowledge by being construed as a single sentence with an injunction — this has been established in the <s>Arthavāda-adhikaraṇa</s> and similar [discussions in the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>]. But when it pertains to a specific object that is inherently purposeful, it attains validity even independently — this is established in the <s>Samanvaya Sūtra</s>. And when there is a desire for attaining that [purpose], there is engagement with the sentence that teaches its means. It is fourfold — due to the divisions of <s>nindā</s> (censure), <s>praśaṃsā</s> (praise), <s>parakṛti</s> (precedent of another), and <s>purākalpa</s> (ancient practice).

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 32 hitānuśāsanarūpaṃ vākyamiha vidhiḥ /

children.translated_text: And it is of many kinds — due to the divisions of <s>nitya</s> (obligatory), <s>naimittika</s> (occasional), <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated), combined injunctions, prohibitions, and the like.
<s>Niyama</s> (restrictive rule) and <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (exclusive enumeration) are also sub-types of injunction.

children.text: tatraivaṃ vivekaḥ--- aprāptasya vidhau prāptirniyame prāptapūraṇam /
children.translated_text: The distinction among these is as follows: in the case of <s>vidhi</s> (injunction proper), there is the obtaining of what was not [previously] obtained; in the case of <s>niyama</s> (restrictive rule), there is the specification of what was [already] obtained;
while in <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (exclusive enumeration), there is the exclusion of what was obtained, but only partially.
<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 32. Here, <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) is a sentence in the form of a beneficial instruction (<s>hitānuśāsana</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 33 athātra ko nāma liṅādipratyayārthaḥ ? na tāvadapūrvam, tasmin pramāṇāntarāgocare vyutpattyayogāt, tadgocaratve tu apūrvatvavyāghātāt, liṅādibodhite vyutpattāvitaretarāśrayaprasaṅgāt /
vimarśataḥ siddhiḥ syāditi cenna, vimarśasya smṛtyanubhavātiriktasyānamyupagamāt, kriyākāryevyutpannasya cānvayāyogyatāyāmapi lakṣaṇādibhireva nirbāhyatvāt, abhidhānānyathākaraṇāyogāt, prathamavyutpatterapi sarvatra kārya eveti niyamābhāvāt /

tathā---gāmānayetyādiprayojakavṛddhavākyaśravaṇasamanantaraṃ gavānayane pravṛttaṃ puruṣamālokya pārśvastho vyutpitsuścetanapravṛtteḥ kāryatābuddhipūrvakatvāt prayojyavṛddhakāryatābuddheśca kāraṇāntarādarśanāt yadanantaraṃ yat dṛśyate tattasya kāraṇamiti prayojakavṛddhavākyameva prayojyavṛddhakāryatābuddheḥ kāraṇamityadhyavasyati /
children.translated_text: Thus — immediately upon hearing the sentence of the prompting elder (<s>prayojakavṛddha</s>), such as 'bring the cow,' the person who wishes to learn (<s>vyutpitsu</s>), standing nearby, observes another person engaging in the act of bringing the cow; since the activity of a conscious being is preceded by the cognition of duty-to-be-done (<s>kāryatābuddhi</s>), and since no other cause is seen for the cognition of duty in the prompted elder (<s>prayojyavṛddha</s>), he ascertains — by the principle that 'whatever is seen immediately after something is the cause of it' — that the sentence of the prompting elder alone is the cause of the cognition of duty in the prompted elder.

children.text: tathā kasyacit 'putraste jātaḥ' iti kenacidukte pratipannaputrotpattestasya priyatvaṃ ca jñāyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, when someone tells a certain person 'a son has been born to you,' the birth of the son is understood and its being pleasing to him is also known.

children.text: vyutpitsuḥ putrajanmavākyaśrāviṇaḥ puruṣasya mukhavikāsamālokya tasya priyārthapratiprattinimittatvānumānāt tatpratīteśca kāraṇāntarādarśanāt putrajanamavākyameva kāraṇaṃ kalpayati /
children.translated_text: The person wishing to learn, upon observing the brightening of the face of the man who has heard the sentence about the son's birth, infers — from the reasoning that such [facial expression] is caused by the apprehension of a pleasing object — and seeing no other cause for that cognition, posits that the sentence about the son's birth alone is the cause.

children.text: na ca putrajanmanaḥ priyatvaṃ bālenājñātamiti vācyam, prajñātaputrajanmanastasya prauḍhasya bhāṣāntaravat prathamavyutpattāvevaṃ saṃbhavāt, nodāharaṇamādaraṇīyamiti ca nyāyavidaḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor should it be objected that the child does not know that birth of a son is pleasing, because for one who already knows about the birth of a son and is mature, such an initial comprehension is possible — just as with a different language; and the knowers of logic [say that] one should not disregard an illustration [merely because it is not universally applicable].

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 33. Now, what is the meaning of the <s>liṅ</s> (optative) and other [injunctive] suffixes here? It is not <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented transcendent potency), because — if it is beyond the reach of other means of knowledge — there can be no linguistic comprehension (<s>vyutpatti</s>) of it; if it were within the reach [of other means], this would contradict its being <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented); and if comprehension were to arise only from what is conveyed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix itself, there would be the fallacy of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). Nor can one say that knowledge would arise from reflective deliberation (<s>vimarśa</s>), because <s>vimarśa</s>, being nothing beyond memory and experience, is not accepted [as an independent source]; because one who has already comprehended the meaning as referring to an action-to-be-done (<s>kriyākārya</s>) — even when there is incapacity for direct application — can resolve it through secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) and similar means alone; because it is impossible to make the denotative function (<s>abhidhāna</s>) operate otherwise [than what the word naturally means]; and because there is no rule that the initial comprehension must always be in terms of duty (<s>kārya</s>) alone in all cases.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 34 tataśca ye bālānāṃ priyatvena saṃpratipannā bhakṣyabhojyādayaḥ, taddarśī vyutpitsustatsaṃpattiśrāviṇaḥ puruṣasya mukhavikāsadarśanādiprakriyayā vyutpadyata iti kiṃ nopapadyate ? priyāntarasmṛtyādibhirapi mukhe vikāsaḥ saṃbhavatīti cet, tathaiva svayaṃ tadadhīnaprayojanāntarasmaraṇādināpi gavānayanakartavyatābodhaḥ saṃbhavet /
āsatti viśeṣavaśādanekaprayogānugateśca vyavastheti cet, tulyam /

tathāpi tattatpriyānubandhisulagnajanmasukhaprasavasvāduvāktvādiharṣahetvarthāntarasaṃbhāvanayā viśeṣo durniścayaḥ iti cenna, gavānayanepi vatsasaṃyojanakṣīrasaṃpādanādikartavyatābodhakepi vākye tadarthagavānayanasaṃbhavād gāmānametyādivākyaṃ gavānayanakartavyataikabodhakamiti kathaṃ niścinuyāt ? anvayavyatirekamahimavaśād dṛṣṭānugrahācceti cet, tulyam /
children.translated_text: Even so, if it be said that the specific determination is difficult because of the possibility of alternative causes of delight — such as the joy naturally associated with those pleasant things, the happiness arising at birth, the delight of tasting sweetness, eloquence, and so forth — [we reply:] no, because even in the case of bringing the cow, when the sentence could convey the duty of joining the calf, procuring milk, and so on, how would one ascertain that the sentence 'bring the cow' conveys solely the duty of bringing the cow? If it be said that this is through the force of the method of agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) and through the assistance of observed [usage] — the same [reply] applies equally.

children.text: tadevaṃ putrajanmavākyodāharaṇasamīkārasya mandamatīnāṃ durārohatvāt tadupekṣaṇena spaṣṭataravyutpattiprakāro yādṛcchiko buddhipūrvaśca bhāṣyakārairdarśitaḥ; tadatra likhyate--- "evaṃ kila bālāḥ śabdārthasaṃbandhamavadhārayanti; mātāpitṛprabhṛtibhirambātātamātulādīn śaśipaśunaramṛgapakṣisarīsṛpādīṃśca enamavehi, imaṃ cāvadhāraya, ityabhiprāyeṇāṅgulyā nirdiśya nirdiśya taistaiḥ śabdaisteṣu teṣu bahuśaḥ śikṣitāḥ śanaiḥ śanaistaireva śabdaisteṣu teṣvartheṣu svātmanāṃ budhdyutpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhāntarādarśanāt saṅketayitṛpuruṣājñānācca teṣvartheṣu teṣāṃ śabdānāṃ prayogo bodhakatvanibandhana iti niścinvanti /
children.translated_text: Since the illustration of the sentence about the son's birth is thus too difficult for the dull-witted to follow, setting it aside, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Rāmānuja</s>) has shown a clearer mode of comprehension, both spontaneous and intentional. That is written here: "Children learn the relation between word and meaning in the following way: parents and others, pointing with a finger again and again to mothers, fathers, maternal uncles, and to the moon, animals, men, deer, birds, reptiles, and the like, and saying with the intent 'know this one' and 'recognize this one,' instruct them repeatedly with those respective words regarding those respective [objects]. [The children,] gradually observing for themselves the arising of cognition (<s>buddhyutpatti</s>) of those respective meanings through those very words, and seeing no other relation between word and meaning, and being unaware of any person who established the convention, conclude that the usage of those words for those meanings is grounded in [the words'] capacity to convey meaning (<s>bodhakatva</s>).

children.text: punaśca vyutpannetaraśabdeṣvasya śabdasyāyamartha iti pūrvavṛddhaiḥ śikṣitāḥ sarvaśabdānāmarthamavagamya parapratyāyanāya tattadarthāvabodhi vākyajātaṃ prayuñjate /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having been instructed by elders — 'this word has this meaning' — with respect to words for which they had not yet gained comprehension, they apprehend the meaning of all words and employ sentence-groups that convey those respective meanings for the purpose of communicating to others.

children.text: prakārāntareṇāpi śabdārthasaṃbandhāvadhāraṇaṃ suśakam---kenacit puruṣeṇa hastaceṣṭādinā 'pitā te sukhamāste, iti devadattāya jñāpaya'" iti preṣitaḥ kaścit tajjñāpane pravaṛttaḥ 'pitā te sukhamāste' iti śabdaṃ prayuṅkte; pārśvasthonyo vyutpitsurmūkavacceṣṭāviśeṣajñaḥ tajjñāpane pravṛttamimaṃ jñātvānugataḥ tajjñāpanāya prayuktamimaṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā, ayaṃ śabdastadarthabuddhiheturiti niścinotīti kāryārtha eva vyutpattiriti nirbandho nirnibandhanaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: The ascertainment of the relation between word and meaning is also easily accomplished in another way: a certain person is dispatched by another person — through gestures and the like — [with the instruction] 'inform <s>Devadatta</s> that your father is well.' That person, having set out to convey this, utters the words 'your father is well.' Another person standing nearby, who wishes to learn, who understands gestural communication as a mute person would, having realized that this person has set out to convey that [message], and having heard this utterance employed for conveying that [message], concludes: 'this utterance is the cause of the cognition of that meaning.' Therefore, the insistence that initial comprehension must be in terms of <s>kārya</s> (duty/action) alone is without foundation." Thus.

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 34. Thus, foodstuffs and eatables that are recognized by children as pleasant — when the person wishing to learn sees [such items] and observes the brightening of the face of a person who hears of their arrival, through this very procedure he learns [the word-meaning relation]; what is not possible in this? If it be objected that the brightening of the face could also be due to the recollection of some other pleasant thing — then by the same token, the understanding of the duty to bring the cow could also arise from the recollection of some other purpose dependent upon it. If it be said that the determination is through the force of contextual proximity (<s>āsatti</s>) and through consistency observed across multiple usages — the same [reply] applies equally [to our example].

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa 35 atra pitā te sukhamāsta iti vākyasya sthāne apavarake daṇḍaḥ sthitaḥ ityudāharaṇāntaramātramanyatroktam /
ataḥ siddhāsiddhepyādyavyutpattiḥ /
bhavatu vā prathamavyutpattiḥ kārya eva, tathāpi prayogānvayavyatirekavaśādeva śabdaśaktirvivecanīyā /
prayujyante ca siddhaparā evāvivakṣitakartavyaiḥ śabdāḥ; yathā--- kosau rājā ? kauravaḥ /
kautukamātrādeva hyatra praśnaḥ, prativacanaṃ ca tadanuvidhāyyeva /
ato yathā padānāṃ prātisvikī śaktiḥ siddhe kāryepīti yathāsaṃbhavaṃ niṣkṛṣyate, tathā tātparyamapi, yathāyogameva vyutpattyupāyatvepi ca kāryasya sarvaśabdatātparyaviṣayatvāyukteḥ /
kāryavākyepi pravartakatvādilakṣaṇaṃ ca prādhānyamapūrvasya mṛgyam, sukhaduḥkhābhāvābhyāmatiriktasya svataḥ svasmin pravartakatvāyogāt, vyutpattidaśāyāmapyasukharūpasyānayanāderanyaśeṣatayaiva pravṛttiśeṣatvāvagamāt /
ataḥ sukhe duḥkhanivṛttau vā sākṣāt kāryatvabodhaḥ; tadarthatayā tatsādhane /

children.translated_text: And because [the means] is desired, the cognition of duty-to-be-done applies also to the means of the means, just as to the means [itself].

children.text: na ca sukhāditvamapūrvasya; na ca tatsādhanatayā tatpravartakatvamabhyupagatam /
children.translated_text: And <s>apūrva</s> is not of the nature of pleasure and the like; nor is its capacity to motivate accepted as being due to its being the means of that [pleasure].

children.text: abhyupagamepi laukikasevyaprītyeva devatāprītyaiva śrutyādisiddhayā kālāntarabhāviphalasiddhauliṅvācyatayā svarūpeṇa vā tatkalpanāyogāt, rātrisatrādinayācca /
children.translated_text: Even if it were accepted [as the means], since the accomplishment of a result occurring at a later time — established only through the <s>Śruti</s> and other [authoritative sources] — depends on the very delight served in worldly experience, and specifically on the delight of the deity (<s>devatāprīti</s>), there would be no justification for postulating that [<s>apūrva</s>] either as expressed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix or in its own nature; and this is also [supported] by the principle of the <s>Rātrisatra</s> and similar [cases].

children.text: pratiṣṭhādeśaviśeṣaśatayātanāsādhanatvaghṛtāñjanacchāgādiparigrahavat vidhyapekṣitaṃ pratītaṃ ca devatāprītyātmakamevāpūrvaṃ liṅvācyatayā svarūpeṇa vā dvāramupakalpyatām; kimanyena ? //
children.translated_text: Let <s>apūrva</s>, in the form of the delight of the deity — which is required by the injunction, and which is known [through scripture], just as are the foundation, special location, the hundredfold spreading of the sacrificial enclosure, and the use of ghee, ointment, and goats — be posited as the gateway, either as expressed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix or in its own nature. What need is there for anything else?

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 35. Here, in place of the sentence 'your father is well,' an alternative illustration mentioned elsewhere is 'a staff is standing in the inner chamber.' Therefore, the initial comprehension [of word-meaning] is possible whether [the sentence denotes] something established or not yet established. Or even if the initial comprehension were indeed in terms of <s>kārya</s> (duty/action), still the power (<s>śakti</s>) of words is to be discerned through the method of agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) in actual usage. And words are indeed used with the intention of [denoting] established [facts] by those who do not intend [to convey] a duty-to-be-done; for example: 'Who is that king? A <s>Kaurava</s>.' For here the question arises from mere curiosity, and the answer simply follows accordingly. Therefore, just as the intrinsic power of words is extracted as applicable to both established and duty-related [meanings] according to possibility, so too is the <s>tātparya</s> (purport) [determined] only as appropriate; and even though <s>kārya</s> (duty) may serve as a means of comprehension, it is unjustified [to claim] that it is the purport-object of all words. Even in a sentence conveying duty, the primacy of <s>apūrva</s> (transcendent potency) — characterized by its capacity to motivate — must be sought; for something that is beyond [both] pleasure and the absence of pain cannot by itself motivate one toward itself; and even at the stage of initial comprehension, the duty of bringing and the like, being unpleasant, is understood as being only in the service of something else. Therefore, the cognition of duty-to-be-done pertains directly to pleasure or to the cessation of suffering; and through purposive relation, to the means of attaining that.

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 36 yacca jalpantyardhalokāyatikāḥ--- "vigraho havirādānaṃ yugapat karmasannidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, section 36. And as for what the half-materialists (<s>ardhalokāyatikas</s>) declare: "Embodied form, reception of offerings, simultaneous presence at [multiple] rituals,

children.text: prītiḥ phalapradānaṃ ca devatānāṃ na vidyate" //
children.translated_text: delight, and the bestowal of results — these do not belong to the deities."

children.text:
iti, tadapi jaiminihṛdayānabhijñatānibandhanam; na hi svataḥ pramāṇāmnāyasmṛtipurāṇādisiddhāḥ sādhakabādhakapramāṇāgocarāḥ devatāvigrahādayo hātuṃ yuktāḥ /
na cāyogyeṣvanupalambhamātreṇa bādhaḥ śaṅakyaḥ, atiprasaṅgitvāt, sākṣāllokāyatikavādaprasaṅgāt /
stutyā vidhiśeṣabhūteṣvapyarthavādeṣu tadarthatayaiva svārthamabhidadhāneṣu na vākyabhedādidoṣaḥ /
stutyādiparatvepi na mukhyārthabādhaḥ, svārthabādhakābhāvo svārthaprahāṇāyogāt; na ca sarvā stutirayathārthā; na cāsatā guṇena kathitena stutisiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if [the passages] are oriented toward praise and so forth, there is no sublation of the primary meaning (<s>mukhyārtha</s>), because the absence of anything that would sublate their own meaning makes the abandonment of their own meaning unjustified; and not all praise is non-veridical; nor does praise succeed through a quality that is stated but unreal.

children.text: yatra tu mukhyārthabādhaḥ, tatrāpyaipacārikaṃ kiñcidālambanamabhipretam; anyathā viḍambanamātrameva syāt /
children.translated_text: But where there is sublation of the primary meaning, even there some figurative basis (<s>ālambana</s>) is intended; otherwise it would be mere mockery.

children.text: na copacchandanamātratā, tajjñāne puṃsaḥ pravṛttyanupakārāt, nirūpakasya ca tadajñānāyogāt, anyathā bhrāntimūlapravṛttitvaprasaṅgāt; samanvayādhikaraṇanayācca siddhaikaparāḥ santi bhāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is it mere flattery, because if [the praised quality] were known [to be false], it would not serve to motivate a person toward action; and it is impossible for the evaluator to be ignorant of it; otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence of action grounded in delusion. And by the approach of the <s>Samanvaya-adhikaraṇa</s>, there are [indeed] portions that are oriented toward established [realities].
