And following upon those [Vedic texts] are the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like.

This too is grounded in ignorance of <s>Jaimini's</s> intent; for it is not proper to reject the embodied forms and such attributes of deities that are established by the inherently valid Vedic revelation (<s>āmnāya</s>), <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like, and that are beyond the reach of [any] proving or disproving means of knowledge. Nor can an objection be raised merely from non-apprehension among those unqualified [to perceive them], as that would lead to overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>), and would directly entail the position of the full materialists (<s>Lokāyatikas</s>). Even in <s>arthavāda</s> passages that are ancillary to injunctions through praise (<s>stuti</s>), since they convey their own meaning precisely for that purpose [of praise], there is no fault of splitting the sentence (<s>vākyabheda</s>) and the like.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 37 nanvarthavādādhikaraṇe "vidhinā tvekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ" iti sarveṣāmarthavādānāṃ vidhyekavākyatvamuktam; samanvayasūtre tu kathaṃ tadviruddhoktiḥ ? maivam; arthavādāprāmāṇyapūrvapakṣapratikṣepāya vidhyekavākyatayā prāmāṇyaṃ saṃbhavatītyetāvanmātramarthavādādhikaraṇe sthāpitam /
vidhyekavākyatve brahmasvarūpatātparyābhāvapūrvapakṣastu apavarakanidhisadbhāvādivākyavat svataḥprayojanabhūtārthaviṣayavākyānāṃ bhinnavākyatayāpi prāmāṇyamupapādya samanvayasūtre pratikṣipyata iti virodhābhāvāt /
api cautsargiṅkamāpavādikañca taṃ tamarthaṃ pratipādayatsu vākyeṣu viṣayavyavasthayā virodhaśamanaṃ vyākaraṇādiṣvapi dṛṣṭamiti /
ata eva brāhmaṇaśeṣā arthavādā ityārṣamapi vākyamautsargikaviṣayamavagantavyam /
yā tu śabdabhāvanaiva liṅādyartha iti kaumārilakusṛtiḥ, sā tu pratītiviṃsavādādipratihatā; na hi vidhivākyaśrāvī puruṣaḥ, liṅādi svavyāpāramabhidhatte, ato mayā pravartitavyamiti manyate /
na ca yāgādisvarūpe liṅādivyāpāre ca kenacid vākyena samuccitya pratipāditepi kaścit pravartamāno dṛśyate /
liṅādeśca jñāyamānatvalakṣaṇavyāpāramātrācchaktilakṣaṇavyāpārādvā pravartakatve vyutpatteḥ prāgapi tataḥ pravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ; vyutpatterapi sahakāritve tatsāpekṣāyā nirviṣayāyāstasyā asaṃbhavāt tadviṣayo vācyaḥ /
na ca svavyāpāre liṅādiḥ kvacid vyutpannaḥ /
sarveṣāmapi śabdānāṃ svavyāpārātirikta eva hyarthe vyutpatti /
ye cābhidhādayaḥ śabdāḥ, tepi na śṛṅgagrāhikayā svavyāpāramabhidadhati; api tu śabdamātravyāpāre tatpravṛtteḥ sāmānyopādhikroḍīkāreṇa svavyāpārasyāpi niveśaḥ; ata evābhidhādiśabdābhidheyasya nimittasya ca sāmānyataḥ pratipannatvād vyutpattyupapattiḥ /
liṅādestu svavyāpāre pratīte tatra vyutpattiḥ syāt; tatpratītirvyutpannena cet, anyonyāśrayaḥ; avyutpannena cet, atiprasaṅgaḥ, iti /
na ceṣṭasādhanatvamātraṃ liṅādibodhyam, 'taveṣṭa sādhanamidam, ateḥ kuru' iti sahaprayogadarśanāt /
na cādarādinibandhanā punaruktiriyam, pratīteratathātvāt, hetusādhyanirdeśāyogācca /
'kartavyamidam, ataḥ kuru ityapi dṛśyate, iti cenna, brāhmaṇasya kartavyamidam, atastavāpi kartavyamitivat sāmanyaviśeṣādivivakṣāyā avirodhāt, atyantaikārthavivakṣāyāṃ tu tatrāpi prayogāyogāt /
ata eva āptasya vakturicchāmātraṃ liṅādyarthaḥ, iti pratyuktam; āptasyeṣṭamidam, atā mamedaṃ kāryam iti pravartamānapuruṣābhilāpaviśeṣadarśanāt /
na ca liṅārthatvādeva nimantraṇādivad vidhirapi vaktrabhiprāyamātramiti vācyam, saṃbhāvanādibhirviśeṣavihitaiścānaikāntyāt; ekaśabdavācyatāmātreṇaikatve cānekārthaśabdabhaṅgaprasaṅge dṛṣṭāntopi na sidhyet /
yadyapi paramate hyudayanoktā niṣedhānupapattiḥ, tathāpi na sāsmatpakṣamavagāhate, kartavyatāyā vidhyarthatve na kartavya iti nañanvayāvirodhāt; kartṛvyāpārasādhyatvameva ca kartavyatvam; tathāhi vedārthasaṅgahe "liṅādeḥ koyamarthaḥ parigṛhītaḥ"' iti praśnapūrvakaṃ pratyuktam--- "yaja devapūjāyām, iti devatārādhanabhūtayāgādeḥ prakṛtyarthasya kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāṃ vyutpattisiddhāṃ liṅādayobhidadhatīti na kiñcidanupapannam, kartṛvācināṃ pratyayānāṃ prakṛtyarthasya kartṛvyāpārasaṃbandhaprakāro hi vācyaḥ; bhūtavartamānatādimanye vadanti, liṅādayastu kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāṃ vadanti" iti /
bhāṣye cādyasūtre---"ato vidhivākyeṣvapi dhātvarthasya kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāmātraṃ śabdānuśāsanasiddhameva liṅādervācyamityadhyavasīyate, dhātvarthasya ca yāgāderagnyādidevatāntaryāmiparamapuruṣasamārādhanarūpatā, samārādhitāt paramapuruṣāt phalasiddhiśceti 'phalamata upapatteḥ' iti pratipādayiṣyate" iti /
atra kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāmātramiti niṣkṛṣṭārthapradarśanāyoktam; pratipattiprakārastu yajetetyādau svavyāpārasādhyayāgādiviśiṣṭaḥ iti kartṛprādhānyenaiva /
yathoktaṃ dīpe kartradhikaraṇai--- "yajeta, upāsīta, iti hi kartari lakāraḥ, ataḥ kartārameva bodhayati śāstram" iti /
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Dīpā</s> (sub-commentary) in the <s>kartṛ</s>-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the agent): "'<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice), '<s>upāsīta</s>' (one should meditate) — for the <s>lakāra</s> (verbal suffix) is in the agent [voice], therefore the scripture instructs the agent alone."

children.text: uktaṃ ca vedārthasaṃgrahepi-- "svargakāmo yajeta, ityevamādiṣu lakāravācyakartṛviśeṣasamarpakāṇāṃ svargakāmādipadānāṃ niyojyaviśeṣasamarpakatvaṃ śabdānuśāsanāviruddham" iti /
children.translated_text: And it has been stated in the <s>Vedārthasaṅgraha</s> as well: "In sentences like '<s>svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one who desires heaven should sacrifice), it is not inconsistent with grammatical science that words like '<s>svargakāma</s>' (desirer of heaven) and the like, which specify the particular agent denoted by the <s>lakāra</s> (verbal suffix), function as specifiers of the particular person who is enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>)."

children.text: yadyapi dīpagranthaḥ puṃsaḥ kartṛtvaṃ śrutisiddhamityatraiva tatparaḥ, tathāpi dhātvarthasādhyatāparaliṅādiṣvapi kartapradhānatayā vṛttiṃ pradarśya sāṃravyān pratikṣipatīti tādarthyāt tatrāpi tatparatvameva grāhyam /
children.translated_text: Although the <s>Dīpā</s> text is primarily concerned with establishing that the agency of the person is scripturally established, nevertheless, by demonstrating that even in the <s>liṅ</s> suffixes and the like — whose other [function] is to express the accomplishability of the verbal root's meaning — the usage is with the primacy of the agent, it refutes <s>Sāṃravya</s>'s [view]; therefore, because of that purposive connection, the text should be understood as having that very purport there as well.

children.text: pacatītyādau pākaṃ karotītyādinipuṇavyākriyāśca kṛtikarmatayaiva dhātvarthasyānvayaṃ vyañjayanti //
children.translated_text: And the precise grammatical analyses of forms like "<s>pacati</s>" (he cooks) as "<s>pākaṃ karoti</s>" (he performs cooking) reveal that the verbal root's meaning has its syntactic connection precisely as the object of the action (<s>kṛtikarma</s>).

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 37. Now, in the <s>arthavāda</s>-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic on laudatory passages), it has been stated that "but because of forming a single sentence with the injunction, the laudatory passages serve the purpose of praising the injunctions" — thus the single-sentence unity (<s>ekavākyatva</s>) of all <s>arthavādas</s> with <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) has been declared; but in the <s>samanvayasūtra</s> (the sūtra on coherent interpretation), how can there be a statement contradicting that? It should not be so understood; in the <s>arthavāda</s>-<s>adhikaraṇa</s>, only this much was established — that validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is possible for <s>arthavādas</s> through their single-sentence unity with <s>vidhi</s>, in order to reject the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) that <s>arthavādas</s> lack validity.
The prima facie view that single-sentence unity with <s>vidhi</s> precludes the purport being about the nature of <s>Brahman</s> is refuted in the <s>samanvayasūtra</s> by demonstrating that sentences whose subject matter is inherently purposeful — like sentences about the existence of hidden treasures in caves and the like — possess validity even as independent sentences; hence there is no contradiction.
Moreover, when statements teach a particular meaning in both a general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) and an exception (<s>apavāda</s>), the resolution of contradiction through domain-distinction (<s>viṣayavyavasthā</s>) is observed even in grammar and other disciplines.
For this very reason, the ancient statement that "<s>arthavādas</s> are supplements to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>" should be understood as pertaining to the general-rule domain.
As for the Kumārila sophistry that <s>śabdabhāvanā</s> (the verbal prompting power) itself is the meaning of <s>liṅ</s> (the optative suffix) and so forth — that has been refuted by the argument from the discrepancy with actual cognition (<s>pratītivimśavāda</s>) and other arguments; for a person hearing an injunctive sentence does not think that the <s>liṅ</s> suffix expresses its own operation, and therefore "I must act."
Nor is anyone seen to engage in action even when a sentence has presented, by combining together, both the essential nature of sacrifice and the like and the operation of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix.
Moreover, if the <s>liṅ</s> suffix's capacity to prompt action arose merely from its operation characterized as being-cognized, or from its operation characterized as potency (<s>śakti</s>), then there would be the unwanted consequence of engagement even before linguistic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>); and if linguistic competence too is a cooperating factor, then since that competence, being dependent on it, would be objectless and thus impossible, its object must be specified.
And the <s>liṅ</s> suffix has never been understood through linguistic competence as referring to its own operation.
For all words whatsoever, linguistic competence pertains to a meaning other than their own operation.
And words like <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and the like also do not denote their own operation by directly grasping it; rather, since their usage pertains to word-operation in general, their own operation is included through the incorporation of the general qualifier; for this very reason, since what is denoted by words like <s>abhidhā</s> and the occasioning cause are understood only in a general way, the possibility of linguistic competence is explained.
But for the <s>liṅ</s> suffix, if its own operation were cognized, then linguistic competence would pertain to that; if that cognition requires one already linguistically competent, there is mutual dependence; if it does not require competence, there is over-extension.
Nor is it the case that the <s>liṅ</s> suffix conveys merely "being a means to what is desired," because we observe concurrent usage such as "this is a means to what you desire, therefore do it."
Nor is this a redundancy based on emphasis and the like, because the cognition is not of that nature, and because the designation of cause and effect would be inappropriate.
If one objects that "this is to be done, therefore do it" is also observed — that is not so, because just as "this is to be done by a Brāhmaṇa, therefore it is to be done by you too" involves no contradiction due to the intention of expressing the general and the particular, so too here; whereas if absolutely identical meaning were intended, the usage would be inappropriate there as well.
For this very reason, the view that the meaning of <s>liṅ</s> and the like is merely the wish of a trustworthy speaker (<s>āpta</s>) has been answered — because we observe the specific utterance of a person who acts thus: "this is desired by the trustworthy authority, therefore this is my duty."
Nor should one say that, just because it is a meaning of <s>liṅ</s>, <s>vidhi</s> too is merely the speaker's intention, like invitation (<s>nimantraṇa</s>) and the like — because there is non-conclusiveness due to supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanā</s>) and other specifically prescribed usages; and if identity were established merely from being expressible by one and the same word, then the absurd consequence of breaking apart all polysemous words would arise, and even the illustrative example would not be established.
Although in the opponent's system the objection regarding the impossibility of prohibition raised by <s>Udayana</s> [would apply], nevertheless it does not affect our position, because when <s>kartavyatā</s> (obligation) is the meaning of <s>vidhi</s>, there is no contradiction in the negation particle combining as "not to be done" (<s>na kartavya</s>); and <s>kartavyatva</s> (obligation) is precisely <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatva</s> (being accomplishable through the agent's effort). Thus indeed, in the <s>Vedārthasaṅgraha</s>, after the question "What meaning of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix has been accepted?" the answer was given: "In '<s>yaja</s>' meaning worship of gods, the <s>liṅ</s> suffixes and the like express the <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatā</s> — the accomplishability through the agent's effort — of the verbal root's meaning, namely sacrifice and the like, which is worship of the deity; this is established through linguistic competence, so nothing is unexplained. For suffixes that denote the agent, the mode of relation of the verbal root's meaning to the agent's effort is what is to be expressed; others say [these suffixes express] past, present tense and so on, but the <s>liṅ</s> suffixes express <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatā</s>."
And in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) on the first <s>sūtra</s>: "Therefore, even in injunctive sentences, it is ascertained that what the <s>liṅ</s> suffix expresses is merely the <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatā</s> of the verbal root's meaning — this is established by grammatical science itself. And the nature of the verbal root's meaning, namely sacrifice and the like, as worship of the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>) who is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, and the attainment of results from that worshipped Supreme Person — this will be taught in the sūtra '<s>phalamata upapatteḥ</s>' (the result [comes] from Him, since it is logically consistent)."
Here, the word "merely" in "merely <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatā</s>" is stated to indicate the precisely extracted meaning; but the mode of apprehension in sentences like "<s>yajeta</s>" (one should sacrifice) is qualified by the sacrifice and the like that are accomplishable through one's own effort — thus the primacy is of the agent alone.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 38 śrīgītābhāṣye caitad vyañjitam--- 'yudhyasva' ityatra 'yuddhākhyaṃ karmārabhasva' iti vyākhyānāt /
vyākaraṇāt karaṇatayā ca dhātvarthasyānvaye kathaṃ kriyāviśeṣaṇasya karmavibhaktyantatā ? na hi viśeṣyeṇa viśeṣaṇaṃ bhāvayedityanveti, phalasyāpūrvasya vā bhavadbhirbhāvyatvābhyupagamāt; vartamānavyapadeśādiṣu ca sādhyāntarābhāvepi na viśeṣaṇamātraṃ sādhyam, na ca prathamāntaṃ kiyāviśeṣaṇam; karaṇapakṣepi dhātvarthenānanvayaprasaṅgāt, ananvitaviśeṣaṇatādyanupapatteḥ /
na cākarmavibhaktyantena dhātunā karmavibhaktyantasya kathaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyamiti vācyam, karaṇavibhaktyantenāpyasāmānādhikaraṇyaprasaṅgāt, na ca prapavatīyamāne karmatvenānvaye kaściddoṣo dṛśyate, priyaṅgukāmaḥ kṛṣiṃ kuryāditivat svargakāmo yāgaṃ kuryāditi vākyārthepi virodhābhāvāt, tadvadevārthatastasya tadupāyatvasiddheḥ keneti karaṇākāṅkṣāyā api śamanāt /
nāmadheyagatatṛtīyānvayopi nāvaśyaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyena, tattannāmakaiḥ karmaviśeṣaiḥ devatāpūjāṃ kuryādityevaṃparatvepi svarasānvayāt, sāmānyaviśeṣarūpeṇa vyadhikaraṇanirdeśopapatteḥ /
cāṭuvādena rājānaṃ prīṇayeditivād yāgaṃ kuruṣvetyādau na kṛñarthasyāpi sādhyatvaprasaṅgaḥ, tasyaiva kartṛvyāpārarūpatve tatsādhyatvāyogāt, prakṛtipratyayoranyatarasya kṛtāvudāsīnatvāt, ekaḥ, dvau, bahavaḥ, ityādivat /
tatrāpi yadā karmatāṃ vivakṣati, tadāpi kartṛvyāpārāntaramabhipretya vā, bhedopacāreṇa vā nirvāhaḥ; yathā---udakāharaṇakriyāṃ karotītyādau /
na ca tāvatānavasthā, pratītyanāroheṇa vyavahārasya paryavasitatvāt /
agnihotraṃ juhotītyādiprayogaścāsmatpakṣānukūlaḥ /
ataḥ, kiṃ, kena, kathamiti bhavatproktavat, kimarthaṃ, kiṃ, kena, kathamityākāṅkṣācatuṣṭaye svargādinā kimarthamityākāṅkṣāpūraṇam, devatāṃ prīṇayediti kimityākāṅkṣānaśāntiḥ, jyotiṣṭomenetyādināmadheyādibhiḥ kenetyākāṅkṣā pūryate, kathamityākāṅkṣāpūraṇaṃ tu bhavatāmasmākaṃ ca tulyameveti śābdoyaṃ panthāḥ /
atastattadadhikāriṇaḥ svasādhyadhātvarthaviśiṣṭatābodhini yajetetyādau tattaddhātvarthānuṣṭhāne phalam ananuṣṭhāne pratyavāyaśca sarvapraśāsituḥ saṅkalpād bhavatītyapi vākyādavagatam /
avāntaradevatābuddhivṛttiviśeṣastu sadvārakayajate śrāddhabhojipuruṣaprītyādivadānuṣaṅgikaḥ, anyathā kalpāntarādiṣu pralīnaprācīnadevatāgaṇeṣu pūrvakalpānuṣṭhitakarmaphalānutpattiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: The particular mental disposition directed toward the subordinate deities is merely incidental (<s>ānuṣaṅgika</s>), like the pleasure of the person who feeds Brāhmaṇas at a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) being mediated through the good [deity]; otherwise, when the assemblies of ancient deities have dissolved at the end of a cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>) and in other such periods, there would be the absurd consequence that the fruits of rituals performed in a previous <s>kalpa</s> would never arise.

children.text: ata eva hyekasyaiva śrutirājñā; anyeṣāṃ cārādhakatvavadārādhyatvamapi tadāyattamiti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the scriptural kingship belongs to one alone; and for the others, just as their status as worshippers is dependent on Him, so too their status as objects of worship is dependent on Him.

<s>Nārāyaṇārya</s> (the venerable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, i.e., <s>Nārāyaṇamuni</s>) has stated thus: "Some have declared that [the meaning of <s>vidhi</s> is] the command (<s>niyoga</s>) of a trustworthy authority (<s>āpta</s>) who desires [our] welfare.
The revered <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator, i.e., <s>Rāmānuja</s>) also approved of exactly this."

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 38. And this has been indicated in the <s>Śrī Gītā Bhāṣya</s> — from the explanation of "<s>yudhyasva</s>" (fight!) as "commence the action called battle" (<s>yuddhākhyaṃ karmārabhasva</s>).
From grammar, and also when the verbal root's meaning has its syntactic connection as an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), how can the action-qualifier end in the accusative case (<s>karmavibhakti</s>)? For a qualifier does not connect with its qualificand by the relation "it should bring about" (<s>bhāvayet</s>). Regarding result — whether <s>apūrva</s> (unseen transcendent merit) as you [the opponent] maintain — in the fourfold expectancy of "for what purpose," "what," "by what means," and "how": the expectancy "for what purpose" is fulfilled by heaven and the like; the expectancy "what" is satisfied by "one should please the deity"; the expectancy "by what means" is fulfilled by names such as <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like; and the fulfillment of the expectancy "how" is the same for both you and us — this is the path established by verbal testimony.
Therefore, in sentences like "<s>yajeta</s>" (one should sacrifice), which convey to each qualified person (<s>adhikārin</s>) the qualification by the verbal root's meaning that is accomplishable through one's own effort, it is also understood from the sentence that the result arises from the performance of each respective verbal root's meaning, and adverse consequence (<s>pratyavāya</s>) from non-performance — both arising from the will (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) of the universal commander.
Thus.

children.text: atra ca "svaśāsanāvabodhi śāstraṃ ca pradiśya" iti bhāṣyamabhisaṃhitam /
children.translated_text: And here, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement "having set forth the scripture that makes known His own commands (<s>svaśāsana</s>)" is what is intended.
And this is established by the force of statements about punishment and reward consequent upon following or transgressing injunctions and prohibitions.
"The <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are My command alone; whoever conducts himself transgressing them,

children.text: ājñācchedī mama drohī madbhaktopi na vaiṣṇavaḥ" //
children.translated_text: he is a violator of My command, a traitor to Me — even if he is My devotee, he is not a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>."
Thus.
And the grammarians have analyzed: "<s>vidhi</s> means <s>preraṇa</s> (prompting/commanding)."
And <s>preraṇa</s> (prompting) is nothing other than <s>śāsana</s> (command).

children.text: tattvaratnākarakāraiścaivamuktam--- "kriyā tacchaktirvā kimapi tadapūrvaṃ pitṛsura- prasādo vā kartuḥ phalada iti raṅgeśa kudṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the author of the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s> has stated thus: "Is the meaning of <s>vidhi</s> the action itself, or its potency, or some <s>apūrva</s> (unseen transcendent force), or the gratification of ancestors and gods that yields fruit to the agent? O <s>Raṅgeśa</s>, what a distorted view!

The fruit of worship of You and of meritorious works (<s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>) is born of delight in You — thus the elders versed in the three <s>Vedas</s> [declare], and each <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) is Your command (<s>preraṇa</s>)."

children.text: " nityanaimittikādividhibhedeṣu ca praśāsiturabhiprāyaviśeṣāḥ vyañjitāḥ--- "ājñā te sanimittanityavidhayaḥ svargādikāmyadvidhiḥ sonujñā śaṭhacittaśāstravaśatopāyobhicāraśrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: And regarding the distinctions among <s>vidhi</s> as <s>nitya</s> (obligatory), <s>naimittika</s> (occasional), and others, the specific intentions of the Commander have been indicated: "Your commands are the obligatory and occasional injunctions; the injunction for desired ends like heaven and so on is Your permission (<s>anujñā</s>); the scriptural passage about sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>) is a stratagem for those of wicked minds to come under the control of scripture.

children.text: sarvā yasya samastaśāsituraho śrīraṅgarājasya te rakṣākūtanivedinī śrutirapi tvannityaśāstistataḥ" //
children.translated_text: All [these injunctions] belong to You, the universal Commander — O <s>Śrī Raṅgarāja</s>! Even the <s>Śruti</s> itself, which reveals Your protective intent, is therefore Your eternal command."
Thus.

children.text: api ca vedārthasaṅgahepyupāttaṃ draviḍabhāṣyam--- "svaśāsanānuvartino jñātvā kāruṇyāt svabhāvācchraddhayait vidvān karmadakṣaḥ" iti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Draviḍa Bhāṣya</s> (Tamil commentary) has also been cited in the <s>Vedārthasaṅgraha</s>: "Knowing those who follow His commands, out of compassion, by His very nature, the wise one, skilled in [prescribed] action, [acts] with faith."

children.text: anantaraṃ cāyamevārtho bhagavadgītāyāmapi darśitaḥ--- "ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ /
children.translated_text: And immediately after, this very meaning has been shown in the <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> as well: "Those human beings who always follow this teaching of Mine,
endowed with faith and free from envy — they too are released from [the bondage of] actions.
But those who, finding fault with this, do not follow My teaching —
know them to be deluded in all knowledge, lost and devoid of discrimination."

children.text: iti svājñānuvartinaḥ praśasya viparītān vinindan punarapi svajñānupālanamakurvatāmāsuraprakṛtyantarbhāvamabhidhāyādhamā gatiścoktetir idṛśa eva vidhiśabdārtho vedāntibhiḥ svīkṛtaḥ" iti /
children.translated_text: Thus, having praised those who follow His own command and censured those who oppose it, and having further declared that those who do not uphold His ordinance fall into the category of those with demoniac nature (<s>āsuraprakṛti</s>) and that the lowest destiny is proclaimed [for them] — it is precisely this meaning of the word <s>vidhi</s> that has been accepted by the <s>Vedāntins</s>."
Some among the opponents too have concurred with this.

children.text: ato mūlaskandhīkṛtaniyogaṃ dhātvarthasya kartṛvyāpārasādhyatvaṃ vā nirviṣayapreraṇāsaṃbhavāt tatsādhyatvaparyantaṃ preṣaṇameva vā liṅādyasādhāraṇārthaḥ, iti sthite "vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ" iti samabhivyāhṛtanimantraṇādisamānayogakṣematayā vidhiśabdārthatayā vyākṛtasya preṣaṇasyaiva liṅādiśabdavācyatvaṃ yuktamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the distinctive meaning of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like is either <s>niyoga</s> (injunction) — which has been made its root and trunk — or <s>kartṛvyāpārasādhyatva</s> (accomplishability through the agent's effort) of the verbal root's meaning, or — since objectless prompting is impossible — <s>preṣaṇa</s> (commanding) that extends up to the accomplishment of that [action]. This being established, since in the Pāṇinian rule "<s>vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ</s>" (the optative <s>liṅ</s> is used in injunction, invitation, respectful address, instruction, inquiry, and request), <s>vidhi</s> is co-listed with invitation and the like, and shares the same grammatical domain with them, it is fitting that <s>preṣaṇa</s> (commanding) — which has been grammatically analyzed as the meaning of the word <s>vidhi</s> — is what is expressed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and related forms.
Others hold that even on an alternative interpretation, <s>preṣaṇa</s> (commanding) is implicitly included [in the meaning of <s>liṅ</s>].

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 39 idaṃ ca vidhivākyānāmīśvaraśāsanātmakatvaṃ jaiminināpi sūcitameva--- "codanālakṣaṇortho dharmaḥ" iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 39. And this view — that injunctive sentences are of the nature of the Lord's command (<s>īśvaraśāsana</s>) — has been indicated by <s>Jaimini</s> himself as well: "<s>Dharma</s> is that which is characterized by <s>codanā</s> (injunction/impulsion)" [<s>Mīmāṃsā Sūtra</s> 1.1.2].

children.text: codanāśabdo hi codakaṃ kañcit puruṣaṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: For the word <s>codanā</s> (injunction) implies some person who impels (<s>codaka</s>).

children.text: ahṛdayādapi śābarodāharaṇādidaṃ vyajyate--- "ācāryacoditaḥ karomīti hi dṛśyate" iti //
children.translated_text: This is revealed even from the illustration cited by <s>Śabara</s>, though perhaps without full deliberation: "For it is observed that 'I act as prompted by the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>).'"

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 40 evaṃ codanāśabdasūcitaśca puruṣaḥ svavākyena prāgeva viśeṣato darśitaḥ /
apica autpattikasūtre "tasya jñānamupadeśaḥ" ityasūtrayat /
upadeśopi hi upadeṣṭāramākṣipati /
"tatpramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasya" iti sūtrakhaṇḍe ca svasya svācāryabhūtabādarāyaṇasamānābhiprāyatvaṃ vyañjitam /
sa ca bādarāyaṇo jaiminiṃ svaśiṣyamabhyupagateśvarāditattvaṃ "sākṣādapyavirodhaṃ jaiminiḥ" ityādiṣu bahuṣu sūtreṣvadarśayat /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> showed <s>Jaimini</s>, his own disciple, as one who accepted the reality of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and other truths, in many <s>sūtras</s> such as '<s>Sākṣād apy avirodhaṃ Jaiminiḥ</s>' ('Even directly, there is no contradiction, [says] <s>Jaimini</s>') and so forth.

children.text: pratikṣepastu kvācitkaḥ anyaparoktyāpātapratītārthamandamatimohanirāsārtho vā kṣudrapramādamātrasyāpyuddhārārtho veti na pradhānavirodhakalpanaliṅgam /
children.translated_text: The occasional refutation [of <s>Jaimini</s>'s views] is either for removing the confusion of dull-witted persons who understand the apparent meaning of another's statement, or for correcting even a minor inadvertent error — it is not a reason (<s>liṅga</s>) for imputing a fundamental disagreement.

children.text: arthavādādhikaraṇe ca "vidhinā tvekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ" iti preraṇarūpavidhipratipādakaliṅādyavayavadvārā samudāyabhūtaṃ vidhyuddeśavākyaṃ lakṣayitvā tadekavākyatvamarthavādānāṃ vadan kṛtsnasya vedasyeśvarājñārūpavidhipratipādakatvaṃ tadvākyakaṇṭhoktamasūcayat /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Arthavādādhikaraṇa</s> (section on eulogistic passages), by the [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>Vidhinā tv ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ</s>' ('But because of forming a single sentence with an injunction, they [arthavādas] would serve the purpose of praising the injunctions'), having indicated the sentence that is a unified whole (<s>samudāya</s>) — which conveys an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) in the form of a prompting — through its component parts such as prompting-markers (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like, and stating that the <s>arthavādas</s> (eulogistic passages) form a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatva</s>) with that [injunction], he indicated what is explicitly stated in the very text of those sentences: that the entire <s>Veda</s> conveys injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>) in the form of the commands of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).
The same should be understood elsewhere as well. //

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 40. And the person implied by the word <s>codanā</s> has already been specifically identified earlier by his [<s>Jaimini</s>'s] own statement.
Furthermore, in the <s>autpattikasūtra</s> (the sūtra on the innate [connection of word and meaning]), he composed the sūtra: "Instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>) is the knowledge of that [<s>dharma</s>]." And <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction) too implies an instructor (<s>upadeṣṭṛ</s>).
And in the section of the sūtra "That [Vedic word] is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) — [this is the view] of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>," [<s>Jaimini</s>] has indicated his own agreement with <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, who is his own teacher.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 41 evaṃ śrutistāvadīśvarājñā, tadanuvidhānāt smṛtirapi /
brāhmaṇamantrārthavādamayā hyanantā vedāḥ saṅkīrṇā vikīrṇāḥ kvacit kadācidutsannāśca /
tatra kṛtsnavedino manvādayastattaddeśakālaviśeṣeṣvakṛtsnavedināṃ tattvānuṣṭhānaviplavapraśamanāya svānubhūtān vedārthān yathāvannibadhnanti; atastanmūlonādivācāmarthanirṇayaḥ /
śrutismṛtivirodhe tu smṛtyā mūlāntarānumānādanuṣṭhānavikalpaṃ kecidāhuḥ /
sarveṣāṃ guṇatrayavatāmāptatamatvepi kvācitkabhramasaṃbhavācchrutyā smṛtibādhaḥ, ityapare /
tattvaviṣanaye tu virodhe bādha eva, ānyaparyaṃvā, vastuni vikalpāsaṃbhavāt /
smṛtidvayavirodhe tu parigrahatāratamyādibhirvyavasthā /
na ca kvacit smṛtīnāmaprāmāṇye sarvatrānāśvāsaḥ, bādhakādarśanāt, kāraṇadoṣakḷpteśca niyataliṅgābhāvāt, saṃvādabhūyastvādibhiḥ parigrahānyathānupapattyā ca śrutereva mūlatvakalpanopapatteḥ; anyathā pauruṣeyavākyasya sarvasyāprāmāṇyaprasaṅge vilīnamāgamena /
na caitannāniṣṭamiti vaktuṃ śakyam, pitrādyāptavākyaṃ pramāṇīkṛtya cāvārkasya pravṛttidarśanāt /
na ca kvācitkasaṃvādamātreṇa bāhyāgameṣvapi visrambhāvakāśaḥ, pratyakṣaśrutivirodhabhūyastvena vaidikaparigrahābhāvena vedabāhyatvaprasiddhyā vedapratikṣepācca vedākhyamūlakalpanasyāśakyatvāt /
na cālaukikaṃ pratyakṣādimūlatvasaṃbhavaḥ /
yogajasākṣātkāramūlatvakḷptirapi vedāviruddhasthale syāt; na ca tatrāpi niścayaḥ, viparītopalambhasyāpi saṃbhavāditi /
children.translated_text: The assumption that [non-Vedic traditions] are rooted in <s>yogaja-sākṣātkāra</s> (direct perception born of yoga) would apply only where they do not contradict the <s>Veda</s>; and even there, there is no certainty, because the occurrence of erroneous perception is also possible.
Therefore, the <s>smṛtis</s> rooted in the <s>Veda</s> are threefold — based on the distinction of <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (law codes), <s>itihāsa</s> (epics), and <s>purāṇa</s> (ancient lore).
Of these, the first two are placed within a single field of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>) because their distance [from the Veda] is not great.

children.text: atra cādhikṛtānadhikṛtavibhāgena balābalaniyatirābhāsāhnike darśitā; purāṇeṣvapi sāttvikarājasādivibhāgaśca //
children.translated_text: And here, the determination of relative strength through the division of those who are qualified and those who are not qualified has been shown in the section on semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>); and in the <s>Purāṇas</s> too, there is the division into <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), <s>rājasa</s> (passionate), and so forth. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 41. Thus, <s>śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) is indeed the command of <s>Īśvara</s>; and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) likewise, because it follows that [śruti]. / For the <s>Vedas</s>, consisting of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>arthavāda</s>, are infinite, intermixed, scattered, and in some places at some times, lost. / Therein, <s>Manu</s> and other [sages] who know the entire <s>Veda</s>, in order to pacify the disturbance in the understanding and practice of truth among those who do not know the entire <s>Veda</s> in particular places and times, compose the meanings of the <s>Veda</s> as they have experienced them, faithfully; therefore, the determination of the meaning of those beginningless utterances that have that [Veda] as their root [is established]. / But when there is a conflict between <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, some say there is an option in practice, by inferring a different Vedic source for the <s>smṛti</s>. / Others [say that] because even for all those [sages] who are subject to the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), though they are most trustworthy, occasional error is possible, <s>smṛti</s> is overridden by <s>śruti</s>. / But in a conflict concerning matters of reality (<s>tattva</s>), there is indeed overriding, or reduction to a different meaning (<s>ānyaparya</s>), because an option is impossible with respect to a [fixed] reality. / In a conflict between two <s>smṛtis</s>, the resolution is through relative acceptance, gradation, and so forth. / Nor does the invalidity of <s>smṛtis</s> in some cases lead to distrust everywhere, because no overriding factor is seen [universally], because there is no invariable mark for inferring a defect in the cause, and because through the preponderance of corroboration and the impossibility of explaining the acceptance [of smṛti] otherwise, it is reasonable to assume that <s>śruti</s> alone is its root; otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence that all human-authored utterances are invalid, and the entire body of tradition (<s>āgama</s>) would be dissolved. / Nor can one say 'that is not undesirable,' because we observe that even a child (<s>avārka</s>) acts by accepting as authoritative the words of trustworthy persons such as father and others. / Nor is there scope for trust in non-Vedic traditions merely on the basis of occasional agreement, because through the preponderance of conflict with perception and <s>śruti</s>, due to the absence of Vedic acceptance, through the well-known fact of their being outside the <s>Veda</s>, and through their rejection of the <s>Veda</s>, it is impossible to assume a Vedic root for them. / Nor is it possible for supernatural [doctrines] to have their root in perception and such.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 42 yānipunaḥ sāṃkhyayogapāśupatapañcarātrāṇi, tānyapi dharmaśāstrabhedā eva;pariśuddhātmacintanarūpajñānayogapradarśanādhikṛtaṃ śāstraṃ sāṃkhyam; samādhiparyantakarmayoganiṣṭhaṃ śāstraṃ yogaḥ; pratibuddhetaraviṣayapaśupatibhajanapratipādakaṃ pāśupatam; pratibuddhaviṣayabhagavadananyabhajanopadeśapravṛttaṃ tu śāstraṃ pañcarātram /
etāni ca kvacit kvacidaṃśe parasparopajīvīni /
parasparavirodhe tu vedānusāreṇa balābalavyavasthā, vedaviruddhe tvaṃśe bādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: In cases of mutual conflict, the determination of relative strength is in accordance with the <s>Veda</s>; but in the portion that contradicts the <s>Veda</s>, there is overriding (<s>bādha</s>).
Because inadvertent error is possible for all [authors] who are not <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

children.text: vipralambhasya tu asurādivyāmohanodyate sākṣādīśvare 'pi; yathoktaṃ bhagavataiva--- "tvaṃ hi rudrapa mahābāho mohaśāstrāṇi kāraya /
children.translated_text: But as for deception, it is mentioned even in the case of <s>Īśvara</s> himself, for the purpose of deluding <s>asuras</s> (demons) and others; as stated by the Blessed Lord himself — 'O <s>Rudra</s>, O mighty-armed one, compose deluding scriptures (<s>mohaśāstra</s>).
Show a path of little effort and display quick results. //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 42. Now, as for <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, and <s>Pañcarātra</s> — these too are indeed varieties of <s>dharmaśāstra</s>. The <s>śāstra</s> (teaching) that is devoted to demonstrating <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) in the form of contemplation of the purified self is <s>Sāṃkhya</s>; the <s>śāstra</s> devoted to <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action) culminating in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) is <s>Yoga</s>; that which teaches the worship of <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of bound souls) for those who have not yet attained enlightenment is <s>Pāśupata</s>; but the <s>śāstra</s> that is directed toward teaching the exclusive devotion to the Lord (<s>Bhagavat</s>) for those who have attained enlightenment is <s>Pañcarātra</s>. / And these, in certain respects, are mutually supportive.

children.text: ahaṃ mohaṃ kariṣyāmi yo manaṃ mohayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: I shall create delusion that will delude the minds [of the unworthy].
' Thus. //

children.text:
ato yat sāṃkhyar iśvarānadhiṣṭhitapradhānādipratipādanam, yacceśvaramabhyupagamya kevalanimittakāraṇatvapratiphalanakalpaiśvaryavarṇanaṃ yoge, yacca pāśupate parāvaratattvavyatyayavedaviruddhācārādikalpanam, tat sarvaṃ vyapohya śiṣṭe ḥṃśe prāmāṇyaṃ grāhyam /
na caitat tuṣataṇḍulavibhāgavadalpajñaiḥ śakyam /
ato hi śārīrake trayāṇāṃ nirāsaḥ /
pañcarātraṃ tu kṛtsnaṃ śrutivat smṛtivadvā pramāṇam, pratyakṣaśrutyādivirodhābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Pañcarātra</s>, however, is authoritative in its entirety, like <s>śruti</s> or <s>smṛti</s>, because there is no conflict with perception, <s>śruti</s>, and the like.

children.text: mahābhārate ca āptatama mānavadharmaśāstrasyāpi tanmūlatvokteratyādareṇa vyāsadiparigrahaviśeṣādīśvaradayāmūlatvena ca kāraṇadoṣaprasaṅgābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And because, in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, even the <s>Mānavadharmaśāstra</s> (Laws of <s>Manu</s>), which is [regarded as] most authoritative, is said to have that [Pañcarātra] as its root; because of the special acceptance by <s>Vyāsa</s> and others with great regard; and because there is no occasion for the defect of the cause, since it is rooted in the compassion of <s>Īśvara</s>.
'The Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>, having extracted the essence from the <s>Vedāntas</s>,
the wise one, out of compassion for his devotees, condensed it at ease.' //

Therefore, whatever in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teaches a <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and such that are not presided over by <s>Īśvara</s>; and whatever in <s>Yoga</s>, while accepting <s>Īśvara</s>, describes his sovereignty as merely that of an efficient cause whose glory does not manifest [in creation]; and whatever in <s>Pāśupata</s> involves the reversal of higher and lower realities, conduct contrary to the <s>Veda</s>, and the like — all that is to be rejected, and authority is to be accepted only in the remaining portions. / But this is not possible for persons of little understanding, like separating husk from rice. / Hence indeed the refutation of the three [Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Pāśupata] in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Brahmasūtras].

children.text:
iti ca tatraiva vyakteḥ /
vedaprāmāṇyāṅgīkāratadarthoktibhūyastvatadvaiśadyahetutvavacanasādhuparitrāṇārthatvasattvottaranāradādiśrotṛkatvādinibandhanaspaṣṭaprāmāṇyatvāt /
na ca vipralambhārthaṃ tathā nibandhaḥ, anyatrāpi prasaṅgāt;"adhītā bhagavan vedāḥ" ityāderdurgrahatvamātratātparyeṇa vedanindādirūpatvābhāvāt /

children.translated_text: Even if [certain passages] appear to be of the nature of censure, they function to praise the alternative [i.e., the Pañcarātra] by censuring the other, just as the censure in '<s>uditahoma</s>' (the post-sunrise oblation) [censures the alternative to praise the preferred option].

children.text: "saṅkarṣaṇo nāma jīvo jāyata" ityādestvavatārādigocaratvasya tatraiva siddheḥ /
children.translated_text: As for [the objection based on the passage] '<s>Saṅkarṣaṇo nāma jīvo jāyate</s>' ('A <s>jīva</s> named <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> is born') — the fact that this refers to <s>avatāra</s> (divine descent) and such is established in that very [Pañcarātra] context.

children.text: śarīrake ca--- "utpattyasaṃbhavāt""na ca kartuḥ karaṇam" iti sūtradvayena pūrvapakṣaṃ kṛtvā "vijñānādibhāve vā tadapratiṣedhaḥ" "vipratiṣedhācca" iti tatprāmāṇyapratiṣedhaḥ parihṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Brahmasūtras] — having raised the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie objection) through the two <s>sūtras</s> '<s>Utpattyasaṃbhavāt</s>' ('Because origination is impossible') and '<s>Na ca kartuḥ karaṇam</s>' ('And the instrument is not [produced] from the agent'), the rejection of the authority of that [Pañcarātra] is resolved [in the <s>siddhānta</s>] by '<s>Vijñānādibhāve vā tadapratiṣedhaḥ</s>' ('Or, if [Saṅkarṣaṇa and others] exist as [forms of] knowledge and so forth, there is no prohibition of that') and '<s>Vipratiṣedhāc ca</s>' ('And because of contradiction [with the objections]').

children.text: tathā nirmūlatvāsatparigrahasatparigrahābhāvavaudikasaṃskāravarjanāvaidikasaṃskāravidhānavidyāsthānaparigaṇanābhāvakṣudravidyābāhulyādimandaśaṅkānāṃ bhagavadyāmunamunibhiḥ parihāraḥ prapañcitaḥ iti neha pratanyate //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the feeble doubts — such as [the objection that Pañcarātra] has no Vedic root, that it is accepted by unworthy persons, that it lacks acceptance by worthy persons, that it abandons Vedic rites (<s>saṃskāra</s>), that it prescribes non-Vedic rites, that it is not included in the enumeration of the fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>), that it abounds in trivial doctrines, and so forth — have been elaborately refuted by the blessed <s>Yāmuna</s> sage, and hence are not expanded upon here. //

Thus, because of the clear statement in that very [Mahābhārata]. / Because of its manifest authoritativeness based on: the acceptance of the authority of the <s>Veda</s>, the preponderance of statements of Vedic meanings, being the cause of their clarity, the purpose of protecting the virtuous, having <s>Nārada</s> and other listeners of <s>sattva</s> (pure) nature, and other such grounds. / Nor is such a composition for the purpose of deception, because the same consequence would apply elsewhere too; because passages such as '<s>Adhītā bhagavan Vedāḥ</s>' ('The <s>Vedas</s> have been studied, O Blessed One') are not of the nature of censure of the <s>Veda</s> — their purport being merely the difficulty of understanding [the Vedas].
<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 43. Thus, because it is directly rooted in the compassion of <s>Īśvara</s>, it [Pañcarātra] surpasses the compositions of <s>Manu</s> and others.
For those [compositions of Manu and others], when they conflict with <s>śruti</s>, may indeed be overridden,
because occasional error and the like are possible due to their being subject to the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature).

children.text: smṛtyādīnāṃ hi śrutimūlatayaiva prāmāṇyamiti bhāṣyepyuktaṃ "taduparyapi" ityadhikaraṇe-- "saṅkīrṇabrāhmaṇamantrārthavādamūleṣu dharmaṃśāstretihāsapurāṇeṣu" iti //
children.translated_text: For the authoritativeness of <s>smṛtis</s> and the like is indeed based on their having <s>śruti</s> as their root — as has been said in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) too, in the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) [beginning with] '<s>Tad upary api</s>' ('Even beyond that'): 'In the <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, <s>itihāsas</s>, and <s>purāṇas</s>, which are rooted in the intermixed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>arthavāda</s> [of the Veda].' //

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 44 tata eva caiṣāṃ viprakīrṇaśākhāmūlatvaṃ siddhāntaḥ, ityapi sūcitam /
kvacit kadācit keṣāñcicchākhāviśeṣāṇāmucchedaḥ; te ca punarvyāsādibhiḥ kvacit kadācit pravartyante, ityetāvatā ucchinnaśākhāmūlatvamastu /
uktaṃ ca bhagavatā āpastambena--- "teṣāmutsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogādanumīyante" iti /
manvādivacanaprāmāṇyaṃ nyāyamantareṇāpi śrutyaiva siddham--- "yadvai kiñca manuravadat tadbheṣajam" ityādibhiḥ /
evaṃ śiṣṭācārasyāpi--- "yathā te tatra varteran, tathā tratra vartarthoḥ" "yānyasmākaṃ sucaritāni, tāni tvayopāsyāni" ityādibhiḥ /

children.translated_text: And <s>smṛti</s> [also confirms]: '<s>Smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām</s>' / ('And the remembered tradition and conduct of those who know that [Veda]'),
'and the conduct of the virtuous' — and so forth.

children.text: śrutyaiva dharmanirṇaye saṃbhavati kiṃ dharmaśāstreṇa ? ityāśaṅkyāha marīciḥ --- "durbodhā vaudikāḥ śabdāḥ prakīrṇatvācca ye khilāḥ /
children.translated_text: If the determination of <s>dharma</s> is possible through <s>śruti</s> alone, what need is there for <s>dharmaśāstra</s>? Anticipating this doubt, <s>Marīci</s> says: 'The Vedic words are hard to understand, and because of being scattered, [some are] supplementary (<s>khila</s>);
those very [meanings], made clear in meaning by those who know them, are established in <s>smṛti</s> texts (<s>smṛtitantra</s>).' //

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 44. From this very [principle], the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) is that these [smṛtis] are rooted in scattered Vedic branches (<s>viprakīrṇa-śākhā</s>) — this too has been indicated. / In some places, at some times, certain particular Vedic branches are destroyed; and these are again promulgated by <s>Vyāsa</s> and others at other places and times — to this extent, let there be rootedness in lost branches (<s>ucchinnaśākhā</s>). / And the blessed <s>Āpastamba</s> has said: '<s>Teṣām utsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogād anumīyante</s>' ('Their lost recensions are inferred from practice'). / The authoritativeness of the statements of <s>Manu</s> and others is established by <s>śruti</s> itself, even without independent reasoning — by [passages] such as '<s>Yad vai kiñca Manur avadat tad bheṣajam</s>' ('Whatever <s>Manu</s> said is a remedy') and the like. / Similarly, the [authoritativeness] of the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>) too [is established by śruti] — by [passages] such as '<s>Yathā te tatra varteran, tathā tatra vartethāḥ</s>' ('As they would conduct themselves there, so should you conduct yourself there') and '<s>Yāny asmākaṃ sucaritāni, tāni tvayopāsyāni</s>' ('Whatever good practices are ours, those should be followed by you') and the like.

children.text: iti satyapi dharmaśāstre gṛhyāpekṣāṃ darśayati devalaḥ--- "manvādayaḥ prayoktāro dharmaśāstrasya kīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though <s>dharmaśāstra</s> exists, <s>Devala</s> shows the dependence on <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras] — '<s>Manu</s> and others are declared to be the promulgators of <s>dharmaśāstra</s>;
those who apply what was promulgated by them are the authors of <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras], through their own <s>mantras</s>.' //
Therefore, the determination of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> depends on <s>dharmaśāstra</s>, <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras], and the like.
And in cases of conflict, the determination of relative strength is established as appropriate.

children.text: bhagavaddharmaśāstrasya tu pañcarātrasya śrutyādivirodhe ṣoḍaśigrahaṇāderiva deśakālādhikāryavasthāviśeṣaviṣayatayā vikalpa eva, śruterivāsyāpi doṣasaṃbhāvanāvirahādisiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: But for the divine <s>dharmaśāstra</s> that is <s>Pañcarātra</s>, in the case of conflict with <s>śruti</s> and the like, there is merely an option based on the specificity of place, time, qualified person, and circumstance — just as in the case of the <s>ṣoḍaśi</s>-grahaṇa (taking the sixteenth cup) and the like — because it is established that for this [Pañcarātra], like <s>śruti</s>, there is no possibility of defect.

children.text: āhuścaivamabhiyuktāḥ--- "vede kartrādyabhāvāt" ityārabhya, "tasmāt sāṃkhyaṃ sayogaṃ sapaśupatimataṃ kutracit pañcarātraṃ sarvatraiva pramāṇaṃ tadidamavagataṃ pañcamādeva vedāt" //
children.translated_text: And those who are well-versed have said thus — beginning with '<s>Vede kartr-ādy-abhāvāt</s>' ('Because in the <s>Veda</s> there is no author, etc.') — 'Therefore, <s>Sāṃkhya</s> together with <s>Yoga</s>, together with <s>Pāśupata</s> doctrine, [is authoritative] in some respects; <s>Pañcarātra</s> is authoritative everywhere — this is understood from the fifth <s>Veda</s> itself.' //
Thus.
Thus.

children.text: anyatra ca--- upaniṣadi tu bahvyāṃ vyāvaghoṣyāmadoṣa- pratihataguṇarāśirghuṣyate tārkṣyaketuḥ /
children.translated_text: And elsewhere — 'In the manifold <s>Upaniṣads</s>, He whose fame is unobstructed, whose heap of qualities is unassailed — <s>Tārkṣyaketu</s> (He whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>) — is proclaimed.

children.text: śrutirapi tadupajñaiḥ pañcarātrairvikalpaṃ na labhata iti sūktaṃ bhāṣyakṛdyāmunāryaiḥ" //
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> does not admit of option with respect to the <s>Pañcarātra</s> composed by Him — this was well said by the <s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s> (commentator) and the noble <s>Yāmuna</s>.' //

children.translated_text: And here, there should be no doubt regarding its Vedic status, [because of the verse:] 'He who, in the <s>vākas</s> (prose sections), <s>anuvākas</s> (sub-sections), <s>niṣads</s>, and <s>upaniṣads</s>,
is the great root of the great tree of the <s>Veda</s> — //

Thus. / This has been elaborated by the <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Yāmuna</s>, by refuting all the prima facie objections (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) that were raised [against] the authoritativeness of the <s>Āgama</s> [i.e., Pañcarātra]. / It has been elaborated [by him]. / Following him, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (the author of the Bhāṣya, i.e., <s>Rāmānuja</s>) has commented on the <s>Śrīpāñcarātrādhikaraṇa</s> (section on Pañcarātra in the Brahmasūtras).

skandhabhūtā ṛgādyāste śākhābhūtāstathā mune /

" ityādibhiḥ tacchrutitpratipādanāt /
atra bhagavadyāmunamunibhirevokto grantho likhyate--- "yadapyuktam--- 'garbhādhānādidāhāntasaṃskārāntarasevanāt bhāgavatānāma brāhmaṇyam' iti, tatrāpyajñānamevāparādhyati, na punarāyuṣmato doṣaḥ; yata ete vaṃśaparamparayā vājasaneyaśākhāmadhīyānāḥ kātyāyanādigṛhyoktamārgeṇa garbhādhānādisaṃskārān kurvate, ye punaḥ sāvitryanuvacanaprabhṛti trayīdharmātyāgena ekāyanaśrutivihitāneva catvāriṃśatsaṃskārān kurvate, tepi svaśākhāgṛhyoktadharmaṃ yathāvadanutiṣṭhamānā na śākhāntarīyakarmānanuṣṭhānāt brāhmaṇyāt pracyavante, anyeṣāmapi parasparaśākhāvihitakarmānanuṣṭhānanimittābrāhmaṇyaprasaṅgāt; sarvatra hi jāticaraṇagotrādhikārādivyavasthitā eva samayācārā upalabhyante /
yadyapi sarvaśākhāpratyayamekaṃ karma, tathāpi na parasparavilakṣaṇādhikārisambaddhā dharmāḥ kvacit, samuccīyante /
children.translated_text: Although a single rite is [ideally] attested by all branches, still, duties connected with mutually distinct qualified persons are never combined anywhere.

The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), qualified for rites such as <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>abhigamana</s> (approach), <s>upādāna</s> (collection), <s>ijyā</s> (worship), and so forth — which are the sole means for attaining the Lord (<s>Bhagavat</s>) and which are prescribed by the <s>Ekāyana Śruti</s> at the culmination of the three <s>Vedas</s> (<s>trayyanta</s>) — are distinct from the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who are qualified for rites such as the <s>Aindrāgneya</s> and the like, which are means for enjoying fruits such as heaven, sons, and so forth, prescribed by the three <s>Vedas</s>. Thus, for neither group does the non-performance of rites prescribed by the other's branch result in the loss of brahminhood.

children.text: yathā ca ekāyanaśākhāyā apauruṣeyatvam, tathā kāśmīrāgamaprāmaṇyaṃ eva prapañcitamiti neha prastūyate /
children.translated_text: And just as the non-human-authoredness (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Ekāyana</s> branch [has been established], so too the authoritativeness of the <s>Kāśmīra Āgama</s> has been elaborated in that very [work by Yāmuna], and hence is not discussed here.

children.text: prakṛtānāṃ tu bhāgavatānāṃ sāvitryanuvacanāditrayīsambandhasya sphuṭataramu palabdhirna tattyāganimittavrātyatvādisandehaṃ sahate" iti //
children.translated_text: But for the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> under discussion, the connection with the three <s>Vedas</s> through the repetition of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> and the like is clearly evident, and [this evidence] does not tolerate the doubt of <s>vrātya</s>-status (being an outcast) and the like caused by its abandonment.' //

the <s>Ṛg</s> [Veda] and others are its trunks, O sage, and those [other texts] are its branches.' / And so forth, because of [such] statements. / Also, because in the <s>Ṛgveda</s> recension there is recited '<s>Vratam etat suduścaram</s>' ('This vow is very difficult to perform'), demonstrating agreement [with the Pañcarātra]; because even in the enumeration of Vedic branches by <s>Vyāsa</s>, the <s>Nirukta</s> branch too has been counted; because in the <s>Sāttvata</s>, <s>Pauṣkara</s>, and other [texts] that are the essence of the Lord's teaching, in the prescription of esoteric ritual (<s>rahasyāmnāya</s>), by [statements such as] '<s>Ekāyanīya-śākhā-uktaiḥ mantraiḥ paramapāvanaiḥ</s>' ('With the supremely purifying <s>mantras</s> taught in the <s>Ekāyanīya</s> branch') and the like, [its status as] that <s>śruti</s> is demonstrated. / Here the text composed by the blessed <s>Yāmuna</s> sage himself is cited — 'As for the statement: "By performing rites different from [the usual] sacraments from conception (<s>garbhādhāna</s>) to cremation (<s>dāha</s>), the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> [lose their] brahminhood" — there too it is only ignorance that offends, not a fault of yours; for these [Bhāgavatas], by lineage tradition, study the <s>Vājasaneya</s> branch and perform sacraments from conception onward following the path prescribed by the <s>Kātyāyana</s> and other <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras]. But those who, from the repetition of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> onwards, abandon the duties of the three <s>Vedas</s> and perform only the forty sacraments prescribed by the <s>Ekāyana Śruti</s> — they too, faithfully following the <s>dharma</s> prescribed by the <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtra] of their own branch, do not fall from brahminhood because of non-performance of rites prescribed by another branch; for otherwise, the same consequence of loss of brahminhood would apply to all others too, due to non-performance of rites prescribed by each other's branches. For everywhere, ritual practices are observed as established according to <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>caraṇa</s> (school), <s>gotra</s> (lineage), qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>), and so forth.

caturvidhaṃ cedaṃ vedamūlabhūtāṃśasya upabṛṃhaṇam; tadabhiprāyeṇa hyuktaṃ mahābhārate--- "mahato vedavṛkṣasya mūlabhūto mahānayam /
" ityādi /
caturṇāṃ caiṣāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ śrīpauṣkarādiṣu bhagavataiva darśitam /

yacca teṣu caturṣu sādhāraṇyāsādhāraṇyārcopasaṃhāryānupasaṃhāryādikaṃ vaktavyam, tat sarvaṃ śrīpāñcarātrarakṣāsiddhāntavyavasthāyāṃ sarvaparāmarśena sādhitamasmābhiriti tatraiva tadvistaraḥ sāttvatadharmagopturananyairanusandheya iti nātra prabrūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: And whatever is to be said regarding the commonality and uncommonality, amenability and non-amenability to subsumption under <s>arcā</s> (image worship), etc. among those four [<s>Vaikhānasa</s> texts], all of that has been established by us with comprehensive analysis in the <s>Śrīpāñcarātrarakṣā</s> and the <s>Siddhāntavyavasthā</s>; therefore its detailed treatment is found there alone. It should be investigated only by those uniquely devoted to protecting the <s>Sāttvata</s> (Vaiṣṇava) <s>dharma</s>, and so we do not expound upon it here.

children.text: evaṃ sthite kecid bāhlīkaprāyāḥ āgamabāhyāḥ śrīmadvaikhānasaprāmāṇye viśerate /
children.translated_text: This being the case, certain people, mostly <s>Bāhlīka</s>-like (barbarian-like), who are outside the pale of authoritative tradition, raise objections to the validity of the venerable <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [texts].

children.text: tatra tāvat kalpasūtraṃ nāpramāṇam, itaravadeva kalpasūtratvāt, tatkartuśca kalpasūtrakāratvaprasiddheḥ, vedāviruddhatvāt, vaidikamantraireva sakaladharmavidhānāt, sūtrāntarāṇāmapi kuṇḍasanniveśalakṣaṇādiṣu kvacit kvacit tadupajīvanāt, varṇāśramadharmāṇāmanukūlaṃ nārāyaṇaparatvapratipādanāderapi sattvamūlatvena prāmāṇyaikahetutvāt, "harimeva smarennityaṃ karmapūrvāpareṣvapi /
children.translated_text: In that regard, first, the <s>Kalpasūtra</s> is not without authority, because it is a <s>Kalpasūtra</s> just like the others, because its author is well-known as a <s>Kalpasūtra</s>-maker, because it does not contradict the <s>Veda</s>, because all <s>dharma</s> prescriptions employ Vedic <s>mantras</s> themselves, because other <s>sūtras</s> also rely upon it here and there in matters such as the layout of the fire-altar and similar topics, and because its teaching of supreme devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in a manner favorable to <s>varṇāśramadharma</s> (duties of social classes and life-stages) is grounded in <s>sattva</s> (goodness), which is the sole cause of validity. [As stated:] "One should always remember <s>Hari</s> in all acts, prior and subsequent;
One should meditate upon Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in bathing and other rituals."

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 45. And this <s>Pañcarātra</s> is fourfold: <s>Āgamasiddhānta</s>, <s>Divyasiddhānta</s>, <s>Tantrasiddhānta</s>, and <s>Tatrāntarasiddhānta</s>. / And this fourfold [Pañcarātra] is the amplification (<s>upabṛṃhaṇa</s>) of the portion that forms the root of the <s>Veda</s>; for with that in view, it has been said in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> — 'This great one is the root of the great tree of the <s>Veda</s>,' / and so forth. / And the definitions and other details of these four have been shown by the Blessed Lord himself in the <s>Śrīpauṣkara</s> and other [texts].

children.translated_text: If one objects that there is contradiction with the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> — no, because in reality there is no such [contradiction]; because the differences in prescribed rituals and the like are explicable as pertaining to specifically qualified practitioners, just like the differences in procedural variations among <s>Kalpasūtras</s>, and just like the division of ritual types among the four sub-divisions of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> in the form of <s>Āgama</s>, <s>Divyatantra</s>, and other <s>tantras</s>.
In the <s>Āśvamedhika</s> section of the venerable <s>Vaiṣṇavadharmaśāstra</s>, both [<s>Vaikhānasa</s> and <s>Pāñcarātra</s>] are accepted as equally authoritative.

children.text: dvayorapi parasparaprāmāṇyam "viṣṇostantraṃ dvidhā proktam" ityādiṣu vyañjitam /
children.translated_text: The mutual authority of both is indicated in passages such as "The <s>tantra</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is declared to be twofold."

children.text: parasparākṣepavacanāni tu ikṣubhakṣakṛticikīrṣubhirasahiṣṇubhirupakṣiptāni vā svaśāstrapraśaṃsārthavādarūpāṇi veti na tato virodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: As for statements of mutual censure, they are either interpolated by those who, like people desiring to eat sugarcane [for themselves], cannot tolerate [others], or they are in the nature of <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages) for the purpose of praising one's own scripture — therefore there is no contradiction from them.

Because <s>Śaunaka</s> and others have likewise prescribed it in passages such as these; and because, since it has been continuously studied by <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s through an unbroken lineage, there is no scope for textual corruption.
If one objects: "Let there be some such text, but what certainty is there that this is that [original text]?" — [we reply:] because the alternative is not found and this is found; otherwise there would be occasion for such doubt everywhere regarding <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and so forth.
Even granting that this is indeed that [text] and is authoritative, how can the four [texts] of <s>Bhārgava</s> etc. have authority? — This objection is invalid, because it has already been answered: the grounds of being composed by great sages, non-contradiction with the <s>Veda</s>, and so forth apply equally [to them].

kva tarhi nikṛṣṭajātyantaram ? /
kimasmāsu tannyāsīkṛtam ?; yenāsmābhiḥ pradarśanīyam /
na cāsmābhiranantā deśā draṣṭuṃ śākyāḥ /
sambhavati cocchedaḥ, idānīṃ kṣatriyavaiśyamāhiṣyādivat /
teṣāṃ keṣāṃ cinnāmasāmyamātrādatrānupraveśaḥ saṃbhavatīti cenna, kasyā api śaṅkāyāḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāt; asti ca varṇitvabhikṣutvādīnāṃ sāmyamanyatrāpi /
children.translated_text: If one objects that the entry [of non-Brāhmaṇas] into this [caste] is possible through mere similarity of name with some of them — no, because any such suspicion is easily raised anywhere; and the similarity of terms like <s>varṇin</s> (student) and <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) exists in other contexts as well.

children.text: yaścaivamatiśaṅkayā dūyate, sa tu svamātāpitṛcaritānavadhāraṇena svabrāhmaṇyamapi yathārhamatiśaṅketeti jitaṃ lokāyatena /
children.translated_text: And he who torments himself with such excessive suspicion should, by failing to ascertain the conduct of his own mother and father, raise excessive suspicion about his own <s>brāhmaṇya</s> as well — thus the <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialist) position triumphs [i.e., this leads to absurdity].
And the Lord has said: "The ignorant, the faithless, and the one whose self is full of doubt perishes;

children.text: nāyaṃ lokosti na paro na sukha saṃśayātmanaḥ" //
children.translated_text: For the doubting self, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness."

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 46. [Objection:] Now, the <s>Bhārgava</s> texts and others are not <s>Kalpasūtras</s>, since they are not accepted as such, since there is no established tradition [recognizing them as such], and since it is unreasonable. Nor are they other <s>Smṛtis</s>, since they are not listed among <s>Manu</s> and others, and since there is no such established recognition of them. Nor are they independent separate <s>tantras</s>, since they are not seen listed alongside <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and such systems, and because they follow the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [tradition].
Then by what category is their authority asserted?
[Reply:] Just like <s>Manu</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, etc., and just like the <s>Nāradīya</s> and others, their authority too is as <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (legal texts), because authoritative scholars accept that the enumeration of eighteen and so forth is merely illustrative [not exhaustive].
If one objects that in other <s>Smṛtis</s> there is no elaboration of festivals for deities and the like — let there be no elaboration; at least the basic form is acknowledged, and those [<s>Vaikhānasa</s> texts] are devoted to elaborating upon that.
Even so, [if one argues that] since the infinite mutual inequality among <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) is universal, those [texts] are for practitioners of lower qualification — no, because in those and in other [texts] as well, the primary emphasis is on <s>brāhmaṇya</s> (brahminhood) alone, and because this is what is actually observed.
If asked how they possess <s>brāhmaṇya</s> — peace be upon sin! Let us close our ears [to such blasphemy]! Still, it must be addressed.
For these [<s>Vaikhānasa</s>s] are indeed observed through an unbroken lineage to be <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who study the <s>Veda</s>, who are endowed with all Vedic <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments) prescribed in the <s>Vaikhānasa Sūtra</s>, who are diligent in the duties of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, and who are exclusively devoted to the Lord.
Surely it is a donkey among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who, precisely because of their <s>brāhmaṇya</s> and their being <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees of the Lord), wanders about in the opposite direction [i.e., denies their status]. Otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that even the <s>Vaikhānasa Kalpa</s> itself would be without authority, having no qualified practitioners.
[Objection:] Let it have authority; and let there be qualified practitioners in another region or another time; but who are these [present ones]? — [Reply:] Because one could say the same about other regions and times as well; or why should not the reverse be the case? And if so, what confidence is there even in other <s>Sūtras</s>?
[Objection:] The <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s' status is doubtful because of statements declaring them to be of low caste and because of disputes — [Reply:] because no such statement exists in authoritative texts; because even if it did, there is no evidence for their being of low caste; because the same applies to explaining the designations of <s>Sātvata</s> and others whose authority in <s>Āgama</s> has been established; for it is not the case that polysemous words do not exist, nor that identity of word entails identity of meaning, nor that difference of word entails difference of meaning — otherwise even the third <s>āśrama</s> (forest-dwelling stage) would be dissolved [since the same word is used differently]. And as for the dispute, since it depends merely on the wagging of tongues like yours, it could easily be raised regarding <s>sūtra</s>, <s>gotra</s> (lineage), and so forth as well.
[Objection:] At least before this time there was no [such dispute] — [Reply:] no, because this dispute too cannot be beginningless, and before that there was absence [of dispute]. And since there is no difference in the nature of dispute whether it is yours, present or future, there would be the consequence of perpetual lack of confidence in them.
[Objection:] At least we have no doubt about those [other Brāhmaṇas] — [Reply:] And do we have any [doubt] about these [<s>Vaikhānasa</s>s]?
[Objection:] Where then is the separate low caste [group with the same name]?
Has it been deposited with us, that we should have to produce it?
Nor can we survey infinite regions.
And extinction is possible, as now with <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Māhiṣyas</s>, and the like.
Thus.

children.text: tat siddhaṃ viśiṣṭādhikārikaṃ vedāviruddhaṃ vaikhānasādismaraṇaṃ pramāṇamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is established that <s>Vaikhānasa</s> and other <s>Smṛtis</s> are authoritative, being for specifically qualified practitioners and not contradicting the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: yacca dharmaśāstrādiṣu aṣṭādaśādiparisaṃkhyānam, na tadadhikasaṃkhyāvyavacchedaparam, anyeṣāmapi śiṣṭaparigrahāderaviśiṣṭatvāt, anuktāṃśadarśanādinā upajīvyatvācceti /
children.translated_text: And as for the enumeration of eighteen and so forth in the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>, it is not intended to exclude a greater number, because the same grounds of acceptance by the learned apply to others as well, and because [other <s>Smṛtis</s>] are relied upon for matters not found [in the eighteen].
Thus it is established that the <s>Veda</s>, together with its auxiliaries, is the [ultimate] authority.

children.text: "chandaḥ pādau śabdaśāstraṃ na vaktraṃ kalpaḥ pāṇī jyautiṣaṃ cakṣuṣī ca /
children.translated_text: "Meter is [the <s>Veda</s>'s] feet, grammar is its mouth, <s>Kalpa</s> (ritual procedure) its hands, <s>Jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy) its eyes,

children.text: śikṣā ghrāṇaṃ śrotramuktaṃ niruktaṃ vedasyāṅgānyāhuretāni ṣaṭ ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Śikṣā</s> (phonetics) its nose, <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology) is said to be its ears — these six are declared to be the limbs of the <s>Veda</s>."

children.text: " evaṃ saparikaravedārthatattvanirṇayaviṣayā "athāto dharmajijñāsā" ityārabhya "anāvṛttiḥ śabdādanāvṛttiḥ śabdāt ityevamantā viṃśatilakṣaṇī mīmāṃsā /
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> in twenty chapters, which has as its subject the determination of the true meaning of the <s>Veda</s> together with its auxiliaries, beginning with "Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>" and ending with "Non-return, from the word; non-return, from the word" —

children.text: "tatra ca saṃhitametaccharīrakaṃ jaiminīyena ṣoḍaśalakṣaṇeneti śāstraikatvasiddhiḥ" iti bhāṣyopātto vṛttigranthaḥ //
children.translated_text: "And therein, this <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtra) is connected with the <s>Jaiminīya</s> [Mīmāṃsā] of sixteen chapters, thus establishing the unity of the <s>śāstra</s>" — this is the statement from the <s>Vṛtti</s> text adopted in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary).

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 47 tattvaratnākare tvevamuktam--- "karmadevatābrahmagocarā sā tridhodbhabhau sūtrakārataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 47. In the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s>, however, it is stated thus: "That [<s>Mīmāṃsā</s>], dealing with <s>karma</s> (ritual action), <s>devatā</s> (deities), and <s>Brahman</s>, arose in three parts from the <s>Sūtrakāras</s> (authors of aphorisms):"
"From the sage <s>Jaimini</s>, from <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>, and from <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, in that order."
Thus.

The statements in these two [sources] that the <s>Devatākāṇḍa</s> (section on deities) belongs to <s>Jaimini</s> [in one] and to <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> [in the other] should be reconciled as intending subordination and the like, since they aim at the same meaning.

There [in the tradition], the content of the <s>Karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual section) has been summarized thus: "[The sixteen chapters deal with] the ascertainment of <s>dharma</s>, authority, distinction, subsidiary elements, application, sequence, agents,
transference, specification, prohibition, supersession, independent procedure, and incidental connection."
Thus.

children.text: "vedārthe nyāyacintye prathamamavasitaṃ karma taddevatā cā- thātaḥ śārīrakāṃśe niravadhikaphalabrahmacintā tvasūtri /
children.translated_text: "In the inquiry into the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> through logical investigation, first <s>karma</s> (ritual action) and <s>devatā</s> (deity) are settled; then, in the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtra) portion, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> of unlimited fruit is aphorized.

children.text: tatrādhyāye parasmin svayamupaniṣadāmanvayosyāvirodho mokṣopāyotha muktirviṣayaviṣayiṇau siddhasādhyau dvikārthau //
children.translated_text: Therein, in the first chapter, the coherence of the <s>Upaniṣads</s> and their non-contradiction [with other texts]; then the means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); then liberation itself; the object and the subject — the established and that to be established — these are the two purposes of the [last] two [chapters]."

"In the first [chapter], from beginning to end, the statements about the deeply hidden and clearly manifest <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and related matters are [discussed]; subsequently, the refutation of objections free from deficiency by means of <s>Smṛti</s> and other [texts], and the [discussion of] <s>Brahman</s> as the material cause, the senses, and so forth.

In the third [chapter] too, the merits and defects [of views] regarding the lower and higher [states], <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and its auxiliaries, and then in the last [chapter], worship, practice, their efficacy, the departure [of the soul], the path, and the fruits are investigated."
"Even before [philosophical] inquiry, study [of the <s>Veda</s>] is already obtained through injunction;
Therefore, inquiry by one who has not studied the <s>Veda</s> is prohibited by <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: kramo viṃśatilakṣaṇyā na vaidhaḥ kintu yauktikaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sequence of the twenty chapters is not injunctive but logical;
Therefore, in out-of-order investigation, no impropriety is taught."

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 48 evaṃ viṃśatilakṣaṇīśravaṇamananābhyāṃ supratiṣṭhitasamastaśāstrārthasya mokṣasādhanatayā vidheyaṃ nididhyāsanaṃ na vākyārthajñānamātram, tasya rāgaprāptaśravaṇādisiddhatvāt /
ata eva ca tasmin viśeṣe vedanādisāmānyaśabdaparyavasānam /
na ca nididhyāsanādikaṃ niṣiddham, varaṇīyatvameva vihitamiti vācyam; svatantrānyakartṛkavaraṇakarmībhāvasyāpuruṣatantretvenāvidheyatvāt /
atastaddhetunā prītirūpatvena upāsanameva viśiṣyate;tathā sati "bhaktyā tvananyayā" iti smṛtyavirodhaśca /
tadeva ca nididhyāsanaṃ prītirūpaṃ prakaraṇaviśeṣāt samādhiḥ /
ca cāṣṭāṅgaḥ śāstreṣu śiṣyate /

children.translated_text: And to that extent, the authority of the <s>Pātañjala</s> [Yoga system] also [holds].
And the cultivation of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is to be continued with moderation until the fruit [is attained].
And they record: "From <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) one should resort to <s>yoga</s>; from <s>yoga</s> one should enter into <s>svādhyāya</s>;
Through the perfection of <s>svādhyāya</s> and <s>yoga</s>, the Supreme Self is revealed."

<s>Nyā. Pa. Śa.</s> 48. Thus, for one who has well-established knowledge of the entire <s>śāstra</s> through <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing) and <s>manana</s> (reflection) on the twenty-chapter [<s>Mīmāṃsā</s>], what is to be practiced as the means to <s>mokṣa</s> is <s>nididhyāsana</s> (sustained meditation), not mere knowledge of the sentence-meaning, since the latter is already accomplished through <s>śravaṇa</s> and other [means] that are naturally desired.
And for this very reason, the general terms such as <s>vedana</s> (knowing) culminate in that specific [practice of <s>nididhyāsana</s>].
Nor should it be said that <s>nididhyāsana</s> and the like are [merely] not prohibited, that only their desirability is enjoined — because the state of being the object of another's independent act of choosing is not within a person's control and hence cannot be enjoined.
Therefore, <s>upāsana</s> (devotional meditation) is distinguished as having the nature of <s>prīti</s> (loving devotion) through its cause; and when this is so, there is also non-contradiction with the <s>Smṛti</s> [verse] "through exclusive devotion" (<s>bhaktyā tvananyayā</s>).
And that very <s>nididhyāsana</s> which has the nature of loving devotion is, by virtue of the specific context, <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption).
And that [<s>samādhi</s>] is taught in the <s>śāstras</s> as eightfold (<s>aṣṭāṅga</s>).
Thus.
As for what is heard: "The wise one, having studied the texts, intent upon knowledge and realization,
Should abandon the texts entirely, as one seeking grain [discards] the chaff."

children.text:
iti, tat kośatyāgābhiprāyam; na ca sādarapaṭusaṃskārapracayasaṃsiddhamedhāsaṃpadaḥ puruṣasya kośena kiñcit sāddhyam /
medhāvīti ca viśeṣvate /
"dhīrdhāraṇāvatī medhā" iti ca naighaṇṭukāḥ /
adhīmahe ca-- "medhāmanīṣe mā viśatāṃ samīcīna bhūtasya bhavyasyāvaruddhyai" iti /
children.translated_text: And we recite [the Vedic prayer]: "May <s>medhā</s> (intelligence) and <s>manīṣā</s> (deep thought) enter me, for the securing of the past and the future."

children.text: yaddhā muktaprāyātyantaniṣpannayogapuruṣaviṣayametat; na hi tasya śāstreṇa jñātavyaṃ tadānīmasti, sākṣātkṛtasamastatattvārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: Or else this [statement about abandoning texts] pertains to a person who has nearly attained liberation, whose <s>yoga</s> is fully accomplished; for such a person has nothing more to learn from <s>śāstra</s> at that point, since he has directly realized the meaning of all truths.
As for what is recorded: "Scriptural learning is full of hardship and is a cause of mental agitation;
Having understood <s>Hari</s> through instruction, one should withdraw from all [other] activities."

That is intended [to refer to the abandonment of] the outer husk [of textual study]; for a person whose intellectual capacity has been perfected through the accumulation of refined impressions gained with diligent and sharp [study] has nothing further to accomplish with the husk.
And he is specified as "wise" (<s>medhāvin</s>).
The etymologists say: "<s>Medhā</s> is intelligence possessed of retention."

children.text: iti, idaṃ tu tīvrasaṃvegināmalasāstikānāṃ ca grāhmam; buddhicalanahetūnāmasacchāstrāṇāṃ tyāgārthaṃ vā; tadā viśeṣaṇasāphalyam; dharmavidyāsthāneṣvapi hi bahirdaleṣvatisaṃrambho mumukṣorapodyate--- "na śabdaśāstrābhiratasya mokṣo na caiva ramyāvasathapriyasya /
children.translated_text: This is to be accepted by those of intense urgency and by those who are pure-minded devotees; or it is intended for the abandonment of false scriptures that cause mental agitation — in that case, the qualifying term ["mental agitation"] has its proper significance. For even in the domains of <s>dharmavidyā</s> (knowledge of duty), excessive engagement with the outer petals [i.e., subsidiary disciplines] is deprecated for the seeker of liberation: "There is no liberation for one absorbed in grammar, nor for one fond of pleasant dwellings,
Nor for one devoted to food and clothing, nor for one delighting in captivating people's minds."

children.text: iti, tat śābdaṃ prameyatattvamadhijigamiṣatāṃ pramāṇeṣu sāram, tadabhāve puṃsaḥ paśubhiḥ samatvaprasaṅgāt iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, for those who wish to attain the reality of what is to be known, verbal testimony is the essence among the means of knowledge; for in its absence, there would be the absurd consequence of a person being equal to animals.
He whose command is a she-pigeon dwelling on the sole palace-pinnacle of the <s>Vedas</s>, at whose mere play of the brow the thrones of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s> become obedient,

children.text: yaḥ sarvatra yathāpuraṃ vitanute nāmāni viśvākṛti- rnityaṃ naḥ pratibhātu sarvavacasāṃ niṣṭhā sa nārāyaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: He who, as the form of the universe, extends names everywhere as of old — may that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the ultimate ground of all words, ever shine in our minds.

children.text: iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntānacāryasya kṛtiṣunyāyapariśuddhau śabdādhyāye dvitīyamāhnikam //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the works of <s>Śrīmad Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the lion among poets and logicians, independent master of all systems, teacher of <s>Vedānta</s>, in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in the <s>Śabdādhyāya</s> (Chapter on Verbal Testimony), the second <s>āhnika</s> (daily lesson) [is concluded].
And the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) is complete.
<s>Smṛtyadhyāya</s> (Chapter on Tradition/Smṛti)
First <s>āhnika</s> (daily lesson).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 49 atha smṛtirnirūpyate--- saṃskāramātrajaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ, iti tallakṣaṇam /
nanu smṛtirna pramāṇam, avidyamānaviṣayatvāt, ananubhūtitvāt, bhramasambhavocceti cenna, smṛtimātrāprāmāṇyasya prathamāhnikre pratikṣiptatvāt, avādhitabāhyārthadarśanāt, atītānāgataviṣayānumānādibādhaprasaṅgāt, sarvalokavirodhāt, ananubhūte arthāntarepi smṛtiprasaṅgāt, smṛterapi svaprakāśatvepi vedyākāre saṃskārādisāpekṣatvāt /
na ca pūrvānubhavapuraskāreṇaiva grahaṇādaprāmāṇyamiti cenna, smṛtipramoṣe tadabhāvāt, pramāṇatayā saṃmatāyāṃ pratyabhijñāyāṃ bhāvācca /
paratantratvādapramāṇyamiti cenna, svahetupāratantryamātrasya sārvatrikatvāt, anubhavamūlatvasya pramāṇamūlatvasya ca savikalpakādibhiranaikāntikatvāt, saṃskāramātrajanyatvasyāsādhāraṇatvāt, svaviṣayaprakāśavyavahārayostu smṛterapi svatantratvāt /
icchādivadviṣayaniyamepi pāratantryamastīti cenna, tadvadevājñānatvaprasaṅgāt; jñānameva hi svato viṣayapravaṇamicchasi; ata eva hi nityayorapi riśvaracikīrṣāprayatnayorviṣaya niyamāya jñānāpekṣāṃ brūṣe /
icchādīnāmapi svato viṣayaprāvaṇyaṃ jñānatvaṃ cāsmābhiḥ svīkṛtam /
nanu saṃskāravaditi cenna, tasyāpi svahetusamānaviṣayajñānotpādanaśaktasvabhāvatvāt /
ato hetuniyataviṣayatvameva phalitam /
tacca anubhavepi samam /
tathā ca samānaviṣayānubhavajanyatvatadabhāvābhyāṃ smṛtyanubhavayoḥ pāratantryasvātantryavyavahāro mandānām /
svaprāmāṇyanirṇayādāvapi nānubhavāpekṣatvanirbandhaḥ, svaviṣayaprakāśanabādhavirahādibhisatatsiddheḥ, gṛhītamātragrāhitvasyāsādhāraṇatvāt /
prābhākarāṇāmanumānādau naiyāyikādīnāṃ dhārāvāhikādau yogasiddhasarvajñavādināṃ dvitīyayogapratyakṣādau keṣāñcidīśvaravādināmanityeśvarajñāne ca vyabhicārācca /
niṣprayojanatvādaprāmāṇyamiti cenna, tṛṇādiviṣayapratnayakṣādinānaikāntyāt, asiddheśca;smṛtyaiva hi jagatāṃ kṛtākṛtapratyavekṣaṇādisiddhiḥ; smṛtyaiva hi śabdānumānayoḥ pravṛtiḥ; parabhaktyādiniṣpattiśca /
pūrvānubhuvasyaiva tāniprayojanānīticet, sarvajagadādikāraṇasya brahmasaṃkalpasyaiva kiṃ na syuḥ ? /
children.translated_text: If it be said that those purposes belong to the prior experience itself — then why should they not belong to the volition of <s>Brahman</s>, which is the cause of the entire universe and everything else?

children.text: evaṃ cānubhavasyāpi na tatsiddhiḥ, tatkāraṇasyeti vaktuṃ śakyatvāt /
