children.translated_text: In that case, even for direct experience those purposes would not be established, since one could equally say they belong to its cause.
As stated in the <s>Prajñāparitrāṇa</s> — "Because it has the nature of knowledge whose object is already known, and because it relinquishes what is to be its own object of proof,
even though it does not deviate from its object, <s>smṛti</s> is held to be invalid as a <s>pramāṇa</s>."

Nyāyapariśuddhi, Section 49. Now <s>smṛti</s> (memory) is examined — "Knowledge born solely from <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) is <s>smṛti</s>" — such is its definition.
If it be objected that <s>smṛti</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), because it has a non-existent object, because it is not direct experience, and because error is possible — no, because the invalidity of all <s>smṛti</s> without exception has been refuted in the first <s>āhnika</s> (chapter); because there is perception of an unsublated external object; because there would be the absurd consequence of sublating <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and other means regarding past and future objects; because it would contradict all people's practice; because there would be the absurd consequence of <s>smṛti</s> arising even regarding objects never experienced; and because even though <s>smṛti</s> is self-luminous, it depends on <s>saṃskāra</s> and other factors with respect to the form of the object to be known.
Nor can it be said that it is invalid because it apprehends only with reference to a prior experience — no, because in the case of <s>smṛtipramoṣa</s> (lapse of memory) that prior experience is absent, and because <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), which is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, also involves such reference.
If it be said that it is invalid because of dependence on another — no, because mere dependence on one's own cause is universal to all knowledge; because the argument from being rooted in experience or rooted in a <s>pramāṇa</s> is inconclusive, as shown by <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate cognition) and similar cases; because being produced solely from <s>saṃskāra</s> is a distinguishing feature, not a defect; and because with respect to illuminating its own object and generating practical activity, <s>smṛti</s> too is independent.
If it be said that even with restriction to a definite object, there is dependence, as with desire and so forth — no, because by that very reasoning there would be the absurd consequence that desire too is not knowledge; for you yourself hold that knowledge alone is inherently directed toward objects; and it is precisely for this reason that you say even the eternally existent will and effort of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) require knowledge for the determination of their objects.
We accept that desire and the rest also have inherent directedness toward objects and are themselves forms of knowledge.
If it be said "just as with <s>saṃskāra</s>" — no, because <s>saṃskāra</s> itself has the nature of a power to produce knowledge having the same object as its own cause.
Therefore what follows is simply that the object is determined by the cause,
and this is equally true of direct experience as well.
Accordingly, the conventional usage of "dependence" for <s>smṛti</s> and "independence" for <s>anubhava</s> (experience), on the basis of being produced from an experience of the same object or the absence thereof, is for those of limited understanding.
Even in establishing intrinsic validity, there is no insistence on independence from experience, since that is established through the illumination of one's own object, absence of sublation, and so forth; and because being a cognizer of only what has already been grasped is not a universally applicable distinguishing mark —
as shown by the deviation in the case of <s>anumāna</s> and other means for the <s>Prābhākaras</s>, in <s>dhārāvāhika</s> (continuous stream) cognition and the like for the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, in the second <s>yogapratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception) for those who hold the doctrine of omniscient beings perfected through yoga, and in the non-eternal knowledge of <s>Īśvara</s> for certain theists.
If it be said that it is invalid because it serves no purpose — no, because this is inconclusive given direct perceptions of trivial objects like grass and so forth; and because the claim is unestablished — for it is through <s>smṛti</s> alone that people accomplish the review of what has been done and what has not been done; it is through <s>smṛti</s> alone that <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) operate; and the attainment of <s>parabhakti</s> (supreme devotion) and the rest also depends on it.

children.text:
ityādi, tadapyanena parihṛtam /
pramāṇavyavahārābhāvādaprāmāṇyamiti cenna, pāmaravyavadvārābhāvasyānaikāntikatvāt, evaṃ parīkṣakavyavahāra bhāvasyāpi; vigītatvācca; sarvaparīkṣakavyavahārābhāvasya cāsiddheḥ; mānamanoharādau vāgīśvarādibhistaprāmāṇyasyoktatvāt, katipayaparīkṣakavyahārābhāvasya cātiprasañjakatvāt, akṣapādādivyahārāvyavahārayorbṛhaspatyādivyavahāravadasmābhirnātīvādaraṇāt, indrapāṇinyādīnāṃ tu sarvasaṃpratipatterabādhāccādarāt, pārāśaryādīnāṃ pramāṇaparigaṇanānadhikṛtatvena tadanukteraprayojakatvāt, āgamaḥ pramāṇamityapi vyavahārābhāvāt /
"pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam /
ityādiṣu ca pratyakṣādimūlasmṛteḥ pratyakṣādisamānacarcatvena pṛthagvyavahārābhāvopapatteḥ /
pramāṇahetukā smṛtiḥ pramāṇameva, avisaṃvādāt, iti /
uktaṃ ca nyāyatattve smṛtyudāsīnabhedake caturthedhikaraṇe--- "apramāṇamūlatvaṃ tu ubhayorapi nāsti, vyabhicārābhāvenānadhigatārthaṃ pramāṇamiti viśeṣaṇasyāyuktatvāt /

children.translated_text: Where is it seen that valid cognition is impossible regarding what has already been validly cognized?

children.text: smṛtau cet, pratijñaiva dṛṣṭāntaḥ syāt; jñānāntare cenna nujānāmi" ityādi /
children.translated_text: If in <s>smṛti</s> — then the thesis itself would become the example; if in some other cognition — I do not know of such" — and so forth.
And in the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s> — "A determination that accords with reality is a <s>māna</s> (valid means), as is its cause — so say the learned.

children.text: nātivyāptiḥ smṛtau vyāptiryathārthena hi sā pramā" //
children.translated_text: There is no over-extension to <s>smṛti</s>; rather the extension is proper, for that <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is indeed one that accords with reality."

And so forth — that too has been answered by the foregoing.
If it be said that it is invalid because of the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>-usage — no, because the absence of usage among ordinary people is inconclusive, and likewise the presence of usage among critical examiners is also inconclusive; and because the matter is disputed; and because the absence of usage among all examiners is unestablished; and because in works such as the <s>Mānamanoharā</s>, <s>Vāgīśvara</s> and others have stated its validity; and because the absence of usage among only some examiners proves too much; and because we do not attach great weight to either the usage or non-usage of <s>Akṣapāda</s> and others, just as we do not to that of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and others; but we do respect <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pāṇini</s>, and others because of universal agreement and non-sublation; and because the non-mention by <s>Parāśara</s> and others is inconsequential since they were not engaged in enumerating <s>pramāṇas</s>; and because there is also no usage of the statement "<s>āgama</s> (scripture) is a <s>pramāṇa</s>" as such.
In passages such as "Perception, inference, and scripture of various traditions" and so forth, since <s>smṛti</s> rooted in perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s> is discussed on the same level as perception and the rest, the absence of separate mention is explained.
<s>Smṛti</s> that is caused by a <s>pramāṇa</s> is itself a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because it is non-deceptive — thus it is stated.
And it has been said in the <s>Nyāyatattva</s>, in the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> which distinguishes <s>smṛti</s> from what is neutral to it — "The absence of an invalid source is true of both; because in the absence of deviation, the qualifier 'having an object not previously known' in the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is unjustified.

children.text: ityuktvā asyottarārdhavivaraṇepyuktam--- "anubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ; yathā---sa ghaṭa ati /
children.translated_text: Having said this, it is also stated in the commentary on the latter half of this verse — "<s>Smṛti</s> is the non-loss of an object that has been experienced; as for example — 'That is a pot.'

children.text: nanu tāmapi vyāpnoti lakṣaṇamya ; satyam; tadvyāptau nātivyāptiḥ, tasyāpi lakṣyapakṣe nikṣepāt /
children.translated_text: If it be objected that the definition also extends to that (<s>smṛti</s>) — yes, it does; but in extending to it there is no over-extension, because <s>smṛti</s> too is included within the class of what is to be defined.
"How can a definition be applied while disregarding what is to be defined and what is not to be defined?
The wise know that the boundary between what is to be defined and what is not extends up to the conventions of ordinary cognition and usage."

children.text:
ityādi /
yattu--- "anubhavaḥ pramāṇam /
smṛtivyatiriktaṃ jñānamanubhavaḥ" ityādinā smṛteraprāmāṇyamuktamiva śrīviṣṇucittaiḥ, tannūnaṃ paramatānvāroheṇa /
ata eva hi taiḥ svataḥ prāmāṇyanirṇayadaśāyāmanyathā vyavahṛtam /
tathāhi--- "tasmāt siddhametat pramāṇānāṃ yathārthatvalakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ guṇajñānānapekṣāt svapramāṇādevāvasīyate, svakīyāt kāraṇādeva jñāyata iti ca" iti /
tathā "arthatathātvaṃ guṇasaṃvādajñānānapekṣajñapti, tadabhāvepi jñāyamānatvāt" ityādau /
"na ca hetorasiddhatvam; tathāhi--- rajatajñānasyārthatathātvaṃ nāma rajataviṣayatvam; taccāsati bādhake rajatagrāhiṇaiva jñānenāvagamyate" ityādi /
ato yathāvasthitavastuniścayātmakatvameva prāmāṇyaṃ pramāṇajñānānāmātmīyāt kāraṇājjñāyate, na guṇasaṃvādajñānamapekṣate, iti /
tathā pramāṇānāṃ yathāvasthitavastuniścayātmakatvameva prāmāṇyam /
tadābhāsayuktayaḥ pūrvapakṣiṇocyante /
siddhāntepi vivekapradarśanameveti /
yadi cānubhava eva pramāṇam, tanna yuktamupayuktaṃ vā /
na ca sarvamanubhavaṃ pramāṇatayā vyavaharanti, pītaśaṅkhabhramādiṣvadarśanāt; nāpi sarvāṃ smṛtimapramāṇatayā, pramāṇamūlasmṛtiṣu tadabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For people do not treat all <s>anubhava</s> as valid, as seen in the case of illusions such as a yellow conch-shell and the like; nor do they treat all <s>smṛti</s> as invalid, since that is not the case for <s>smṛti</s> rooted in a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
The statement of <s>Varada Viṣṇumiśra</s> that "a <s>pramāṇa</s> is that which has the capacity to grasp what has not yet been grasped" should also be understood as following the opponent's position.
As for what was stated in the <s>Āgamaprāmāṇya</s> — "An intellect that pervades objects seen by other <s>pramāṇas</s>,

children.text: pramāṇameva tatpūrvaṃ na cet svārthaṃ vigāhate" //
children.translated_text: if it does not independently apprehend its own object, is itself a <s>pramāṇa</s> only derivatively" —

And so forth.
As for what was stated by <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> in such passages as — "<s>Anubhava</s> (experience) is a <s>pramāṇa</s>; knowledge other than <s>smṛti</s> is <s>anubhava</s>" — which appears to declare the invalidity of <s>smṛti</s>, that must surely be understood as following the opponent's position.
For it is precisely for this reason that he himself has spoken otherwise in the context of establishing intrinsic validity.
Thus — "Therefore it is established that the <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) of the <s>pramāṇas</s>, characterized as accordance with reality, is ascertained from the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself without depending on knowledge of its excellences — that is, it is known from its own cause alone."
And likewise — "The accordance of the object with reality is a cognition that does not depend on knowledge of corroborating qualities, since it is known even in the absence of such" — and so forth.
"Nor is the reason unestablished; for the accordance with reality of the cognition of silver, namely its having silver as its object, is apprehended, in the absence of a sublating cognition, by the very cognition that grasps silver" — and so forth.
Therefore, <s>prāmāṇya</s> is precisely the nature of being a determination of a thing as it actually exists, and this is known for <s>pramāṇa</s>-cognitions from their own cause, without depending on knowledge of corroborating correspondence.
Likewise, the <s>prāmāṇya</s> of the <s>pramāṇas</s> is precisely the nature of being a determination of a thing as it actually exists.
The arguments that would appear to deny this are stated by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector).
Even in the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), the purpose is merely to demonstrate the distinction.
And if only <s>anubhava</s> were a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that would be neither logically sound nor practically useful.

children.text: iti, idamapyanuvādavākyasyānyaparatayā svārthaprāmāṇyavyavacchedārtham; anyathā smṛtipramoṣe pramuṣitatadaṃśe pūrvānubhavapuraskāreṇa svārthāvagāhanāsiddheḥ kathaṃ tatra smṛtitvanibandhanamaprāmāṇyaṃ bhaviṣyati ? //
children.translated_text: this too is meant, by construing the quoted statement as subordinate to another point, to exclude independent <s>prāmāṇya</s> for its own object; otherwise, in the case of <s>smṛtipramoṣa</s> (lapse of memory), where that portion has been forgotten, and apprehension of one's own object through reference to the prior experience is not established, how could invalidity be based on the mere fact of being <s>smṛti</s>?

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 50 yattu bhāṣye sanmātragrāhipratyakṣanirākaraṇadaśāyāmuktam-- "aśve hastini ca saṃvedanayorekaviṣayatvenoparitanasya gṛhītagrāhitvād viśeṣābhāvācca smṛtivailakṣaṇyaṃ na syāt" iti, na tatra smṛteraprāmāṇyaṃ sūcitam, prakārāntareṇāpi vailakṣaṇyasiddheḥ, tadapekṣayā ca prasaṅgopapatteḥ /
yaccāparaṃ bhāṣyam--- "indriyajanmanaḥ pratyakṣasya hyeṣa svabhāvaniyamaḥ, yat svasamakālavartinaḥ padārthasya grāhakatvam, na tu sarveṣāṃ jñānānāṃ pramāṇānāṃ ca, smaraṇānumānāgamayogipratyakṣādiṣu kālāntaravartinopi grahaṇadarśanāt" ityādi, tatrāpi parasyāniṣṭaprasaṅgāya tadabhiprāyānudhāvanena vibhajyodāharaṇaṃ yuktam /

yacca śāstrayonyadhikaraṇe bhāṣitam--- "bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajanmanastasya viśadāvabhāsatvepi pūrvānubhūtaviṣayasmṛtimātratvānna prāmāṇyamiti kutaḥ pratyakṣatā ?" iti, idamapi na sākṣāt siddhāntastham; na ca yāthārthyaṃ tatra pratikṣiptam /
children.translated_text: And what was stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>Śāstrayoni</s> (Scripture-as-source) <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — "Even though that cognition born at the culmination of intense meditation has vivid manifestation, since it is merely <s>smṛti</s> having a previously experienced object, it has no <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) — so how can it be <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception)?" — this too does not directly represent the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion); nor is the veridicality of <s>smṛti</s> denied there.
Other passages too should be understood in this manner.
Even the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, who maintain the invalidity of <s>smṛti</s> as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, classify it under <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) on account of its veridicality.

children.text: tata eva ca tadekadeśibhirapi tatprāmāṇyaṃ svīkṛtam, iti //
children.translated_text: And it is precisely for this reason that those who partially share their view have also accepted its <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity).

Nyāyapariśuddhi, Section 50. As for what was stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> in the context of refuting the view that perception grasps only bare existence — "If the cognitions of a horse and an elephant had the same object, then since the latter cognition would grasp what was already grasped and there would be no distinction, there would be no difference from <s>smṛti</s>" — the invalidity of <s>smṛti</s> is not indicated there, since the difference can be established by other means as well, and the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) is justified with reference to that.
And the other passage in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — "For <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), which is born from the senses, this is the natural restriction: that it grasps an object existing at the same time as itself; but this is not true of all cognitions and all <s>pramāṇas</s>, since in <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembering), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>āgama</s> (scripture), <s>yogipratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception), and the like, we observe the grasping of objects existing at other times" — there too, it is proper to understand the division and examples as following the opponent's intended meaning for the purpose of drawing out an undesirable consequence for the opponent.

children.text: iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu nyāyapariśuddhau smṛtyadhyāye prathamamāhnikam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>āhnika</s> (chapter) of the <s>Smṛtyadhyāya</s> (Chapter on Memory) in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, a work of <s>Śrīmad Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the <s>Vedāntācārya</s> (teacher of <s>Vedānta</s>), known as <s>Kavitārkikasiṃha</s> (Lion among Poets and Logicians) and <s>Sarvatantrasvatantra</s> (Independent Master of All Sciences).
The <s>Smṛtyadhyāya</s> (Chapter on Memory).
Second <s>āhnika</s> (chapter).

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 51 evaṃ tāvadvivecitaṃ pramāṇam /
cārvākāstu pratyakṣamekaṃ pramāṇamityāhuḥ /
teṣveva kecit anumānasya pratyakṣentarbhāvamicchanti; kecittu aprāmāṇyam; pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca kāṇādāḥ saugatāśca /
tatra pūrve śabdasyānumānentarbhāvamāhuḥ; pare tu kecit antarbhāvam; kecidaprāmāṇyam; te cāgamaṃ ca sāṃkhyāḥ, bhūṣaṇamatānuvartinaśca /
tatra vedasyānāditvaṃ pūrve parijagṛhuḥ; uttare tvīśvarasṛṣṭatām; tāni ca smṛtiṃ ca vaiśeṣikaikadeśinosmatsiddhāntaikadeśinaśca; tānyeva sārthāpattikāni prābhākarāḥ; anupalabdhiṣaṣṭhāni tānyeva tautātitāḥ, tatpralobhanarucayo māyāvādinaśca; tānyeva saṃbhavatihyayuktāni purāṇaśaraṇāḥ /
adyatanapramāṇaparigrahopalambhaprakriyeyam /
anante pūrvāparakāle kaḥ kimaṅgīkuryāt, kiṃ vā bahiṣkuryāt, iti ko jānātyanyatra kalpasākṣātkāriṇastasmādekasmāddevāt /
iha ca nyūnavādinastadavasare nirastāḥ /
adhikatayā parābhimatānāṃ tu arntabhāvo vaktavyaḥ /
tatra yathā pratyabhijñādīnāṃ pratyakṣādiṣveva niveśa iṣyate, evamanyeṣāmapi /
pratyabhijñā tāvat grahaṇātmikaivetyeke; tathāhi--- "pratyabhijñāyāmapi smṛtiranubhava ityaṃśabhedosti cet" ityāśaṅkya pratyuktaṃ śrīviṣṇucittaiḥ--- "yadi viṣayabhedaḥ, tadā aṃśabhedaḥ saṃbhavet; aikyameva hi niraṃśaṃ pratyabhijñāpratyakṣaviṣayaḥ /
kathaṃ saṃskāraḥaparokṣadhījanakaḥ iti cet, na, cakṣurādīndriyasahakṛtasya saṃskārasya jñāturaikyāt tadidamityaparokṣadhīhetutvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: If it be asked how <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) can generate immediate cognition — no, because <s>saṃskāra</s> assisted by the sense organs such as the eye, since it belongs to the same knowing subject, can reasonably be the cause of immediate cognition of the form 'that is this.'
It is the establisher of the identity of an immediately present object.
That <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), having the form 'this is indeed that very person,'
is not <s>smṛti</s> because it is not born from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone — it is itself a <s>pramāṇa</s>."

Nyāyapariśuddhi, Section 51. Thus far, <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) has been examined.
The <s>Cārvākas</s> hold that <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) alone is a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Among them, some accept the inclusion of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) within <s>pratyakṣa</s>; others hold its invalidity. The <s>Kāṇādas</s> (Vaiśeṣikas) and the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) accept <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>.
Among them, the former assert the inclusion of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) within <s>anumāna</s>; among the latter, some accept inclusion, others hold its invalidity. The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, and those following the view of <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s>, accept those plus <s>āgama</s> (scripture).
Among them, the former accepted the beginninglessness of the <s>Veda</s>; the latter, that it was created by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). Those plus <s>smṛti</s> are accepted by certain <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> sub-schools and certain sub-schools of our own <s>siddhānta</s>. Those very ones together with <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) are accepted by the <s>Prābhākaras</s>. Those very ones with <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) as the sixth are accepted by the <s>Tātparyavādins</s> (Bhāṭṭas), those inclined to that view, and the <s>Māyāvādins</s> (Advaitins). Those very ones together with <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion), <s>itihāsa</s> (tradition), and <s>yukti</s> (reasoning) are accepted by those who take the <s>Purāṇas</s> as their authority.
This is the survey of the acceptance of <s>pramāṇas</s> at the present time.
In the infinite stretch of past and future time, who would accept what and who would reject what — who knows, other than that one <s>Deva</s> (God) who directly witnesses all the <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles)?
Here, those who accept fewer <s>pramāṇas</s> have been refuted at the appropriate places.
As for those accepted additionally by others, their inclusion within the established <s>pramāṇas</s> must be stated.
Just as <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) and the like are held to be included within <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, so too for the others.
Regarding <s>pratyabhijñā</s>, some hold that it is purely an act of apprehension. Thus, when the doubt is raised — "Even in <s>pratyabhijñā</s>, is there not a division of aspects, namely <s>smṛti</s> and <s>anubhava</s>?" — <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> replied — "If there were a difference of objects, then there could be a difference of aspects; but identity itself, which is without parts, is the object of the <s>pratyabhijñā</s>-perception.

children.text:
iti /
dīpe ca 'anusmṛteśca' iti sūtre bhāṣitam- "pratyabhijñānācca na paṭādeḥ kṣaṇikatvam; tadevedamiti pratyabhijñāyate; pratyabhijñā hi nāmātītavartamānakālavartyekavastuviṣayamekaṃ pratyakṣajñānam /
tasya kāladvayasambandhāviśiṣṭamekameva vastu viṣayaḥ /
na ca tadityaṃśaḥ smaraṇam, idamaṃśaśca grahaṇam, atītasambandhinīndriyasaṃprayogābhāvāt iti vācyam, tadidamiti sāmānādhikaraṇyena grahaṇasyaikatvasphuraṇāt /
pūrvānubhavajanitasaṃskārasacivendriyasaṃprayogayuktasya puruṣasya tathā grahaṇamupapadyata eva; anvayavyatirekādhīnaṃ hi sarvatra sāmagrīparikalpanam" iti /
anye tu atra dhībhedabāddhyaparihārau matvā tadidamaṃśayostadaṃśe saṃskārānvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanāt parokṣarūpatayā idamaṃśe ca patyakṣarūpatayā cobhayātmakatvamāhuḥ /
tanmate saṃskārādhīnaprakāśā smṛtiriti lakṣaṇam, aparokṣajñānaṃ pratyakṣam, ubhayalakṣaṇayogāt pratyabhijñāyāmubhayātmakatvam, iti /
abhyupagantavyaṃ cāsmatsiddhāntibhiḥ sarvaiḥ pratyakṣetarajñānānāṃ parokṣāparokṣarūpatvam, svayaṃprakāśatvāt, sarvajñānānāṃ vedyetarāṃśāpekṣayā ca pratyakṣatvāt /

uktaṃ cedaṃ śrīviṣṇucittairapi --- "svaprakāśakaṃ viṣayaprakāśakaṃ caikameva jñānam; tatra smṛtriranubhūtiriti kuto bhedaḥ ?" iti paricodya, "prakāśamānabhedāt, iti brūmaḥ; yathā--- gaurayamityekasminneva jñāne prakāriprakāraviṣayabhedena jñānāṃśabhedaḥ; yathā--- gaurayamityekasminneva jñāne prakāriprakāraviṣayabhedena jñānāṃśabhedaḥ; yathā ca ghaṭapaṭāvityekasminneva jñāneṃśabhedaḥ; yathā vā parābhyupagatabhramajñāneṣvadhiṣṭhānāṃśe prāmāṇyam, itaratrāprāmāṇyaṃ ca" iti parihārāt; tathā "smṛteḥ svaprakāśāṃśopi saṃskāramātraja eva, indriyādipratiniyatakāraṇāntarābhāvāt" iti paricodya "naivam, jñānānāṃ prakāśamānatvasya svābhāvikatvāt" iti parihārācca /
children.translated_text: And this has been stated by <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> as well — having raised the objection: "Knowledge is one and the same, being both self-luminous and object-illuminating; therein, whence the distinction between <s>smṛti</s> (memory) and <s>anubhūti</s> (direct experience)?" the answer was given: "From the difference in what is illuminated, we say; just as in the single cognition 'this is a white [cow],' there is a difference of aspects of knowledge due to the difference between the qualificand, the qualifier, and the object; just as in the single cognition 'this is a white [cow],' there is a difference of aspects of knowledge due to the difference between the qualificand, the qualifier, and the object; and just as in the single cognition '[there are] a pot and a cloth,' there is a difference of aspects; or just as in erroneous cognitions accepted by the opponent, there is validity in the substrate-aspect and invalidity in the other" — thus by this resolution; and likewise, having raised the objection: "Even the self-luminous aspect of <s>smṛti</s> (memory) is produced merely from impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), because of the absence of any other cause restricted to the sense organs and so forth," the answer was given: "Not so, because the luminous nature of cognitions is intrinsic."
Therefore, everywhere the distinction into directness (<s>aparokṣatva</s>), inferentiality (<s>anumititva</s>), memoriality (<s>smṛtitva</s>), and so forth is made only with reference to the object.
But the intermixture or non-intermixture of universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like is to be determined by observation and non-observation, just as with adventitious intermixture and the like.
Thus, since the dual nature [of pratyabhijña as both perception and memory] is established, <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) too is of a dual nature.

Thus it is stated.
And in the <s>Dīpa</s> (commentary), on the <s>sūtra</s> 'and from recollection,' it is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — "From <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) too, momentariness of cloth and other objects is disproved; for it is recognized that 'this is that very thing.' <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> is indeed a single <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perceptual) cognition having as its object one and the same entity persisting across past and present times. Its object is a single entity undifferentiated by its relation to two times. Nor can it be said that the 'that'-aspect is remembering and the 'this'-aspect is perception, on the ground that there is no sense-contact with what is related to a past time — because the apprehension as 'that is this,' through co-referentiality, manifests unity. Such apprehension is perfectly explained for a person who possesses sense-contact assisted by <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) born from prior experience; for everywhere the determination of the causal aggregate depends on co-presence and co-absence."
Others, however, considering that this view faces the difficulties of denying the distinction of cognitions and of explaining it away, hold that since in the 'that'-aspect and 'this'-aspect one observes the co-variation of the 'that'-aspect with <s>saṃskāra</s>, it has a mediate nature in that aspect, and since the 'this'-aspect has an immediate nature, <s>pratyabhijñā</s> has a dual nature.
On that view, the definition is: <s>smṛti</s> is cognition whose manifestation depends on <s>saṃskāra</s>; <s>pratyakṣa</s> is immediate cognition; and <s>pratyabhijñā</s>, possessing the characteristics of both definitions, has a dual nature.
But it must be accepted by all proponents of our <s>siddhānta</s> that all cognitions, whether perceptual or otherwise, have both mediate and immediate aspects — because of their self-luminous nature, and because all cognitions are perceptual with respect to the aspect other than the object to be known.

children.text: nyā. pa. śa. 52 pratyabhijñāpyabhijñāvat tridhā cākṣādibhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 52. <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), like <s>abhijñā</s> (initial cognition), is threefold according to the distinction of sensory and other [sources],
and becomes ninefold because it is rooted in the combination of the respective <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions).
The statement that [recognition is] perceptual, as in the case of a lamp and so on, should be understood as intended for illustration.

children.text: na hi liṅgādibhiḥ soyamiti jñānaṃ na jāyate //
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that a cognition of the form "this is the same one" does not arise through <s>liṅga</s> (inferential marks) and the like.
Recognition born of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) operates by depending upon [prior cognition],
and the principle of the <s>śākhāntara</s>-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of different Vedic branches) [applies] in the case of both <s>kratu</s> (ritual) and <s>vidyā</s> (meditation).
Just as in the case of a lamp and the like, everywhere, because of the impossibility of a sublating cognition and the like,
<s>pratyabhijñāna</s> (recognition), though disputed, is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), just like <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate cognition).
Due to the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) of temporal difference and the like between doing and not-doing,
since there is no contradiction, one cannot postulate difference in a seed and the like.
Otherwise, by spatial difference, by doing and not-doing, and so forth,

children.text: ekaṃ jagati naiva syāditi syāt sarvaśūnyatā //
children.translated_text: nothing in the world would be one — and thus there would be universal voidness (<s>sarvaśūnyatā</s>).
Therefore, through the recognition of objects that are in contact with contradictory [properties],
the permanence of the selves (<s>ātman</s>) is established, and the reality of external objects as well.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 53 pratisandhānamapyātmagocaraṃ pratyabhijñāviśeṣa eva; yohamadrākṣaṃ sa eva spṛśāmi, ityevamādirūpatvāt /
pratisandhirarthadvayaviṣayaikabuddhirityeke /
tatrāpi pṛthaganubhūtānekārthagocaraikakartṛkaikabuddhiriti pūraṇīyam, iti /
saṃvādo nāma jñānajātyantaram, iti kecit; tadayuktam, saṃkhyāntarāsaṃbhavāt /
yattu varadaviṣṇumiśrairuktam--- "gṛhītārthaviṣayaṃ śabdakāraṇakaṃ jñānaṃ saṃvādaḥ" iti, tadapi śābdāvāntarabhede saṃjñāviśeṣaniveśamātraparam;"na hi gṛhītārthaviṣayatve śabdaśaktiprasūtatvamapaiti; gṛhītamātragocarapramāṇāntarepi tadanyatvaprasaṅgāt; bhavati hi parvatoyamagnimāniti śabdaśravaṇānantaraṃ dhūmaṃ parāmṛśatopi tādṛśī buddhiḥ /

children.translated_text: The same should be seen in the case of a second yogic perception and the like as well.
And the [objection of] non-dependence and so forth applies equally to inference and the like whose object is something already known from scripture.

children.text: na cāpekṣāyuktaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ bhedobhedo vā, tṛṇādipratyakṣasyāpi tathā prasaṅgāt" ityuktam /
children.translated_text: "Nor is it the case that validity or difference-and-identity is [vitiated] by dependence, since even perception of grass and the like would have the same unwanted consequence" — thus it has been stated.

children.text: kimarthaṃ tarhi vedānāṃ vedāntānāṃ cāprāptaviṣayatvaṃ samarthyate ? iti cet, atathāprāptau sākṣādaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt; tathāprāptāvapi anapekṣitatayā prekṣāvadbhirnirarthakaprayāsabhīrubhistyājyatvāpātena phalatoprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt, iti paśya //
children.translated_text: If one asks: for what purpose then is the thesis maintained that the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedānta</s> have objects not otherwise attainable? — [the answer is:] because if the objects were not thus unattainable, there would be the direct consequence of invalidity; and even if the objects were thus unattainable, because of the apparent consequence that, being non-dependent [on other means], they would be discardable by prudent persons who fear fruitless effort — there would be the consequence of invalidity in terms of result. Consider this carefully.

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 53. <s>Pratisandhāna</s> (recollective synthesis) too, insofar as it pertains to the self, is simply a special case of <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition); because it has the form "the very I who saw am now touching," and so on.
Some say that <s>pratisandhi</s> is a single cognition whose object is two things. Even there, it should be supplemented thus: it is a single cognition by a single agent, whose object is many things experienced separately.
Some say that <s>saṃvāda</s> (corroboration) is a different genus of cognition; that is incorrect, because no additional numerical category is possible.
As for what <s>Varada Viṣṇumiśra</s> has said — "A cognition whose object is something already apprehended and whose cause is verbal testimony is <s>saṃvāda</s>" — that too is merely intended to assign a special designation to a sub-variety of verbal cognition; "for when the object is something already apprehended, the fact that it is produced by the power of words does not cease; since even in the case of another <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is merely something already grasped, there would be the unwanted consequence of its being something other [than what it is]; for indeed, after hearing the verbal statement 'this mountain has fire,' a person who then cognizes the smoke also has such a cognition."

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 54 upamānamapi yadi gṛhyamāṇapadārthagatasādṛśyavijñānāt smaryamāṇapadārthagatasādṛśyavijñānam, tadā smṛtiḥ, tattadvastusaṃsthānaviśeṣādyatiriktasya sādṛśyasyābhāvāt, tasya ca pūrvadṛṣṭatvāt, smaryamāṇatvācca /
vyavahāropyastvapūrvaḥ tattadvyavahāravat pratisambandhaviśeṣaparāmarśopādhikaḥ /
yadvā yo yatsadṛśaḥ, sa tadgatasādṛśyapratiyogī; yathā---mithaḥ svahastau, iti vyāptisiddhau gauretatsadṛśaḥ, etadgatasādṛśyapratiyogitvāt, ityanumānāt smaryamāṇagatasādṛśyāsiddhiḥ; anyathā gṛhyamāṇagatavaisādṛśyajñānāt smaryamāṇagatavaisādṛśyapratītirapi mānāntaraṃ syāt /
sā cet arthāpattiḥ, sādṛśyadhīrapi tathā kiṃ na syāt ? iti /
athavā yugapadeva tatsadṛśoyamiti pratyayenaivobhayavṛttisādṛśyasphuraṇānna taddhetukam, anyathā pṛthaganubhūtayostadānīmapratītasādṛśyayoḥ parastādyugapat smaryamāṇayoryugapadeva pratīyamānasādṛyayoḥko nirvāhaḥ ?, tatrāpi vā pramāṇāntaraṃ kalpyate ? /
yathā gauḥ tathā gavayaḥ, govad dviśapho na bhavatyaśvaḥ, dīrghagrīvaḥ pralamboṣṭho vikaṭākṛtiḥ paśuḥ kramelakaḥ, iti tu sādharmyavaidharmyadharmyamātraviṣayam /

children.translated_text: All three types of <s>atideśa</s> (analogical extension) statements are simply <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony).

children.text: yattu-- "śrutātideśavākyasyagavayādāvatideśavākyārthapratyabhijñānamupamānam, tacca vyutpattiphalakam" iti, tadapyanupapananam, prāgeva vyutpattisiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the view that "the recognition of the meaning of an analogical-extension statement about a <s>gavaya</s> and so forth, upon hearing the analogical-extension statement, is <s>upamāna</s>, and that its result is linguistic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>)" — that too is untenable, because linguistic competence is already established beforehand.
As for the verse: "Because similarity is the occasioning cause, and because the cause is not cognized,
the convention is difficult to grasp initially, whether through word or through inference" —

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 54. As for <s>upamāna</s> (comparison/analogy) — if it is a cognition of similarity residing in a remembered object, arising from the cognition of similarity residing in a presently perceived object, then it is [merely] <s>smṛti</s> (memory), because there is no similarity apart from the specific configuration and the like of each respective object, and because that [similarity] has been previously seen, and because it is being remembered.
Let the resulting practice be novel, like any other practice — being conditioned by the apprehension of a particular relational connection.
Alternatively: whoever is similar to whatever is the counter-correlate of the similarity residing in that thing; just as one's own two hands are [similar] to each other — when such <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion/invariable concomitance) is established, the similarity residing in the remembered object is established by inference: "this cow is similar to that [<s>gavaya</s>], because it is a counter-correlate of the similarity residing in that." Otherwise, a cognition of dissimilarity residing in the remembered object, arising from a cognition of dissimilarity in the perceived object, would also be a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.
If that [dissimilarity cognition] is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), then why should the cognition of similarity not also be the same?
Alternatively, since by the very cognition "this is similar to that" the similarity residing in both is manifest simultaneously, no separate cause is needed; otherwise, for two things experienced separately, whose similarity was not perceived at that time, and which are subsequently remembered simultaneously — when their similarity is perceived simultaneously — what would be the explanation? Would yet another <s>pramāṇa</s> be postulated there too?
Statements like "as is a cow, so is a <s>gavaya</s>" or "a horse, unlike a cow, is not cloven-hoofed" or "a camel is a long-necked, pendulous-lipped, ungainly-shaped animal" are merely about agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>), difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>), and the bare property to be proved (<s>dharmya</s>).

children.text:
iti, tatra nimittasyāpratītitaḥ, iti tvasiddham, gavayatvādereva jātiviśeṣasya gosādṛśyākāropalakṣitasya prathamameva vākyārthatayā pratītiḥ; gosādṛśyākāropalakṣitasya prathamameva vākyārthatayā pratītiḥ; gosādṛśyopalakṣitaḥ kaścid vyaktiviśeṣo gavaya iti hi pratītiḥ /
paścāt pratyakṣitagavayasya tadvaiśadyamātrameva; uktaṃ ca śrīviṣṇucitteḥ--- "gosadṛśo gavayaḥ iti gosādṛśyaikādhikaraṇaṃ sāmānyaṃ vācyamiti vyutpannam, prathamaṃ vākyārthatayā pratīteḥ /
gosādṛśyopalakṣitasyānirṇaye paścādapyanirṇayaḥ /
anyathānirṇaye tathā paścādapi /
tato vākyaśravaṇavelāyāmeva nirṇitam" iti /
evaṃ cānabhyupagame kathaminrdādiśabdavyutpattiḥ ?; na hyatra nimittabhūtasaṃsthānaviśeṣādidṛṣṭiḥ /
na ca nityaṃ tatrāvyutpattiḥ, tadarthaviśiṣṭavākyārthabodhāpātāt /
evaṃ nityātīndriyaviṣayasaṃskārādiśabdānāmapi nityamavyutpattireva syāt /
tatra cet kathañcinnirvāhaḥ, tathātrāpi /
tat siddhaṃ nopamānamatiriktam, iti /
arthāpattistvanumānameva; tathāhi---anupapadyamānadarśanādupapādakakalpanaṃ nāma vyāpyādvyāpakajñānam, avyāpyasya tena vinānupapadyamānatvābhāvāt, avyāpakasya ca tadupapādakatvāyogāt, iti /
pramāṇadvayavirodhe sati viṣayavyavasthāpanamarthāpattiḥ, ityapi na vācyam, pramāṇayoḥ satorvirodhābhāvāt, viruddhayorapi prāmāṇyāyogāt /
nanu devadattasya jīvane kutaścit pramāṇāt pramite, jīvatā kvacit sthātavyam, ityaviśeṣeṇa deśasāmānyasambandhāvagatau gṛhamapyāskandantyāṃ satyāṃ pratyakṣe ca gṛhe tadabhāvaṃ pratipādayati spaṣṭo virodhaḥ, atastacchānyai bahirbhāvakalpanamarthāpattiḥ, iti; maivam, kvaciditi viditasya jīvanasya niyamābhāvāt, bahirvidyamānatāsaṃdehe niścayarūpeṇa gṛhābhāvapratyakṣeṇa pratispardhitumasāmarthyāt /
na ca viruddhaviṣayayorvāstavaṃ kutrāpi samabalatvaṃ samasti;ubhayāprāmāṇye tu kathañcit syāt /
ābhimānikabalasāmyepi tathaiva /
yadā vaiṣamyagrahaḥ, tadā tata eva balābalasiddhau kimarthāpattyā sādhyam ? /
ataḥ kevalaniravakāśavirodhiviśeṣasannidhau sati sāvakāśaṃ sāmānyaṃ saṃkocayitavyamiti vyavasthā syāt /
sāpi ca tathaiva vyāpteḥ, ityanumānaphalameva; anyathā virodhiviṣayatyāga ivāvirodhiviśeṣaparyavasānādāvapi mānāntarakḷptiḥ kiṃ na syāt ? /
evamanabhyupagame ca dhūmānumānādāvapyarthāpattitvaprasaṅgaḥ /
agniṃ vinānupapadyamānatvasvaya liṅgapratyakṣarūpapramāṇadvayavirodhasya ca vaktuṃ śakyatvāt /
dhūmo hi kāraṇabhūtaṃ vahnimākṣipati, pratikṣipati tu pratyakṣam, iti virodhe parvatārvāgbhāge vahniriti vyavasthākalpanasyārthāpattitvaṃ syāt /
vyāptinirūpaṇamantareṇa gamakatā gamakasyaiva dharmāntarayogitayā gamyate ityādibhedāstvāśāmātrakalpitāḥ, iti /

children.translated_text: And <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> has stated: "<s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is [nothing but] <s>anumāna</s> (inference)" — and so on.
Some, however, assign the designation <s>arthāpatti</s> to purely negative inference (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>).
Since that [purely negative inference] has already been refuted earlier, it does not gain entry into the class of <s>pramāṇas</s>.
Or even if it did gain entry, it would not be [counted as] separate.

regarding that, the claim "because the cause is not cognized" is unestablished; for the particular universal (<s>jāti</s>) such as <s>gavayatva</s> (gavaya-hood), which is indicated by the appearance of similarity to a cow, is cognized from the very first as the meaning of the sentence. The cognition is: "A certain particular individual, indicated by similarity to a cow, is a <s>gavaya</s>."
Subsequently, when the <s>gavaya</s> is directly perceived, there is merely the vividness of that [previously cognized meaning]. And <s>Śrī Viṣṇucitta</s> has stated: "'A <s>gavaya</s> is [an animal] similar to a cow' — from this, it is understood through linguistic competence that a universal co-located with cow-similarity is what is denoted, since it is first cognized as the meaning of the sentence.
If what is indicated by cow-similarity is not determined [from the sentence], then it would remain undetermined even later.
Otherwise, if it were undetermined, it would remain so later as well.
Therefore, it is determined at the very time of hearing the sentence."
And if this is not accepted, how would linguistic competence regarding words like '<s>indra</s>' and the like [ever arise]? For there is no perception of a distinctive configuration and the like as an occasioning cause.
Nor is there perpetual non-competence regarding those [words], because the understanding of the meaning of sentences qualified by those meanings would be undermined.
Likewise, for words like '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (impression) and others that refer to objects that are eternal, supersensory, and so forth, there would be perpetual non-competence.
If there is some solution there, then the same applies here.
Thus it is established that <s>upamāna</s> is not a separate [<s>pramāṇa</s>].
And <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is simply <s>anumāna</s> (inference); for the postulation of an explanans from the observation of something inexplicable is nothing but knowledge of the pervader from the pervaded — because what is not pervaded would not be inexplicable without that [postulated entity], and because what is not a pervader would not be capable of explaining it.
Nor should one say that <s>arthāpatti</s> is the determination of domain-distinction when two <s>pramāṇas</s> are in conflict — because when both <s>pramāṇas</s> are valid, there is no conflict; and if they conflict, [at least one of] them cannot be valid.
If one objects: when <s>Devadatta</s>'s being alive is established by some <s>pramāṇa</s>, and since a living person must be somewhere — when his general connection with place in general is known without specification, and though even the house is a possible location, perception teaches the absence of him in the house — there is a clear conflict, and therefore the postulation of his being outside to resolve this is <s>arthāpatti</s> — not so; because of the ascertained fact that his being alive, known [to be the case] in some [place], has no restriction [to any particular place]; and because the perception of absence in the house, being a definitive cognition, is incapable of competing with the mere doubt about his being present outside.
Nor is there anywhere a real equality of strength between cognitions with contradictory objects; such could only arise if both were invalid.
Even in the case of equality of apparent strength, the same [applies].
When the inequality is grasped, then since the relative strength is established from that alone, what is to be accomplished by <s>arthāpatti</s>?
Therefore, the procedure would be: when a particular contradicting factor with no other scope is present, the general [cognition] that has scope is to be narrowed. And that too, being [based on] pervasion in just that way, has inference as its result; otherwise, just as one might postulate a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> for abandoning a contradicted object, why not also postulate one for arriving at a non-contradicted particular?
Moreover, if this [reduction to inference] is not accepted, then even in smoke-inference and the like, there would be the consequence of its being <s>arthāpatti</s> — since one can state both the inexplicability without fire and the conflict between the two <s>pramāṇas</s> of mark-perception and direct perception.
For smoke implies fire as its cause, while perception negates it — and in this conflict, the determination that fire exists on the far side of the mountain would be <s>arthāpatti</s>.
Distinctions such as "the capacity to indicate is understood merely as a property of the indicator, without determining the pervasion" — these are fabricated by mere wishful thinking.

children.text:
nyā. pa. śa. 55 yattu āgamaprāmāṇye "anubhavaścendriyaliṅgaśabdasadṛśānyathānupapadyamānārthapūrvakaḥ" ityādiṣu upamānārthāpattiparigrahaḥ pratibhāti, tadapi pūrvapakṣapradeśagatatvānna siddhāntatvāya kalpate /
abhāvastvasmanmate bhāvāntarātmā /
sa cākṣādibhiryathāsaṃbhavaṃ sidhyati /
abhāvātmanā tu grahaṇepi pratiyogismaraṇādisahakārisahitāni tānyeva pramāṇanīti na tadatiriktakalpanāvakāśaḥ /
ata eva hi prāgartajābhāvādivijñānamapi nirvyūḍham; dṛṣṭa eva hi deśakālādisaṃsargādiviśeṣaḥ paścāt pratiyogismaraṇādimataḥ puruṣasya tadabhāvātmanā dhiyamadhirohati, smartavyasya smaraṇābhāvādvā; tatra tadabhāvānumānam /
evamatiriktābhāvapakṣepi nirmūlā pramāṇāntarakḷptiḥ; saghaṭaṃ bhūtalamitivat aghaṭaṃ bhūtalamityapi hyaparokṣā pratītiḥ; na cādhikaraṇagrahaṇopakṣīṇamindriyam, guṇādiṣvapi prasaṅgāt; atirekavadanatirekepyajñātakaraṇatvādīnyanumānāni ca sulabhānīti /
saṃbhavopyanumānameva, sahasre śataṃ saṃbhavati ityādeḥ pūrvānubhūsahasragatavyāptibodhanatvāt, saṃbhavati kṣatriye śairyamityādeḥ saṃdehātmakatvenāpramāṇatvāt /
avirodhaniścayarūpatvepi tadavirodhaniścāyakapramāṇāntare viśramaḥ /
aitihyaṃ tu pramāṇamūlaṃ cedāgamaḥ; tadābhāsamūlaṃ cet tadābhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for <s>aitihya</s> (tradition) — if its source is a [genuine] <s>pramāṇa</s>, it is <s>āgama</s> (valid testimony); if its source is a semblance [of a <s>pramāṇa</s>], it is a semblance [of valid testimony].
Likewise, gestures, written characters, and the like, being invariably accompanied by a specific intention regarding specific phonemes, are simply <s>anumāna</s> (inference).
Regarding gestures, the venerable <s>Varada Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭāraka</s> has stated thus: "Even through gesture, an imitation of verbal usage is made,
which conveys its own meaning to those skilled in verbal cognition.

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> section 55. As for the fact that in [the discussion of] the validity of <s>āgama</s> (scriptural testimony), in passages like "experience is preceded by objects [apprehended through] the sense organs, inferential marks, verbal testimony, similarity, and the otherwise-inexplicable" — there appears to be an inclusion of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>arthāpatti</s> — that too does not serve to establish the final position, because it occurs in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie objection) section.
As for <s>abhāva</s> (absence), in our view it is identical with a positive entity (<s>bhāvāntarātman</s>).
And it is established through sensory and other [means of knowledge] as appropriate.
Even when absence is grasped as absence, those very <s>pramāṇas</s>, assisted by cooperating factors such as the memory of the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) and so forth, [accomplish the cognition] — so there is no occasion for postulating anything beyond them.
For this very reason, the cognition of prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) and the like has also been explained: for the specific connection with place, time, and so forth that has been observed [as empty] subsequently gives rise, in a person who recalls the counter-correlate, to a cognition in the form of the absence of that [object] — or [it arises] from the non-occurrence of the memory of what ought to be remembered; therein, that constitutes an inference of absence.
Thus, even on the view that absence is a separate category, the postulation of a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> is groundless; for just as the cognition "the ground with a pot" is direct, so too is the cognition "the ground without a pot" direct; and the sense organ [that cognizes the ground] is not exhausted by apprehending the locus [alone], since the same absurd consequence would arise regarding qualities and the like; and inferences based on unknown instruments and the like, as in the case of positive entities, are easily available in the case of non-entities as well.
<s>Saṃbhava</s> (inclusion) too is simply inference, because statements like "a hundred is included in a thousand" convey the pervasion residing in the previously experienced thousand, while statements like "valor is included in a <s>Kṣatriya</s>" are not <s>pramāṇa</s> because they are of the nature of doubt.
Even if [<s>saṃbhava</s>] has the form of a determination of non-contradiction, the ultimate reliance is on another <s>pramāṇa</s> that determines that non-contradiction.
In beginningless usages, gestures whose powers have been recognized
would be informative just like direct perception — if this is your view,

children.text: ceṣṭā giro vā svīkāryāḥ parapratyāyanāya hi /
children.translated_text: [we reply:] either gestures or speech must be accepted for communicating with others;
since both are beginningless, the beginninglessness of speech is superior.
Gesture is conventional, following verbal usage;
'this [gesture] conveys this [meaning]' — this is established in the <s>āgama</s> (tradition) of <s>Bharata</s> and others."

children.text:
dṛśyatenādirāmnāyosmaryamāṇapraṇetṛkaḥ /
" ityādi /
tattvaratnākare tvevamuktam--- "vyutpannabodhyabodhakaniyamaṃ cet ceṣṭitaṃ śābdam /
aniyatamapi sahadṛṣṭyā smārakamiti na pṛthageṣṭavyam iti /
lipyakṣareṣu tu ayaṃ gakāraḥ ayaṃ ghakāraḥ iti varṇātmanā jñānamapramāṇameva /
etena cihnenedamakṣaraṃ jānīhītyabhiprāyeṇalipyakṣarasaṃbandhagrāhakāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ /

children.translated_text: And from that, the establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion/invariable concomitance) [follows].

children.text: eṣā lipiretadvarṇaviśeṣābhiprāyapūrvikā, bhramādirahitavarṇābhiprāyavatpuruṣalikhitaitallipitvāt, saṃpratipannavyutpattikālalipivat, ityādirūpaḥ prayogo draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inferential application should be seen in the following form: "This writing was preceded by the intention of a specific phoneme; because it is writing written by a person who intended the phoneme without error and the like, just like the writing at the time of [one's own] acknowledged linguistic competence" — and so on.

children.text: yattu pratibhāyāmuktaṃ tattvaratnākare--- "nanu ca pratibhā kācid yathārthā mānamiṣyatām /
children.translated_text: As for what has been stated in the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s> regarding <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition): "But let some veridical <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) be accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s> —
let it be capable of [producing] knowledge of external objects without dependence on external objects.

"An authorless revealed tradition is observed, whose author is not remembered" — and so on.
And in the <s>Tattvaratnākara</s>, it has been stated thus: "If gesture is verbal [in nature], having the restriction that it conveys meaning only to the linguistically competent, then even when unrestricted, since it serves as a reminder through co-observation, it need not be sought as a separate [<s>pramāṇa</s>].
As for written characters, the cognition 'this is the letter <s>ga</s>, this is the letter <s>gha</s>' — as a cognition of the phoneme-nature [of the character] — is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all. The activity of those who learn the connection between written characters and phonemes proceeds with the intention: 'know this phoneme by this sign.'"
The possibility of excellence dependent on a distinguished time, person, and the like —
True, but the distinction based on time and so forth is difficult to discern for persons such as ourselves.
Even though that [distinction] exists, it is disregarded as not useful in practical application.
When the result of <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash) is observed, the ascertainment of its validity
is not examined by the discerning from any other source, since the purpose is already accomplished thereby.
In meritorious persons, this [<s>pratibhā</s>] is for the most part truth-revealing.

children.text: tasmāt patañjaliḥ prāha pratibhā ceti tāṃ pramām" //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Patañjali</s> declared it as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) by saying '<s>pratibhā</s> also.'"
Thus, that [discussion] too pertains only to a particular type of yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>) as mentioned earlier.

children.text: nanvevaṃ, tadapi pramāṇatritvaṃ catuṣṭvaṃ vānupapannam, pratyakṣaparokṣarūpeṇa dvitvasyaiva yuktatvāt, iti cenna, atiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: If [one objects:] "In that case, even the threefold or fourfold [classification] of <s>pramāṇas</s> is untenable, since a twofold division as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and non-perception (<s>parokṣa</s>) alone is appropriate" — no, because of overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
For thus — by extracting each one from among many and grouping the rest together,
in a twofold division, the same [absurdity] would follow even for pots and the like.
By the division of inference and non-inference, verbal testimony and non-verbal-testimony,

children.text: pramāṇadvitvamevaṃ te vada kiṃ vāna rocate //
children.translated_text: a twofold classification of <s>pramāṇas</s> [would result] — tell us, does this also not appeal to you?
If the distinction of perception from the other two [is justified] by apprehending its dissimilarity [from them],
then the dissimilarity of those two [inference and verbal testimony] from each other is equally evident to us.
Because the unique grounds — called sense-contact (<s>akṣa</s>), inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and word (<s>śabda</s>) — [are distinct],
the nature of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), which is to be characterized [by these], is remembered as threefold or even fourfold.
As for what the <s>Jainas</s> have stated as a twofold [division] — 'clear' and 'unclear' —
that does not differ from the division into perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and non-perception (<s>parokṣa</s>).

children.text: ato na tāvati dvaidhe sādhite vivadāmahe /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we do not dispute that much — the establishment of a twofold [division].
[But] the oneness of the non-perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s> is difficult to maintain, because of the establishment of [internal] differences.
If [one argues:] "But even in perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) there is differentiation — based on the division into external and internal,
as divine and non-divine, and also by the distinction of eye, ear, and other [sense faculties]"—
"In the same way, from the differentiation of the one non-perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s>,
why is not the distinction of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>) accepted?"
This has been answered already: "This particular [thing] is seen, and that particular [thing] is heard,
and this [particular thing] is inferred" — common parlance is the witness here.
Some dissimilarity from something or other, and similarity with something or other,
is easily found everywhere — agreed, it is accepted here too.
Therefore, even from the division into <s>smṛti</s> (memory) and <s>anubhūti</s> (experience), a twofold [classification] of <s>pramāṇas</s> is not appropriate —
thus the well-established method stated earlier [holds good].
Experience (<s>anubhava</s>) is indeed threefold, and memory (<s>smṛti</s>) grounded in it is likewise [threefold].

children.text: iti ṣoḍhā vibhāge tu na vimanyāmahe vayam //
children.translated_text: In such a sixfold division, we do not take offense.
Since the division of memory grounded in [experience] is already accomplished by the division of experience [itself],
their grouping together has been stated [as justified].
For this very reason, with the intention of subsuming that [memory] within those [experiences] which are its grounds,
some earlier [authorities] analyze the <s>pramāṇa</s> group as threefold.
In this manner, other [related matters] too should be considered. Thus.

children.text: nanu anenana kiṃ pramāṇacintākleśena ? avimṛśyāpi pramāṇavargamupalambhānvayavyatirekādivaśāt paśvādīnāmiva manuṣyādīnāmapi laukikeṣvartheṣu pravṛttinivṛttitatprayojanādikaṃ nirupadravaṃ sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Now [one objects:] "What is the purpose of this toil over <s>pramāṇa</s> investigation? Even without scrutinizing the <s>pramāṇa</s> classification, through the force of the agreement and difference of apprehension and the like, for humans just as for animals, engagement, disengagement, and their purposes in worldly matters are accomplished without impediment.

children.text: alaukikeṣvapi tattadvidhāyakaistadanugrāhakaiśca kalpasūtrādibhiścaritārthadhiyāṃ kimanena piṣṭapeṣaṇādikalpena vṛthā vimarśeneti cet, maivam; avakāśoparodhāya tattvopaplavamicchatām /
children.translated_text: Even in supra-mundane matters, for those whose understanding is already accomplished through the respective prescriptive texts and their auxiliary <s>Kalpasūtras</s> and the like — what is the use of this futile deliberation, akin to grinding what is already ground?" — [the answer is:] Not so; to prevent the obstruction of [valid cognitive] scope by those who desire the overthrow of truth,
and for the establishment of freedom from error, the method of the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) must be purified.
And recollecting the purpose demonstrated in the introductory chapter (<s>prārambhāhnika</s>),
the effort regarding the means of knowledge together with its auxiliaries (<s>sāṅga</s>) is for the purification of the objects to be established (<s>sādhyaprameya</s>).
Even by the greatest <s>Yogins</s> who have directly perceived all objects,
the ocean of philosophical confusion (<s>tattvaviplavasāgara</s>) is crossed by resorting to the raft of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge).
Therefore, purification must be carried out in the manner stated.

children.text: śuddhānyāyaniṣevitā śrutiśiraḥśuddhāntasiddhāntinī bhadrāṇāṃ pratipādanāya bhajatu pratyakṣatāmakṣatām /
children.translated_text: Resorting to pure logic (<s>śuddhanyāya</s>), establishing the doctrines of the pure culmination of the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation), may [this work] attain unimpaired direct manifestation for the edification of the virtuous.

children.text: patyau nityarase samaṃ karuṇayā pātivratīṃ bibhratī sarvagranthivimocanī bhagavatī sā me samīcī kṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: Bearing the faithfulness of a devoted wife (<s>pātivratī</s>) together with compassion toward the Lord (<s>Pati</s>) who is of eternal delight (<s>nityarasa</s>), may that auspicious composition of mine, which unties all knots, be well-directed.

children.text: iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu nyāyapariśuddhau smṛtyadhyāye //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the works of <s>Śrī Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the <s>Vedāntācārya</s> (teacher of <s>Vedānta</s>), the lion among poets and logicians (<s>kavitārkikasiṃha</s>), master of all systems (<s>sarvatantrasvatantra</s>), in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in the chapter on <s>Smṛti</s> —
the second session (<s>āhnika</s>).
And thus the fourth chapter is concluded.
The chapter on <s>Prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge).
First session (<s>āhnika</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. prame. 1 evaṃ saparikaraṃ pramāṇaṃ viśodhitam /
atha prameyaṃ pradarśayāmaḥ /
tatra yat punaḥ ṣaṭsaptādirūpeṇa padārthān vibhajya vaiśeṣikādayaścintayanti, tanna sākṣādapavargāṅgamiti tairevābhyupetam /

children.translated_text: Moreover — by abandoning what exists and accepting what does not exist,
those deliberations are deluding; they should be excluded by seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣus</s>).
In those [systems] which have their own sub-divisions, regarding the efforts of deliberation on each respective [category] here,
for the sake of brevity, we state merely the direction of the faults.

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 1. Thus, the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) has been purified together with its accessories. Now we shall set forth the objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>). Therein, as for what the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others deliberate upon by classifying the categories (<s>padārthas</s>) in the form of six, seven, and so on — that is not directly an auxiliary to liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), as is conceded even by them.

children.text:
yat tatrāhuḥ--- "abhidheyaḥ padārthaḥ /
sa ca bhāvābhāvabhedena dvidhā" iti, tat tāvat "asadvyapadeśānneti cenna, dharmāntareṇa vākyaśeṣādyukteḥ, śabdāntarācca" ityārambhaṇādhikaraṇasūtreṇābhāvasya parābhyupagatābhāvābhāvasyeva bhāvāntaratvasamarthanāt pratikṣiptam /
yadapi ca--- dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyarūpeṇa bhāvarūpāṇāṃ padārthānāṃ ṣoḍhā parisaṃkhyānam, tadapi vaiśeṣikādhikaraṇe "samavāyābhyupagamācca sāmyādanavasthiteḥ" iti sūtrakāraireva samavāyākhyapadārthāntaradūśaṇena parāstam /
abhāvatadadhikaraṇayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasaṃnidhiviśeṣādiśabdavācyasaṃbandhāntarānumānamapi samavāyadūṣaṇacchāyayaiva dūṣitameva /
yaścānyonyamatyantatulyeṣu muktātmādiṣu mitho vyāvṛttadhījananāya dravyatvādihetunā viśeṣākhyaḥ padārthaḥ kalpyate, sopi tulyanyāyatayā sūtrakārairdūṣitaprāya eva /
"mahaddīrghavadvā hvasvaparimaṇḍalābhyām" ityanupapannaparamāṇudvyaṇukādiprakriyānidarśanenānyeṣāmapi tadabhyupagatānāmunapapannatvasya sūcitatvācca /
api cānityeṣu dravyeṣu tāvajjātiguṇapādibhireva vyāvṛttadhīḥ sidhyatīti nityeṣu hi viśeṣonyaḥ kalpyate; yathāhuḥ--- "nityadravyavṛttayontyā viśeṣāḥ" iti, tathāpi vedāntibhirdiksaṃjñakavibhupadārthāntarānabhyupagamādākāśasya ca kāryatvādiśruteḥ prakṛtivikārabhūtapṛthivyādyaṃśaviśeṣātiriktaparamāṇujālapratikṣepāt tathāvidhaparamāṇūnāṃ cāvasthāpravāhasyānādyantatvānna tatra viśeṣakḷptiḥ /
tataḥ kālātmānau pariśiṣyete /
tatrāpi cetanānāṃ na kālatattvamātmatayā bhāti /
kṣaṇalavādyavasthāyogitvaparāktvācetanatvādibhireva, tasmāt sveṣāṃ svebhyaśca tasya vyāvṛttadhīsaṃbhavāt /
anyathānyenāpi kalpitena tadasaṃbhavaprasaṅgāt /
ataḥ ātmapariśeṣe tatrāpi jīveśvarayoraṇutvavibhutvaniyāmyatvaniyantṛtvādheyatvādhāratvaśeṣatvaśeṣitvaśarīratvaśarīr itvābhiranekavidhairdharmabhedairvyāvṛttadhīsiddhau kimanyena viśeṣeṇa ? /
tadatyantasāmyavatsu mukteṣu nityeṣvapi hi tatsāmyasyaiva saṃrakṣaṇāya dharmigrāhakasiddhā yāvadātmabhāvinaste te viśeṣā na parityaktāḥ /
na ceśvaradvaitam; yeneśvarāṇāṃ mithovyāvṛttapratītyai viśeṣaṃ kalpayiṣyāmaḥ, ekasyaiva sarvadeśakāleṣvekātapatratayā sarvaśrutisiddhatvāt, asyaiva ca sāmānyaśabdairviśeṣaśabdaiśca rūḍhito yogatastattadvasatuviśiṣṭatvādinā ca tattatprakaraṇānuguṇaṃ śarīrake pratipādyatvasthāpanāt /
jīveṣvapi baddhānāṃ mitho bhedastattatsukhaduḥkhadhīcchāvaicitryeṇa vyaktaḥ /
baddhamuktayośca kiñcijjñatvasarvajñatvādibhiḥ, muktānāṃ nityānāṃ ca viśuddherādimattvānādimattvābhyāmeva vibhaktadhīsaṃbhavaḥ /
muktadaśāyāṃ nityebhyaḥ kiṃ vaiṣmyamiti cet, kiṃ tena ? /
prāktanena tattadātmavartitayā pratyakṣitena guṇādibhedena tadanyavyāvṛttadhīsiddheḥ /
siddhairapi tadvyavahāre prāktanopādhibhedaireva tattatpramāṇapramitaiḥ pratisaṃhitaiḥ sarvanirvāhāt /
etena muktānāṃ mitho vibhaktabuddhirapi nirvyūḍhā; na hi teṣāmekarūpaḥ prāktanaḥ saṃsāraḥ; viṣamavipākasamayānādyasaṃkhyātakarmapravāhavaicitryapratiniyatadeśakālasvarūpasukhaduḥkhatatkāraṇādisaṃtatereva mitho vyāvartakatvāt /
tadatadvibhāgo hi tatkālavartinaivaṃ dharmeṇeti na niyamaḥ, atatkālavartināpi tanniṣṭhatayopalabhyamānena tatsiddheḥ; na hyatītaḥ saṃsāro muktātmasvarūpamupalabhamānairnopalabhyate, upalabhyamāno vānyaniṣṭhaḥ pratibhāti /
atha nityeṣu mithaḥ kā vārtrā ? /
sāpi kuśalaiva /
teṣāmapi hi satyasaṃkalpānāṃ vicitrāḥ saṃkalpecchādaya riśvarasyevāniyatadeśakālaviṣayāparyanuyojyasāmagrīkā anādyanantasaṃtānavantaḥ santīti kimanyena viśeṣeṇa ? /
api ca yaddarśane yatra yadāropo na bhavati sa hi tasya tato bhedaḥ /
sa eva ca viśeṣaḥ /
sa cet svarūpabhūtohantvamādirūpeṇa bhātaḥ parāropaṃ pratirundhyāt, kastatonyastato viśeṣastasya ? /
evamanabhyupagame viśeṣakḷptāvapi kā gatirvaiśeṣikasya ? svaparanirvāhakāste viśeṣāḥ, iti cet, kiṃ ta eva? /
api ca pṛthaktve vidyamāne kiṃ tairviśeṣaiḥ ? /
pṛthaktvasyaikajātisaṃgṛhītatvānna tatopi vyāvṛttadhīrīti cet, tarhi tato na kvacidapi syāt /
viśeṣeṣvapi vā viśeṣatvākrānteṣu kaste nistāraḥ ? /
viśeṣatvaṃ nāma jātirnāstīti cet, kiṃ tat ? /
upādhiriticet, kiṃ tato na saṃgrahaḥ?, tathā sati kvacidapi tannibandhanānuvṛttadhībhaṅgaprasaṅgāt /
evamanyonyābhāvenāpi gatārthatā dustareti parāstaḥ parābhimataviśeṣaḥ /
sāmānyamapi paroktaṃ sūtrakāraireva nirastaprāyam; tathāhi--- "tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ---" ityādibhiḥ sūtraiḥ kāryadaśāyāmupādānasyāvasthāntarāpattimātrameva, na punaḥ parābhimatamavayavyākhyaṃ dravyamastīti samarthanād ghaṭādyavayavyabhāve tadāśritaghaṭatvādisāmānyamavayavisamavetatayābhyupagataguṇādayastadubhayārambhaprakriyājālaṃ ca nirmūlitam /
yaccopādānasya ghaṭatvādirūpamavasthāntaraṃ saṃyogaviśeṣādirūpaṃ, tat parairapi kāryatayābhyupetamupalambhādibhiśca tathaiva sidhyatīti na tatrāpi nityatvakalpanāvakāśaḥ /
tataḥ sarveṣāṃ dravyāṇāṃ svarūpatonādyanantatvāt kāryadravyatvātmatvādimātrameva śiṣyate /
guṇeṣu nityeṣvavasthārūpeṣu cānuvṛttapratyayanimittaṃ kimiti cintyam; tatraivaṃ bhāṣitaṃ śārīrakādye--- "saṃsthānātirekiṇonekeṣvekākārabuddhibodhyasyādarśanāt, tāvataiva gotvādijātivyavahāropapatteḥ, atirekavādepi saṃsthānasya saṃpratipannatvācca saṃsthānameva jāti /
saṃsthānaṃ nāma svāsādhāraṇaṃ rūpamiti yathāvastu saṃsthānamanusaṃdheyam" iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--- kiṃ saṃsthānātiriktaṃ sāmānyaṃ viviktasphuṭapratyakṣādhyavasāyabhedādaṅgīkriyate, utopapattibalāditi; nādyaḥ, asiddheḥ nāntyaḥ, anyathāsiddheḥ; atiriktasāmānyamabhyupagacchatopi hi tadupalakṣaṇaṃ saṃsthānamiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca /
prativyaktiniyataṃ saṃsthānaṃ kathamanuvṛttapratyayakāraṇamiti cet, kathaṃ vā tajjātīyasya lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati ? /
anuvṛttajātyantarasaṃgṛhītopādhirūpatayeti cet, tāvataiva gavādivyavahārasiddhau kimanyena ? /
tathāpyantatonuvṛttaṃ sāmānyaṃ kvacidabhyupagantavyam, yatrānanyathāsiddhiḥ; anyathopādhisaṃgrahasyāpyasaṃbhavāditi cet, tavāpi vā tatra sāmānyamupalakṣaṇena saṃgṛhyate, na vā ? pūrvatrānyathāsiddhiranavasthitiśca /
uttaratra niyāmakādarśanājjāterāśrayavyavasthā na syāt /
vyāvṛttānāmapi svabhāvata eva kāsāṃcit vyaktīnāṃ tadvyañjakatvaniyatiriti cet, sa eva svabhāvaḥ kiṃ na vyavahāraṃ niyachet /
nirviṣayaḥ kathaṃ vyavahāraḥ syāditi cet, tāsāmeva vyaktīnāṃ viṣayatvāt /
vyāvṛttānāmanuvṛttavyavahāraviṣayatve sarvatra viṣayavyavasthā bhajyeteti cet, vyāvṛttānāmanuvṛttavyañjakatve sarvatra tadvyaktiḥ kiṃ na syāt ? /
saṃbandhāsaṃbandhābhyāṃ niyamāditi cenna, saṃbandhasyāpi samavāyanāmnaḥ sārvatrikatvābhyupagamāt tatrāpyabhivyaktipratiniyamasya mṛgyatvāt, nānāsamavāyavādepi vyaktisvabhāvaniyamasya dustyajatvāt, tathāpi dṛṣṭaikagovyaktervyaktyantare soyamiti pratyabhijñānaṃ kathaṃ syāt ? ayaṃ gaurityekavyaktau vyutpāditaśca kathaṃ vyaktyatyantarepi tacchabdavācyatāṃ pratīyāt ? iti cet, tavāpi vā katham ? /
ekadharmasamavāyāditi cet ? tenaiva dharmeṇa svato militasya samavāyasyaiva nityaṃ sarvatra vṛttyabhyupagamena sarvatra sarvavyavahārasaṃkaraprasaṅgāt /
kāsāṃcideva vyaktīnāṃ tadvyañjakatvasvābhāvyād vyavasthokteti cet, tarhi tāsāmeva vyaktīnāṃ pratisaṃdhānavyavahārayorviṣayatvamastu /
tathā sati bhrāntatvaṃ tayoḥ syāditi cenna, tadvyaktitvena pratisaṃdhānāderabhāvāt ; api tarhi tathātvena vyaktisvarūpātiriktaṃ tathātvaṃ nāmāntareṇa jātireva syāditi cet, tajjātivyañjakaṃ tattadekavyaktisvarūpātiriktaṃ kiṃ na jātyantaraṃ syāt ? /
upādhiviśeṣa evāyaṃ pratiniyatāśraya iti cet, evaṃ tarhi pratiniyatapratiyogikaṃ svabhāvaniyataṃ parasparasmārakatvamupajīvya tajjātīyatayā pratisaṃdhānavyavahāropapattau kimanyakalpanena ? /
tasmārakataditaravibhāgaḥ kutastya iti cet, tadvyañjakataditaravibhāgaste kutastyaḥ ? /
darśanādarśanāyatta iti cet, tulyam /
saṃbandhasādṛśyayorabhāve kathaṃ smārakatvamiti cet, tayorvā katham ? /
sadṛśasahānubhūtadarśanasya saṃskārodbodhakatvāditi cet, tadapi kutaḥ ? /
kāryadarśanāt kalpyate iti cet, tulyam; anyathā saṃbandhaṃ sādṛśyaṃ vaikamupādāya tadanyasya kathaṃ smārakatvamiti codyasya durvāratvāt /
na cātra sādṛśyaṃ nāṅgīkurmaḥ, sausādṛśyarūpatvābhyupagamāt sāmānyasya /
children.translated_text: And here it is not the case that we do not accept <s>sādṛśya</s> (similarity); for we accept that the nature of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) consists in good similarity (<s>sausādṛśya</s>).

children.text: nāmāntareṇa parābhimatajātisvīkāraḥ iti cet, vyāvṛttānāṃ saṃniveśādīnāmeva pratiniyatapratiyogismārakasvabhāvatayā sādṛśyarūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: If [it is objected]: 'This is merely accepting the <s>jāti</s> (universal) as held by the opponents under a different name' — [we reply]: No, because [our universal] consists in the similarity of the very configurations (<s>saṃniveśa</s>) and the like that are [mutually] distinct, which by their nature have the capacity to remind of specific counterparts.

children.text: gavayāderapi tarhi gojātīyatvādiprasaṅgaḥ iti cenna, sādṛśyasausādṛśyavibhāgasvaya sāṃpratyayikasya sarvasaṃmatatvāt iti /
children.translated_text: If [it is objected]: 'Then even a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) and the like would absurdly become of the cow-class (<s>gojātīya</s>)' — no, because the distinction between [genuine] similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>) and [merely] good resemblance (<s>sausādṛśya</s>) is universally accepted as a matter of direct experience (<s>sāṃpratyayika</s>).

children.text: evaṃ sāmānyādiṣu sūtrakārādibhirnirasteṣu pariśiṣṭā dravyaguṇakarmarūpāstrayaḥ padārthāḥ iti kecidācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, since <s>sāmānya</s> (universals) and other [categories] have been rejected by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> and others, certain <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) [hold that] the remaining word-referents (<s>padārthas</s>) are three in number, in the form of substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and action (<s>karma</s>). //

As for what they [the Naiyāyika-Vaiśeṣikas] state there — 'The word-referent (<s>padārtha</s>) is what is denoted; and it is twofold, by the division of existence (<s>bhāva</s>) and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>)' — that, to begin with, is refuted by the <s>Ārambhaṇādhikaraṇa</s> <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Asadvyapadeśānneti cenna, dharmāntareṇa vākyaśeṣādyukteḥ, śabdāntarācca</s>' ('It is not so, because [the designation of] non-existence [is] through another property, as shown by the remainder of the sentence and other words'), since it establishes that <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), just like the non-existence of non-existence accepted by the opponents themselves, is really a positive entity (<s>bhāvāntara</s>). As for the sixfold enumeration of positive word-referents in the form of substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>), and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — that too is set aside in the <s>Vaiśeṣikādhikaraṇa</s> by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (the author of the sūtras) himself through the refutation of the separate category called <s>samavāya</s> (inherence): '<s>Samavāyābhyupagamācca sāmyādanavasthiteḥ</s>' ('And because of the acceptance of inherence, there would be an infinite regress due to parity of reasoning'). The inference of another relation — expressible by terms such as qualifier-qualified relation, proximity, and the like — between <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) and its substratum, is also refuted by the very same line of reasoning that refutes <s>samavāya</s>. And the category called <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), which is postulated through the ground of <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-hood) and the like, in order to generate the cognition of mutual distinction among entities such as liberated selves and others that are completely identical to one another — that too is virtually refuted by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> through parity of reasoning. Also because, by the illustration of the untenable procedure of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) and dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) and so forth — through [the sūtra] '<s>Mahaddīrghavadvā hvasvaparimaṇḍalābhyām</s>' ('Or, like the large and the long, [size results] from the small and the spherical') — the untenability of other [categories] accepted by them is also indicated. Moreover, in the case of impermanent substances, the cognition of mutual distinction is already accomplished through <s>jāti</s> (universal), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and the like alone; for it is only in the case of eternal [substances] that a separate <s>viśeṣa</s> is postulated. As they [the Vaiśeṣikas] say: '<s>Nityadravyavṛttayontyā viśeṣāḥ</s>' ('The ultimate <s>viśeṣas</s> subsist in eternal substances'). Even so, since the <s>Vedāntins</s> do not accept a separate all-pervading substance designated as 'direction' (<s>diś</s>), and because of <s>śruti</s> passages declaring that <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is an effect, and because of the rejection of the network of atoms beyond the specific modifications of earth and other elements that are evolutes of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), and because the stream of states of such atoms is beginningless and endless — there is no occasion for postulating <s>viśeṣa</s> there. From this, [only] time (<s>kāla</s>) and self (<s>ātman</s>) remain. Of these too, for conscious beings, the reality of time does not appear as their essential nature. Because [time is distinguished] by properties such as being subject to states of moments (<s>kṣaṇa</s>), units (<s>lava</s>), and so forth, being remote, being non-conscious, and the like — therefore, the cognition of mutual distinction between time and selves, and among selves themselves, is possible [without a separate viśeṣa]. Otherwise [if viśeṣa were needed], even with another postulated [entity], the same impossibility would arise. Hence, when it comes to the remaining category of self (<s>ātman</s>), even there, between <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the cognition of mutual distinction is accomplished through numerous differences of attributes — such as atomicity (<s>aṇutva</s>) and all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>), being controlled (<s>niyāmyatva</s>) and being the controller (<s>niyantṛtva</s>), being dependent (<s>ādheyatva</s>) and being the support (<s>ādhāratva</s>), being the subordinate (<s>śeṣatva</s>) and being the principal (<s>śeṣitva</s>), being the body (<s>śarīratva</s>) and being the embodied self (<s>śarīritva</s>) — so what need is there for a separate <s>viśeṣa</s>? As for the [objection regarding] liberated and eternal [selves] that possess absolute similarity — even there, those very attributes that endure as long as the self exists, established through cognition that apprehends the substance-possessor (<s>dharmigrāhakasiddha</s>), are not abandoned, precisely in order to preserve that very similarity [i.e., their distinct identities despite similarity]. Nor is there a plurality of <s>Īśvaras</s>, such that we would need to postulate <s>viśeṣa</s> for generating the cognition of mutual distinction among [multiple] Lords — because the sole sovereignty of the one [Lord] over all places and times is established by all <s>śrutis</s>, and because it is established in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Brahmasūtras] that this very [Lord] is taught in various contexts as appropriate, through general terms and specific terms, by conventional and etymological meaning, and by being qualified by particular abodes and the like. Among <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) too, the mutual distinction of bound souls is evident through the diversity of their respective pleasures (<s>sukha</s>), pains (<s>duḥkha</s>), cognitions (<s>dhī</s>), and desires (<s>icchā</s>). Between the bound and the liberated, [distinction is] through limited knowledge (<s>kiñcijjñatva</s>) and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) and the like. And for the liberated and the eternally free (<s>nitya</s>), the possibility of distinct cognition is through the very fact that [the liberated soul's] purity has a beginning while [that of the eternally free] is beginningless. If asked: 'What difference is there between the liberated and the eternally free?' — what of it? Because the cognition of distinction from others is accomplished through the difference of qualities and the like that existed previously and were directly perceived as pertaining to each particular self. Even for those who are accomplished [in knowledge], all dealings regarding them are fully sustained through the differences of prior conditions (<s>prāktanopādhibheda</s>) that were apprehended by the respective means of valid knowledge and then retained. By this, the cognition of mutual distinction among the liberated is also resolved; for their prior <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) is not of a single form — because it is the succession of their respective natures, places, times, pleasures, pains, causes thereof, and so forth, determined by the variety of the beginningless and innumerable stream of <s>karma</s> ripening at unequal times, that serves as the differentiator. For the distinction between 'that' and 'not-that' is not restricted to a property existing at that very time; it is accomplished even through [a property] that is perceived as belonging to that [entity] even though existing at another time. For the past <s>saṃsāra</s> is not unperceived by those who perceive the essential nature of the liberated self, nor when perceived does it appear as belonging to another. Now, what about the mutual distinction among the eternally free (<s>nityas</s>)? That too is well [accounted for]. For even they, being of unfailing will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>), possess variegated volitions, desires, and the like — like <s>Īśvara</s> himself — unrestricted in place, time, and object, with no [external] cause to be questioned, having beginningless and endless succession. So what need is there for a separate <s>viśeṣa</s>? Moreover, that which, when perceived, does not give rise to a superimposition [of identity] upon another — that indeed is the distinction of one thing from another. And that itself is <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity). If that, as an intrinsic nature — appearing in the form of 'pot-ness' and the like — prevents superimposition upon another, what other <s>viśeṣa</s> beyond that [is needed] for it? Thus, if [the Vaiśeṣika] does not accept [this], what course does the Vaiśeṣika have even with the postulation of <s>viśeṣas</s>? If [it is said]: 'Those <s>viśeṣas</s> serve both one's own and the opponent's position' — are they really just those [intrinsic natures]? Moreover, when distinctness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is already present, what need for those <s>viśeṣas</s>? If [it is said]: 'Since <s>pṛthaktva</s> is subsumed under a single <s>jāti</s> (universal), the cognition of distinction does not arise from it' — then it should never arise from it anywhere. Or, with the <s>viśeṣas</s> themselves being pervaded by <s>viśeṣatva</s> (the universal 'particularity-ness'), what is your escape? If [it is said]: 'There is no <s>jāti</s> called <s>viśeṣatva</s>' — then what is it? If [it is said]: 'It is an <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition)' — then why is there no subsumption [under it]? For in that case, the cognition of commonality based on it would collapse everywhere. Thus, the <s>viśeṣa</s> accepted by the opponents is rejected, since the purpose is served even by mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>). As for the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) as propounded by the opponents — that too is virtually rejected by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> himself.
