For thus — by the <s>sūtras</s> beginning with '<s>Tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ</s>' ('Its non-difference [from Brahman is known] from the words "origin" and so forth') — since it is established that in the state of being an effect, there is merely a change of state of the material cause, and not a separate substance called the 'whole' (<s>avayavin</s>) as accepted by the opponents — [therefore] the universal such as <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-ness) that would inhere in such a [non-existent] whole, the qualities and the like that are accepted as inhering in the parts, and the entire network of procedures for originating both — all are uprooted. And that state of the material cause which takes the form of <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-ness) and so forth, [which is] a particular kind of conjunction and the like — that is accepted even by the opponents as being an effect, and is established as such through perception and other [means of knowledge]; hence there is no room for postulating its eternality either. Therefore, since all substances are beginningless and endless in their essential nature, only their being effects (<s>kāryadravyatva</s>), selfhood (<s>ātmatva</s>), and the like alone remain [as universals]. As for what serves as the ground of recurrent cognition in the case of eternal qualities and states — on this point, it has been stated in the opening of the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Bhāṣya]: 'Since no entity beyond configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) that would be apprehended as one form in many [individuals] is perceived, since the usage of <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) and other <s>jāti</s> (universals) is explained by that [configuration] alone, and since even those who assert [a universal] beyond [configuration] accept configuration [as a co-factor] — therefore, configuration itself is <s>jāti</s>. And "configuration" means its own unique form; thus configuration should be understood as it actually is in each case.' What this means is: Is a universal beyond configuration accepted on the basis of a distinct, clear perceptual determination, or on the strength of reasoning [alone]? Not the first, because it is unestablished. Not the second, because of being otherwise explicable. For even one who accepts a universal beyond [configuration] accepts, and indeed observes, configuration as its indicator. If [asked]: 'How can configuration, which is specific to each individual, be the cause of recurrent cognition?' — [we reply]: How indeed does it serve as the defining mark of things of that class? If [answered]: 'Because it has the form of a limiting condition subsumed under another recurrent universal' — then, with that much alone sufficing for the usage regarding cows and the like, what need for anything else? If [it is said]: 'Still, ultimately a recurrent universal must be accepted somewhere, where there is no other explanation; otherwise even the subsumption of limiting conditions would be impossible' — then [we ask]: In your [system] too, is the universal apprehended through an indicator, or not? In the former case, there is the same problem of being otherwise explicable, and an infinite regress. In the latter case, since no determining factor is seen, there would be no fixed assignment of <s>jāti</s> to [particular] substrata. If [it is said]: 'Among the excluded [configurations], some individuals naturally have the capacity to manifest that [universal]' — then why does that very nature not determine the usage [without a universal]? If [asked]: 'How can there be usage without an object [i.e., without a universal as referent]?' — [we reply]: Because those very individuals are the objects. If [objected]: 'If things that are [mutually] distinct become the objects of recurrent usage, the fixed assignment of objects would be violated everywhere' — [we reply]: If things that are distinct [can] manifest a recurrent [universal], why would it not be manifested everywhere? If [answered]: 'There is a restriction due to the presence or absence of the relation [of inherence]' — no, because even the relation called <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is accepted as universal [in scope]; because even there, the restriction of manifestation needs to be sought; because even on the view of multiple inherences, the restriction based on the nature of the individual is inescapable. If [asked]: 'Even so, how would the recognition "this is the same" arise with respect to another individual after seeing one cow-individual? And how would one who has learned the word in connection with one individual understand its denotation with respect to a completely different individual?' — [we reply]: How indeed in your system too? If [answered]: 'Through inherence in one [common] property' — by that very property, since inherence, being naturally conjoined [with it], is accepted as eternally present everywhere, the consequence would be a confusion of all usages everywhere. If [answered]: 'The fixed assignment is stated as being due to the natural capacity of certain individuals alone to manifest that [universal]' — then let those very individuals be the objects of recognition and usage. If [objected]: 'In that case, those [recognitions] would be erroneous' — no, because there is no recognition and the like of them as [instances of] that universal. If [then said]: 'Well then, their being-such, over and above the individual's own nature, would by another name be nothing but a <s>jāti</s> (universal)' — [we reply]: Would not that which manifests that <s>jāti</s>, being something over and above the nature of each individual, itself be yet another <s>jāti</s>? If [answered]: 'This is merely a particular limiting condition restricted to specific substrata' — then, in that case, let recognition and usage of things-of-that-class be explained by relying on the naturally fixed capacity of reciprocal reminiscence that is restricted to specific counterparts; what need for postulating anything else? If [asked]: 'Whence comes the division between what is a reminder and what is not?' — [we reply]: Whence comes your division between what manifests [the universal] and what does not? If [answered]: 'It depends on perception and non-perception' — the same [applies to us]. If [asked]: 'In the absence of relation and similarity, how can there be reminiscence?' — [we reply]: And how [is it possible] through those two? If [answered]: 'Because the perception of something similar that was previously experienced along [with the current object] activates the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>)' — whence does that [capacity] arise? If [answered]: 'It is postulated from the observed effect' — the same [applies to us]; otherwise, the objection that, having taken one entity — be it relation or similarity — how it can serve as a reminder of another, is irrefutable.

nyā. pa. prame. 2 anye tu manyante---yathā tatpratīteranyathāsiddhatayā te padārthā bhāṣyakārādibhirnirasyante, tathā karmāpi, iti, ye tāvadiha sarvatra sūryaparispandādivadapratyakṣaṃ karma phalānumeyamicchanti /
tatra yayā sāmagryā karmaṇaḥ siddhirabhimatā tayaiva dṛṣṭaṃ karmaphalaṃ sādhyatām, kimantarā kalpitena karmaṇā ? /
tathāpi cet kḷptiḥ, anyatrāpi kālaviprakarṣādarśanepi sāmagrīkāryayormadhye anyasya kḷptiprasaṅgaḥ; tathaiva ca tratrāpītyanavasthā syāt /
ye ca "pratyakṣaṃ karma" ityāhuḥ, tairapi nūnaṃ karmaphalatvenābhyupagamasaṃyogavibhāgātiriktaṃ nipuṇanirīkṣaṇepi nopalabhyata iti manyāmahe /
calatipratyayopi hi tāvataiva caritārthaḥ /
na ca vācyaṃ yāvatsaṃyogaṃ calatipratyayaprasaṅga iti, pūrvadeśavibhāgapūrvakadeśāntarasaṃyogaprathamakṣaṇaviṣayatvāt tatpratyayasya /
tata eva hyuttarakāle saṃyoge vartamānepyacaladiti bhūtānusaṃdhānamupapannam /
nanu pravāhamadhyasthite sthāṇau pūrvasalilaskandhaviyogaḥ uttarasalilaskandhayogaśca dṛśyate, na ca tatra calatvamicchāmaḥ; vyomādaya eva sthiradeśatvena vivakṣitāḥ iti cenna, pravāhasya tato viśeṣādarśanāt; laulyam viśeṣaḥ iti cet, tarhi saṃyogavibhāgātiriktaṃ laulyarūpaṃ karmapratyakṣamiti kathaṃ tadapahnavaḥ ? iti /
tatrāhuḥ---yā nāma karmasāmagrī tvayeṣyate sā tattatkarmaphalatayābhimataṃ saṃyogaviśeṣamutpādayantī niyatasvabhāvameva tamutpādayati /
ata eva eva saṃyogonekaniṣṭhopi san kvaciccalatipratyaṃyaṃ kvacit saṃyogamātrapratyayaṃ ca janayati, yathaika eva samavāyoguṇaguṇibhyāmaviśeṣeṇa svato militopi san kvacidāśrayapratyayaṃ kvacidāśritapratyayaṃ ca janayati, na hyāśrayabhāva āśritabhāvo vā samavāyasvarūpātiriktaḥ, tadvadihāpīti /
vayaṃ tu brūmaḥ--- apratyakṣakarmavādastāvat prāguktadūṣaṇādayuktaḥ /

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> as perceptible, however, is difficult to deny in its essential nature.

In that regard, since no rule either affirming or denying its separate existence is found in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and other [authoritative texts], and since there is no contradiction with [its being] another entity, it should be set aside [as a non-issue].

children.text: idaṃ tu manyāmahe--- atirekepi guṇavargānna rāśyantaraṃ karma, vibhājakābhāvāt, svecchākalpitavibhājakasya sarvatra sulabhatvena yathābhimatamekaṃ guṇamubhayaṃ vāṅgīkṛtya rāśyantarakalpanaprasaṅgāt, guṇāvāntaravaicitryasya guṇatvavirodhābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: But we hold this: Even if [<s>karma</s>] exists as a distinct entity, it is not a separate category (<s>rāśi</s>) from the class of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), because there is no differentiating principle; since a differentiating principle fabricated at will is easily available everywhere, there would be the unwanted consequence of accepting any one quality or both and fabricating another category; and because the internal variety of qualities does not contradict their being qualities.
Therefore, the division is simply: <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>adravya</s> (non-substance).

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 2. Others, however, hold that just as those [Vaiśeṣika] categories are rejected by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> and others on the ground that the cognition of them is otherwise explicable, so too is <s>karma</s> (action) [to be rejected as a separate category]. Those who hold that <s>karma</s> everywhere — like the vibration of the sun — is imperceptible and is to be inferred from its effects [are refuted as follows]: By whatever causal complex the accomplishment of <s>karma</s> is accepted, let the observed effect of <s>karma</s> be established by that very complex — what need is there for a fabricated <s>karma</s>? Even if such a fabrication is made, then in other cases too, even where [the effect] is not observed due to temporal distance, there would be the unwanted consequence of fabricating something else between the causal complex and its effect; and the same would apply there too, leading to infinite regress. As for those who say "<s>karma</s> is perceptible," we hold that even they, upon careful examination, do not apprehend anything as the effect of <s>karma</s> that is distinct from <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction). For the cognition 'it moves' is fully accounted for by these alone. Nor can it be objected that there would be the cognition 'it moves' as long as conjunction persists, because that cognition has as its object the first moment of conjunction with a new location preceded by disjunction from the former location. It is precisely for this reason that even when conjunction persists at a later time, retrospective awareness 'it was not moving' is justified. [Objection:] When a post stands in the middle of a current, separation from the earlier body of water and conjunction with the later body of water are observed, yet we do not attribute movement there; things like space are intended as having fixed location. [Reply:] This is not so, because no distinguishing feature of the current [from other cases] is observed. If you say the distinguishing feature is rolling motion (<s>laulya</s>), then how can you deny that <s>karma</s> is perceptible as a rolling-motion-form distinct from conjunction and disjunction? To this they reply: Whatever causal complex of <s>karma</s> you accept — it produces a specific conjunction accepted as the effect of each particular <s>karma</s>, and it produces that [conjunction] with a determinate nature only. It is precisely for this reason that conjunction, though residing in many [substances], generates in some cases the cognition 'it moves' and in other cases merely the cognition of conjunction — just as the single <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), though being indiscriminately united with qualities and qualified alike by its own nature, generates in some cases the cognition of substrate and in other cases the cognition of what inheres, and yet substrate-ness and inherent-ness are not distinct from the essential nature of <s>samavāya</s>; so too here. But we say: The view that <s>karma</s> is imperceptible is untenable, as already refuted above.

children.text: nyā. pa. prame. 3 tatra cātmaguṇatayābhimateṣu sukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnāḥ pañca tattadutpādakatayābhimatabuddhiviśeṣānatiriktā vedārthasaṃgrahe samarthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 3. Among what are accepted as <s>ātmaguṇas</s> (soul-qualities), the five — <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), <s>duḥkha</s> (pain), <s>icchā</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>prayatna</s> (effort) — have been established in the <s>Vedārthasaṃgraha</s> as not being distinct from <s>buddhiviśeṣas</s> (particular modes of cognition) that are accepted as their respective causes.

children.text: dharmādharmau vihitaniṣiddhakriyāsādhyatayābhimatāvājñāvato rājña iva sarvapraśāsiturīśvarasyānugrahanigrahākhyabuddhiviśeṣarūpau bhāṣyādiṣu bahuṣu pradeśeṣu prapañcitau /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), which are accepted as attainable through prescribed and prohibited actions, are, like [the will of] a commanding king, of the nature of particular modes of cognition called <s>anugraha</s> (grace) and <s>nigraha</s> (disfavor) belonging to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the universal sovereign — this has been elaborated in many passages of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and other [texts].

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ saṃskāraḥ sa tāvadbuddhiviśeṣātmanoktaḥ, na ca tatprayuktaḥ; tataściranaṣṭaviprakṛṣṭākāre vyāptyadarśanāt, vāsanānuvṛtteśca vācanikatvāt //
children.translated_text: As for <s>saṃskāra</s> (dispositional tendency), it has been stated to be of the nature of a <s>buddhiviśeṣa</s> (particular mode of cognition) of the self, and is not occasioned by that [alone]; since no pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is observed with impressions whose form is long-undestroyed and remote, and since the continuity of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) is merely verbal.

children.text: nyā. pa. prame. 4 yadyapi "indriyasyendriyasyārthe" ityādigītāślokeṣu bhāṣyakārairvāsanāyā icchādvāreṇaiva pravṛttihetutvavacanājjñānavāsanāviśeṣātiriktā karmavāsanā nāsti, tathāpi jñānavāsanā durapahnavā, tataśca tadāśrayamātraṃ vicāryam, tatra dharmabhūtajñānasya dravyatvaṃnyāyatattvātmasiddhibhāśyādisiddhamanusaratāṃ tanniṣṭhasmṛtyākhyavikārotpādakaḥ saṃskāro 'pi tanniṣṭhaḥ prāptaḥ; antaraṅgatvādabādhācca //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 4. Although in the <s>Gītā</s> verses such as "of each sense toward its sense-object" and others, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> states that <s>vāsanā</s> serves as a cause of activity only through the medium of desire (<s>icchā</s>), and hence there is no <s>karmavāsanā</s> (latent impression of action) distinct from a particular form of <s>jñānavāsanā</s> (latent impression of knowledge), nevertheless <s>jñānavāsanā</s> itself is undeniable. Therefore, only its substratum needs to be examined. In that regard, for those who follow [the view established in] the <s>Nyāyatattvātmasiddhi</s>, the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, and other [texts] that <s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s> (attributive consciousness) is a <s>dravya</s> (substance), the <s>saṃskāra</s> that generates the modification called <s>smṛti</s> (memory) residing in it also properly resides in it [i.e., in <s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s>]; because of its being more intimately connected, and because there is no sublation.

children.text:
nyā. pa. prame. 5 ye tu paraparibhāṣamanusarantastadanuguṇaṃ tasya guṇatvaṃ gṛhṇanti, teṣāmātmanyeva saṃskāraḥ, iti viśeṣaḥ /
na ca buddhornityatvaṃ saṃkocavikāsādidaśābhedaṃ cābhyupagacchadbhiradravyatvaṃ tasyāḥ suvacam; avasthāntarayogitvameva hyupādanatvam; tadeva hi dravyalakṣaṇam /
tathāpi naguṇatvahāniḥ; apṛthaksiddhaviśeṣaṇatvātiriktaguṇatvāvadarśanāt, karmavyatiriktajātimātrāśrayatvādirūpaguṇalakṣaṇasaṃketasyāsmābhiranādaraṇāt /
na ca dravyasyāśritasvabhāvatvalakṣaṇamapṛthaksiddhaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ viruddham, avayavini yuṣmābhirapi svīkaraṇāt /
yathā ca dravyatvaviśeṣaṇatvādibhirna virodha iṣyate, evamatrāpi, upalaṃmbhayuktyādeḥ sāmanacarcatvāt /
children.translated_text: Just as there is held to be no contradiction with substance-hood and attribute-hood, so too here, since the reasoning from apprehension and the like applies equally.

children.text: ato jñānaṃ dravyam, tadavasthāviśeṣāstvadravyāṇīti saṃskārākhyavikārāsthitirapi tatraiva yuktā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>jñāna</s> (consciousness) is a <s>dravya</s> (substance), and its particular states are <s>adravyas</s> (non-substances) — thus the persistence of the modification called <s>saṃskāra</s> in it alone is appropriate.

children.text: vegākhyastu saṃskārastadutpādakatvābhimatakarmaviśaiṣātirikto na dṛśyate, na ca yujyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃskāra</s> called <s>vega</s> (velocity), however, is not observed to be distinct from the particular <s>karma</s> (action) accepted as its cause, nor is it logically tenable [as distinct].

children.text: sthitasthāpakau tu karmanivṛttāvapi tadavinābhūtasaṃyogaviśeṣatvaṃ vaktuṃ yuktam //
children.translated_text: As for <s>sthitasthāpaka</s> (elasticity), it is appropriate to say that even after the cessation of <s>karma</s>, it is a particular conjunction inseparably associated with that [substance].

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 5. Those who, following the terminology of the other [school], accept its quality-nature accordingly — for them, <s>saṃskāra</s> resides in the self itself; this is the difference. Nor is it easy to maintain the non-substantiality of <s>buddhi</s> (cognition) for those who accept its permanence and also its states of contraction, expansion, and so forth; for being a substratum of different states is itself what constitutes being a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>); and that alone is the defining mark of <s>dravya</s> (substance). Even so, there is no loss of its quality-nature; because no quality-nature is observed beyond being an inseparable attribute (<s>apṛthaksiddhaviśeṣaṇa</s>), and because we do not accept the conventional definition of quality as what is a substratum of mere universals (<s>jāti</s>) other than <s>karma</s>. Nor is the inseparable-attribute nature — which is the defining mark of substance's dependent character — contradictory [with substance-hood], since even you [the opponent] accept it in the case of <s>avayavin</s> (composite wholes).

children.text: nyā. pa. prame. 6 ye ca bhagavatonantā maṅgalaguṇāḥ prakīrtyante, te sarvepi ṣāṅguṇyavitatirūpāḥ iti saṃmatam /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 6. The infinite auspicious qualities that are proclaimed of the Lord — it is accepted that all of them are of the nature of the expansion of the <s>ṣāḍguṇya</s> (six divine attributes).
As they say: "Of You who possess infinite qualities, the foremost are six qualities alone,
by which even other [qualities] have been established within the womb of the universe by You Yourself."

children.text:
iti /
ṣaṭsu ca guṇeṣu balaṃ dhāraṇasāmarthyam, aiśvaryaṃ niyamanaśaktiḥ; vikārahetuṣvapyavikṛtatvaṃ vīryam; tejaḥ parābhibhavanasāmarthyam, anyānapekṣatā veti /
lakṣitānāṃ caturṇāmatimathane jñānaśaktivitatirūpatvaṃ vyaktam /
na ca jñānaśaktyorapyevaṃ mithontarbhāvaḥ śakyaḥ, ajñeṣvapi dravyeṣu śaktidarśanāt, aśakteṣvapi jñānadarśanāt /
ata eva jñānaviśeṣaḥ śaktirityapi nirastam /
śaktiviśeṣastu jñānaṃ syāditi cet, kosau śaktiśabdārthaḥ ? /
vilakṣaṇo guṇaviśeṣaḥ prabhākarādinayena padārthāntaraṃ vā iti cet, na tarhi jñānasya tadviśeṣatā sidhyet /
atha kāryopayuktaviśeṣaṇamātraṃ śaktiriti sarvaprayogānugataṃ paśyasi, tadā na kevalaṃ jñānasya, api tu sarvasyaiva śaktitvaṃ prāptam, sarvasyāpi pradhānakāraṇatayābhimate kasmiṃścidviśeṣaṇatvenāvasthānāt /
nanvevamudayanādīnāmiva svarūpasahakārivyatiriktaśaktyabhāvaḥ prasaktaḥ iti cet, ananyathāsiddhayuktivaśādāgamabalādvā tatsiddheḥ /

children.translated_text: We say that the word [<s>śakti</s>] may apply [differently] depending on the particular intention of the speaker.
The extensive discussion for establishing <s>śakti</s> by our <s>Ācāryas</s> should be carefully studied in the <s>Nyāyakuliśa</s>.

The doctrines of the outsiders (<s>bāhyas</s>) that posit <s>śakti</s> alone as cause, etc., are not to be regarded, due to the absence of [support from] apprehension-based reasoning and authoritative scripture.

children.text: sā cedupādānaṃ, sūkṣmandravyamevāsau syāditi na vivādaḥ //
children.translated_text: If that [<s>śakti</s>] is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), then it would simply be a subtle substance — so there is no dispute.

Thus. Among the six qualities: <s>bala</s> (strength) is the capacity for sustaining; <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) is the power of commanding; remaining unchanged even when in contact with causes of modification is <s>vīrya</s> (valor); <s>tejas</s> (splendor) is the capacity to overpower others — or alternatively, independence [from others]. It is evident that the four thus defined are of the nature of the expansion of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>śakti</s> (power). Nor can <s>jñāna</s> and <s>śakti</s> similarly be subsumed under each other, since <s>śakti</s> is observed even in non-sentient substances, and <s>jñāna</s> is observed even in things devoid of [particular] <s>śakti</s>. For this very reason, the view that <s>śakti</s> is merely a particular form of <s>jñāna</s> is also rejected. If it be said that <s>jñāna</s> may be a particular form of <s>śakti</s> — what then is the meaning of the word <s>śakti</s>? If [you say] it is a distinctive quality, or a separate category following the method of <s>Prabhākara</s> and others — then the identity of <s>jñāna</s> with that particular form could not be established. If, on the other hand, you hold that <s>śakti</s> is merely a qualifier useful for producing effects — a meaning that pervades all usages — then not only <s>jñāna</s> but everything whatsoever would have the nature of <s>śakti</s>, since everything accepted as the principal cause of something abides as a qualifier in some respect. [Objection:] In that case, the consequence follows that, like <s>Udayana</s> and others, there would be no <s>śakti</s> distinct from the essential nature and auxiliary causes. [Reply:] [<s>Śakti</s>] is established either by force of reasoning that cannot be otherwise accounted for, or by the authority of scripture.

children.text:
nyā. pa. prame. 7 athāciddravyaviśeṣaguṇān paśyāmaḥ--- tatra śabdādayaḥ pañca tattadbhūtavartinaḥ pratyakṣādibalādabhyupagatāḥ /
sattvarajastamāṃsi ca śāstrānusāreṇa /
saṃyogaśca pratyakṣādisiddhaḥ /
nairantaryamātramevāyamiti cet, tat kiṃ dravyasvarūpam, utāganturavasthāviśeṣaḥ ? /
nādyaḥ, nityatvaprasaṅgāt /
na dvitīyaḥ, nāmāntareṇa tadabhidhānāt, iti /

children.translated_text: As for <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction) and <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness), they should be refuted by the reasoning already stated regarding <s>abhāva</s> (absence).

children.text: paratvāparatve api sukhādicchāyayā; na hi tattadupādhyavacchinnadeśakālaviśeṣasaṃbandhātirikte paratvāparatve paśyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>paratva</s> (remoteness) and <s>aparatva</s> (proximity) follow the same pattern as <s>sukha</s> and <s>icchā</s>; for we do not perceive <s>paratva</s> and <s>aparatva</s> as distinct from the relation to particular space and time delimited by particular limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>).

children.text: tatkalpane ca prāktvapratyaktvādayopi hi bahavo guṇāstulyanyāyāḥ kalpyāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: And if these were to be fabricated [as separate categories], then many other qualities such as priority, posteriority, and the like would have to be fabricated by the same logic.

children.text: evaṃ sadasadguṇapradarśanaprakriyayā saṃkhyāparimāṇagurutvadravatvasnehānāṃ tattvamavasātavyam, ityadravyeṣveṣā dik //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method of demonstrating valid and invalid qualities, the true nature of <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number), <s>parimāṇa</s> (measure), <s>gurutva</s> (heaviness), <s>dravatva</s> (fluidity), and <s>sneha</s> (viscosity) should be ascertained. This is the direction regarding non-substances.

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 7. Now let us examine the qualities pertaining to particular non-sentient substances (<s>acit-dravya</s>). Among these, the five — <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>rūpa</s> (color), and <s>gandha</s> (smell) — which pertain to the respective elements, are accepted on the strength of perception and other [means of knowledge]. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> [are accepted] in accordance with scripture. And <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) is established through perception and other [means]. [Objection:] Is it merely contiguity (<s>nairantarya</s>)? [Reply:] Is that the essential nature of the substance, or an adventitious state? Not the first, because [that would lead to] the unwanted consequence of permanence. Not the second, because it is denoted by a different name [than mere contiguity].

children.text: nyā. pa. prame. 8 atha dravyāṇi vimṛśyante--- tatra tāvat kaumārilābhimatavibhuśabdākhyadravyavādaḥ śabdasyācidavasthāviśeṣatvena śrutyādisiddhatvānnirākāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 8. Now substances are examined. Here, first: the doctrine accepted by the <s>Kumārila</s> [school] that <s>śabda</s> (sound) is an all-pervading substance is not to be rejected, since <s>śabda</s> is established through <s>Śruti</s> and other [authorities] as a particular state of non-sentient [matter].
The view expressed in the <s>Ātmasiddhi</s> that sound transcends its substrate and possesses movement — this should be understood as [operating] through the parts that constitute its material basis.
As for [the verse]: "<s>Tamas</s> (darkness) is indeed mobile, dark blue, possessing the distinction of far and near,
and it does not deserve to be separated from the nine well-known substances based on [alleged] dissimilarity from [known] substances" —

children.text: ityāhuḥ, tadetad dravyaṃ tāvadabhyupagacchāmaḥ; tathā hyuktaṃ varadagurubhistattvasāre--- "tamo nāma dravyaṃ bahulaviralaṃ mecakacalaṃ pratīmaḥ kenāpi kvacidapi na bādhaśca dadṛśe /
children.translated_text: thus they say. We accept that this [darkness] is indeed a substance. For the revered <s>Varadaguru</s> (<s>Varadaviṣṇumiśra</s>) has stated thus in the <s>Tattvasāra</s>: "We apprehend <s>tamas</s> as a substance — dense or sparse, dark, and mobile — by some [means]; and no sublation of this [perception] has been observed anywhere.

children.text: ataḥ kalpyo hetuḥ pramitirapi śābdī vijayate nirālokaṃ cakṣuḥ prathayati hi tad darśanavaśāt" //
children.translated_text: Therefore, a [separate] cause must be postulated; and <s>śābdī</s> (scriptural) cognition prevails [here]. For the eye, in the absence of light, reveals that [darkness] by the power of perception."

children.text:
iti /
etena viyati vitatānāṃ sūkṣmāṇāṃ pṛthivyavayavānāṃ kṛṣṇo guṇastama iti pakṣopi pratikṣiptaḥ; sāśrayasyaiva tasya grahaṇavirodhābhāvāt, guṇamātratayā ca kasyāpyanupalambhāt /
sparśarūparasānāṃ ca śabdagandhavad bhrāntau pramitau vā nirādhāragrahaṇādarśanācca--iti /
evaṃ dravyatve siddhe kṛṣṇavarṇasya dravyasya pṛthivītvamevābhyupagantumucitam, "yat kṛṣṇaṃ tadannasya" iti śruteḥ /
yadyapi pṛthivyāṃ pākaviśeṣavaśāt śuklādirūpaṃ, nānyatra pākādapi bhavati; ākāśādiṣu nailyopalambhopi hi pañcīkaraṇamūlapṛthivīsaṃsargāt /
"ākāśe cāviśeṣāt"iti sūtre bhāṣitam--- "aṇḍāntarvartinaścākāśasya trivṛtkaraṇopadeśapradarśintapañcīkaraṇena rūpavatvāccākṣuṣatvepyavirodhaḥ" iti /
nanvevamākāśameva dravyāntarasaṃsargānnīlaṃ tama ityupalabhyate iti syāditi cet, na syāt, ākāśe tama iti pṛthagupalambhasvārasyāt, dravnayāntaratve tu kalpanāgauravāt, antatotrāpi pañcīkaraṇena dravyāntarasaṃsargasyābhyupagatatvācca iti /
sparśānupalambhastu indranīlālokadurdinātapāderivānudbhavāderapi /
syāt /
na ca pārthivarūpasya sarvasyālokasāpekṣacakṣurgrāhyatvaniyamaḥ kalpyaḥ, karaṇavaicitryādiva viṣayavaicitryādapi vyavasthopapatteḥ /
divābhītānāṃ viśiṣṭāñjanarañjitākṣāṇāṃ cālokanirapekṣameva cakṣuṣaiva padārthā gṛhyante /
ālokābhāvamātre ca tamasi tamojyotiṣornivṛttivacanaṃ cavyāhanyeta, pratiniyatanailyāropakalpanāprayāsaśca /
ataḥ pṛthivīviśeṣatvaṃ tamaso yuktam /
pṛthivyādīni pañca bhūtāni manaśca triguṇadravyapariṇativiśeṣatayā śrutyādisiddhatvānna pṛthagdravyāṇi /
tatra cāvayavyākhyaṃ bhautikadravyam "tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ" ityādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ sūtrairbuddhiśabdāntarāderanyathāsiddhyādyupapādanena nirastam /
"mahaddīrghavadvā hvasvaparimaṇḍalābhyām" ityādibhiśca parāmabhimataḥ paramāṇuḥ /
ataḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣādupalambhayogyatvāyogyatvādidaśāviśeṣayogi prakṛtyādisaṃjñaṃ dravyaṃ vicitravyavasthitakramasamaṣṭivyaṣṭirūpamavatiṣṭhate /
diktattvamapi tattadupādhyavacchinnāstattaddeśaviśeṣā eva, atiriktakalpakānāṃ parāparapratyayaviśeṣādīnāmanyathāsiddheḥ /
digutpattiśrutiśca tadupādhikatannirvāhakasṛṣṭyopapannā; anyathā dyupṛthivyantarikṣādivat triguṇapariṇativiśeṣataiva syāt, na pṛthagdravyatā /
na caivaṃ kālepi prasaṅgaḥ, nityasya kālasya bhagavatparāśarādibhiḥ pṛthakprasaṃkhyānāt /
tasya prakṛtipariṇativiśeṣatvādipakṣāstatpūrvāparakālāvaśyaṃbhāvāt śrutyādibalācca pratyastāḥ /
atastriguṇakālāvātmāceti trīṇi siddhānir /

children.translated_text: But when <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is counted separately, [the substances are] four.

children.text: tasya hi cetanatvādibhiḥ saṃgrahasaṃbhavepyavāntaravailakṣaṇyajñāpanāya pṛthaksaṃkhyānaṃ prācāmanādivācāṃ ca, anyathā prakriyāntareṇācetaneṣvapi saṃgrahaprasaṃgāt /
children.translated_text: For even though He could be subsumed under [the category of] conscious beings through His possessing consciousness and the like, the separate enumeration is [made] in order to indicate His distinctive difference in subordinate aspects, and also because of the ancient Vedic statements; otherwise, by a different procedure, even insentient things could be subsumed [under the same category].

children.text: viviktaṃ ca bhagavatā parāśareṇa--- "paramātmātmanoryogaḥ paramārtha itīṣyate /
children.translated_text: And this has been clearly stated by the venerable <s>Parāśara</s>: "The union of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) and the <s>ātman</s> (individual self) is held to be the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>).
The other substance [i.e., matter] is false, since it does not attain the status of that [ultimate] substance."

Thus. By this, the view that <s>tamas</s> is a dark quality belonging to subtle particles of earth spread across space is also rejected; because that [quality] together with its substrate could be grasped without contradiction, and because no one apprehends a mere quality [without a substrate]. And since <s>sparśa</s> (touch), <s>rūpa</s> (color), and <s>rasa</s> (taste) — like <s>śabda</s> (sound) and <s>gandha</s> (smell) — are never observed to be grasped without a substrate, whether in erroneous or valid cognition. Thus, when its substance-hood is established, it is appropriate to accept this dark-colored substance as being of the nature of earth (<s>pārthiva</s>), based on the <s>Śruti</s>: "That which is dark belongs to food [i.e., earth]." Although in earth various colors such as white and others arise due to particular baking processes, this does not occur elsewhere even without baking; and the apprehension of dark-blue color in space and the like is due to admixture with earth based on <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> (quintuplication of elements). On the <s>Sūtra</s> "And in space, due to non-difference," the <s>Bhāṣya</s> states: "Since space within the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>) possesses color due to the <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> indicated by the teaching of <s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s> (triplication), there is no contradiction in its being visible to the eye." [Objection:] In that case, space itself, due to contact with another substance, is apprehended as being dark — that would be <s>tamas</s>. [Reply:] This is not so, because of the natural force of the separate apprehension of darkness in space [as distinct from space]; whereas if it were another substance [i.e., space itself], there would be excessive postulation; and ultimately, even in that case, contact with another substance through <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> is accepted. The non-apprehension of touch [in darkness] is [explained] as due to non-manifestation, as in the case of sapphire, light, overcast weather, sunshine, and the like. Nor should the rule be fabricated that all earthly color is graspable by the eye only in the presence of light, since systematic arrangement can be justified by variety in the object just as by variety in the instrument [of cognition]. For those who are active in darkness and those whose eyes are anointed with special collyrium grasp objects by the eye alone, independently of light. And [if tamas were mere absence of light,] the scriptural statement of the mutual cessation of darkness and light would be contradicted, along with the useless effort of postulating a definite superimposition of dark-blue [on each specific location]. Therefore, it is fitting that <s>tamas</s> is a particular form of earth. The five elements — earth and the rest — and <s>manas</s> (mind), being established through <s>Śruti</s> and other [authorities] as particular modifications of the substance possessing the three <s>guṇas</s> [i.e., <s>prakṛti</s>], are not separate substances. Therein, the composite substance (<s>avayavin</s>) called a physical product has been rejected by six <s>Sūtras</s> beginning with "Its non-difference [from <s>Brahman</s>], from the words 'origin' (<s>ārambhaṇa</s>)" and the like, by showing that <s>buddhi</s>, alternative terms, and so forth are otherwise explicable. And the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom) accepted by the opponent [is refuted] by [<s>Sūtras</s>] beginning with "As in the case of what is great or long — [the same objection applies] to what is short and spherical." Therefore, the substance designated as <s>prakṛti</s> and the like, which through particular modifications becomes fit or unfit for apprehension and undergoes various states, abides in the form of aggregate and individual in a variously arranged sequence. The category of <s>dik</s> (direction/space) too is nothing but those particular spatial locations delimited by particular limiting adjuncts, since the special cognitions of remoteness and proximity that [the opponent] postulates [as evidence for a separate category] are otherwise explicable. And the <s>Śruti</s> teaching the origin of <s>dik</s> is explained by the creation of the limiting adjuncts and their sustainer; otherwise, like heaven, earth, atmosphere, and the like, it would simply be a particular modification of the three-<s>guṇa</s> [<s>prakṛti</s>], not a separate substance. Nor does the same consequence apply to <s>kāla</s> (time), because <s>kāla</s>, being eternal, is separately enumerated by the revered <s>Parāśara</s> and others. The alternative views that it is a particular modification of <s>prakṛti</s>, etc., are rejected because they would necessitate a prior and subsequent time [leading to regress], and by the force of <s>Śruti</s> and other [authorities]. Thus, the three established [ultimate] realities are: the [substance possessing] three <s>guṇas</s> [i.e., <s>prakṛti</s>/non-sentient matter], <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>ātman</s> (self).

iti /
evaṃ dharmabhūtajñānākhyamapi dravyamajaḍatvāviśeṣepi spuṭataravaidharmyānatarabalāt pṛthaggaṇayanti /
tasyādravyatvavādaḥ keṣāñcinnāthamuniyāmunamunibhāṣyakārādiprabandhavirodhāt prāyaḥ paracittarañjanārthaḥ /
śuddhasattvākhyasya ca dravyāntarasya paravigrahādiyāthārthyopadeśapravṛttaniruktādyāptāgamasiddhatvāt sūkṣmatriguṇāvasthāviśeṣādipakṣā bahiṣkāryāḥ /
ataḥ ṣaḍetāni dravyāṇi /
bhoktṛbhogyaniyantṝṇāṃ sadātmanaikadravyatvādipakṣā api nirviśeṣasanmātrapakṣavad vyāghātaśrutivirodhādibhirbahuśo bhāṣyādiṣu nirastāḥ /

kṣaṇalavādyātmā kālaḥ /
aṇurjñātā jīvaḥ /

children.translated_text: And <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>).
<s>Mati</s> (cognition) is a particular attribute of the cognized object, being the distinctive cause of the activity of knowing.

Thus, the division of substances is sixfold, in the form of: <s>triguṇa</s> (primordial matter), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), <s>śuddhasattva</s> (pure <s>sattva</s>), and <s>mati</s> (cognition).

Thus, for those who wish to traverse the entire range of knowable objects — both substance (<s>dravya</s>) and non-substance (<s>adravya</s>) — by the royal highway of the caravan of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), there shall be no falling into the pitfalls of sophistical reasoning fabricated by heterodox thinkers and non-Vedic [philosophers].

Thus.
Likewise, the substance called <s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s> (attributive knowledge), though not different [from other substances] in being non-inert, is counted separately due to the preponderance of its more manifest dissimilarity.
The view held by some that it is not a substance contradicts the treatises of <s>Nāthamuni</s>, <s>Yāmunamuni</s>, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Rāmānuja</s>), and others, and is mostly intended to please the minds of opponents.
And since the separate substance called <s>śuddhasattva</s> (pure <s>sattva</s>) is established by reliable traditional sources (<s>āptāgama</s>) such as the <s>Nirukta</s> and others — which proceed from the teaching of the reality of the Lord's divine body and the like — the positions that it is a particular state of the subtle <s>triguṇa</s> (three qualities) and the like must be excluded.
Therefore, these substances are six.
The positions that the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), the enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>), and the controller (<s>niyantṛ</s>) have eternal identity as one substance, and the like, have been refuted many times in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and other works — by self-contradiction, conflict with <s>Śruti</s>, and so forth — just as the position of bare undifferentiated being (<s>nirviśeṣasanmātra</s>) [has been refuted].
Therein, <s>triguṇa</s> (primordial matter with three qualities) and <s>śuddhasattva</s> (pure <s>sattva</s>) are to be characterized by their own respective etymologies.
<s>Kāla</s> (time) is that whose nature is moments, instants, and the like.
The <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is an atomic knower.

children.text: iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu nyāyapariśuddhau prameyādhyāye prathamamāhnikam //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the works of <s>Śrī Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the <s>Vedāntācārya</s> (teacher of <s>Vedānta</s>), the lion among poets and logicians (<s>kavitārkikasiṃha</s>), master of all systems (<s>sarvatantrasvatantra</s>), in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in the chapter on <s>Prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge) — the first session (<s>āhnika</s>).
The chapter on <s>Prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge).
Second session (<s>āhnika</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. prame. 9 atra yadyapi pramāviṣayaḥ prameyamiti vyutpattyā āropitākāravyavacchedārthayā anāropitarūpaṃ sarvaṃ prameyam, tathāpi niḥśreyasāntaraṅgatayā tadarthibhiḥ prakarṣeṇa meyaṃ prameyamiha vivakṣim /
yadviṣayeṇa bhrameṇa saṃsarāmaḥ, yadviṣayeṇa ca tattvajñānenāpavarjyemahi, tadiha naḥ prakarṣeṇa meyaṃ prameyam /
tacca dvādaśavidhamuktamākṣapāde--- "ātmaśarīrendriyārthabuddhimanaḥ pravṛttidoṣapretyabhāvaphaladuḥkhāpavargāḥ prameyam" iti /
tatra cetana ātmā /
sa dvidhār---iśvaronīśvara iti /
jagatkartār iśvaraḥ /
jagadvyāpārarahitaścetanonīśvaraḥ /
yaccaitanyasamānādhikaraṇaṃ yadapṛthaksiddhaṃ yaddravyaṃ, tat tasya śarīram /
tad dvividham---karmajam, akarmajaṃ ceti /
ādyamasmadādīnām /
dvitīyamīśvarādīnām /
sāttvikāhaṅkāropādānakaṃ dravyamindriyam /
tadekādaśavidham---pañca jñānendriyāṇi, pañcakarmenidrayāṇi manaśceti /
indriyagocarā ihārthāḥ /
te ca śabdādayo guṇāḥ tadviśiṣṭāni ca /
arthaprakāśo buddhiḥ /
smṛtyādikaraṇamindriyaṃ manaḥ /
manovākkāyānāṃ puṇyāpuṇyarūpo vyāpāra iha pravṛttiḥ /
tathāvidhapravṛttihetavo doṣāḥ /
te ca saṃgrahādrāgadveṣamohāḥ /
pūrvadehaṃ vihāyottaradehaprāptiḥ pretyabhāvaḥ /
pravṛttisādhyaṃ phalam; tadeva puruṣeṇa pravṛttiphalatayoddiṣṭaṃ prayojanam /
pratikūlavedanīyaṃ duḥkham /
tatra sukhatatsādhanādikamapi viṣasaṃpṛktamadhuvat prabhūtānarthānuṣaṅgitvād duḥkhameva mumukṣuṇā bhāvyamiti tasyāpi pratikūlavedanīyatvam /
duḥkhāntarakāraṇāsamānādhikaraṇā duḥkhanivṛttirapavargaḥ /
sa ca svābhāvikātmasvarūpāvirbhāvapūrvakasamastavibhūtiguṇaviśiṣṭaniratiśayānandabrahmānubhavagarbhaḥ iti paramapuruṣārthaḥ /
tatpūrvako vā tādṛśabrahmānubhavopavargaḥ iti /
etadeva ca prameyaṃ saṃgrahāccaturdhā vibhajya kecidanusaṃdadhate--- 'heyam, tasya nivartakam, hānam, tasyopāyaḥ' iti /
ye tu kaṇacaraṇādayaḥ ṣaṭsaptādirūpeṇa sarvān padārthān vibhajya parīkṣante, te sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyādīnāṃ padārthāntaratvapratikṣepeṇa nirastāḥ /
tataśca dravyaguṇakarmāṇi trīṇyevāvaśiṣyante /
tatrāpi karmaṇaḥ saṃpratipannaguṇātiriktatvapakṣepi saṃskārādiguṇāvāntaraviśeṣavad guṇapakṣakakṣīkārāt dvau padārthau /
tatra ca guṇaśabdasyāpṛthaksiddhaviśeṣaṇamātravyutpannasya tathāvidheṣu keṣucid dravyeṣvapi vṛtterdravyaguṇarūpeṇa vibhāgānaucityād dravyamadravyamityeva padārthavibhāgamādriyāmaher, idṛśasya tu vicārasyāpavarge paraṃparayopayogaḥ /
mumukṣūṇāṃ pradhānatamaṃ tu prameyaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ brahmaikameveti manvāno bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ--- "athāto brahmajijñāsā" ityupakramya tadeva saprakāraṃ nirūpitavān; tatprakāratayaivānyat prameyam /
kecittu dehātmavivekakramānusāreṇa "bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā" iti śrutiprakriyayā ca tridhā tattvaṃ vibhajya cintayanti, tatrāpi saprakāradravyacintanādadravyacintāpyantarbhavati /
tattulyanyāyatayā kālacintā ca /
tadabhiprāyeṇa kālasya padārthaviśeṣaṇatayaiva samastavastupratītyantarbhāvānna pṛthagastitvādayo vaktavyāḥ, na ca parihartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In accordance with that intention, since <s>kāla</s> (time) is included within the cognition of all things merely as a qualifier of [other] categories, its existence and the like need not be stated separately, nor should they be avoided [as a topic].

children.text: "kālosti nāstīti vyavahāro vyavahartṝṇāṃ jātyādyastitvanāstitvavyavahāratulyaḥ" iti jainanirākaraṇasamaye bhāṣyakārairuktamātataśca brahmaikameva tattvamiti vā cidacidīśvarabhedena trīṇi tattvānīti vā paśyatāṃ na kaśvidviśeṣaḥ, svarūpabhedasya viśiṣṭaikyasya cobhayeṣāmabhimatatvāt /
children.translated_text: "The usage 'time exists' or 'does not exist' is analogous to the usage about the existence or non-existence of universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like" — this was stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Rāmānuja</s>) at the time of refuting the <s>Jaina</s> [position]. And thus, for those who hold that <s>Brahman</s> alone is the [ultimate] reality, or that there are three realities in the form of the distinction between sentient (<s>cit</s>), insentient (<s>acit</s>), and the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — there is no difference, since both [groups] accept both essential difference and qualified unity.
For this very reason — "<s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self), <s>Vyakta</s> (manifest matter), and <s>Kāla</s> (time), taken separately,
are the forms that are the causes of sustenance, creation, dissolution, manifestation, and existence."

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 9. Here, although by the etymology "<s>prameya</s> is that which is the object of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>)" — which serves to exclude superimposed appearances — everything in its unsuperimposed form is <s>prameya</s>, nevertheless, what is intended here is <s>prameya</s> in the sense of that which is preeminently to be known (<s>meya</s>) by those who seek it, as being intimately connected with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
That regarding which we wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> through error, and that regarding which we would be liberated through knowledge of reality — that is for us the preeminent <s>prameya</s>.
And that has been stated as twelvefold by <s>Ākṣapāda</s> (<s>Gautama</s>): "<s>Ātman</s> (self), <s>śarīra</s> (body), <s>indriya</s> (sense organs), <s>artha</s> (objects), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), <s>doṣa</s> (defects), <s>pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration), <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — these are <s>prameya</s>."
Therein, the <s>ātman</s> is conscious. It is of two kinds — <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and <s>anīśvara</s> (the non-Lord, i.e., the individual soul).
<s>Īśvara</s> is the creator of the world. The conscious being who is devoid of world-creative activity is the <s>anīśvara</s> (individual soul).
Whatever is co-located with that consciousness, inseparably established in it, and is a substance — that is its <s>śarīra</s> (body). It is of two kinds: born of <s>karma</s>, and not born of <s>karma</s>. The first belongs to us and others [i.e., bound souls]. The second belongs to <s>Īśvara</s> and others [i.e., liberated souls].
The substance that has as its material cause the <s>sāttvika ahaṅkāra</s> (the ego-principle predominating in <s>sattva</s>) is the <s>indriya</s> (sense organ). It is of eleven kinds: five <s>jñānendriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs), five <s>karmendriyas</s> (motor organs), and <s>manas</s> (mind).
The objects of the sense organs are here called <s>arthas</s> (objects). These are qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) such as sound and the like, and [substances] qualified by them.
<s>Buddhi</s> (cognition) is the illumination of objects.
<s>Manas</s> (mind) is the internal organ that serves as the instrument of memory and the like.
<s>Pravṛtti</s> (activity) here means the activity of mind, speech, and body in the form of merit and demerit.
<s>Doṣas</s> (defects) are the causes of such activity. These are, in summary: <s>rāga</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion).
<s>Pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration) is the abandoning of the former body and the attaining of a subsequent body.
<s>Phala</s> (fruit) is the result accomplished through activity; that very thing, being aimed at by the person as the fruit of activity, is the <s>prayojana</s> (purpose).
<s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is that which is experienced as adverse. Therein, even pleasure and its means and the like, being accompanied by abundant misfortune — like honey mixed with poison — must be regarded by a seeker of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) as suffering itself; thus that too has the character of being experienced as adverse.
<s>Apavarga</s> (liberation) is the cessation of suffering that is not co-located with any other cause of suffering. And it contains within it the experience of <s>Brahman</s> as unsurpassed bliss (<s>niratiśayānanda</s>), qualified by all divine attributes (<s>guṇa</s>) and glories (<s>vibhūti</s>), preceded by the manifestation of the natural essential form of the self — thus it is the supreme goal of human life (<s>paramapuruṣārtha</s>). Or, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is such experience of <s>Brahman</s>, preceded by that [manifestation].
And some synthesize this very <s>prameya</s> into fourfold form: "that which is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>), its remover, the abandonment (<s>hāna</s>), and the means to it."
As for those such as the followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and others who classify and examine all categories (<s>padārthas</s>) in the form of six, seven, and so on — they have been refuted by rejecting the status of <s>sāmānya</s> (universals), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularities), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and the like as separate categories.
Thus only three remain: <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karma</s> (action).
And even among those, since <s>karma</s> (action), even on the view that it differs from recognized qualities, is subsumed under the category of <s>guṇa</s> — just as sub-varieties of quality such as <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) and the like are — [there are really only] two categories. And since the word <s>guṇa</s>, being etymologically understood as merely an inseparable attribute, applies also to certain substances of such a nature, the division into substance and quality is not appropriate; therefore we favor the division of categories as simply <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>adravya</s> (non-substance). However, such deliberation has only an indirect utility for liberation.
But the venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, holding that the paramount <s>prameya</s> for seekers of liberation is one alone — <s>Brahman</s> in its qualified form (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>) — beginning with "Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>" has established that very [<s>Brahman</s>] along with its modes; all other <s>prameya</s> is [understood] only as a mode of that.
Some, however, following the order of discriminating body from self, and in accordance with the Vedic procedure stated in "knowing the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the impeller," divide reality (<s>tattva</s>) into three and reflect upon it; even there, reflection on non-substance is included within the reflection on substance with its modes. And by the same principle, reflection on <s>kāla</s> (time) is also [included].

children.text: ityādyanusāreṇa caturdhā pañcadhā vā vibhajya cintayatāṃ kāryaviśeṣaiḥ saha pañcaṣaṭsaptaviṃśatyādisaṃkhyāṃ niveśayatāṃ ca pūrvāviśeṣa eva /
children.translated_text: In accordance with such [statements], for those who reflect by dividing [reality] into four or five, and for those who assign the count of twenty-five, twenty-six, twenty-seven, and so on by including particular effects — [there is] no difference from the previous [positions].
And it is heard [in scripture]: "Some call that the twenty-sixth, and others [call it] the twenty-seventh;
the wise knowers of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system and of the <s>Atharvaśiras</s> know the <s>Puruṣa</s> as beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)."
Thus.

children.text: prāpyam, prāptā, prāptyupāyaḥ, nivartyaṃ, phalaṃ ceti kecit pañcadhā prameyaṃ parisaṃcakṣate /
children.translated_text: Some describe the <s>prameya</s> in fivefold form: that which is to be attained (<s>prāpya</s>), the attainer (<s>prāptṛ</s>), the means of attainment (<s>prāptyupāya</s>), that which is to be removed (<s>nivartya</s>), and the fruit (<s>phala</s>).
Others [describe it as] sixfold, by including the specific relationship (<s>saṃbandhaviśeṣa</s>).

children.text:
nyā. pa. prame. 10 athāyamaparaḥ pravṛttyarthaḥ saṃgrahonuṣṭhānaparihārāntaraṅgaḥ; tathāhi--- hitamahitaṃ ca prakarṣeṇa meyam /
tatra laukikahitāhitayoranvayavyatirekāyurvedanītiśāstrādikaṃ pramāṇam; tadapi yogasādhanabhūtaśarīrarakṣaṇārthaṃ mumukṣuṇāpi śrutismṛtyādyavirodhenānusaraṇīyam /
alaukikahitāhitayostu vedāḥ pramāṇam /
tadupabṛṃhaṇatayā smṛtītihāsapurāṇāni ca /
yacca śrutivihitam, tadakhilamapi yathādhikāraṃ hitam /
yacca tanniṣiddham, tadakhilamapyahitam /
nanvabhicārādikarmaṇāmanarthahetūnāṃ kṣudrapuruṣārthasādhanānāṃ ca kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ kathaṃ hitatvam ?; ucyate---adhikāriviśeṣamapekṣya hi sarvo vidhirniṣedhaśca; yathoktam--- "traiguṇyaviṣayā vedāḥ" iti /
yo hi sukhaṃ duḥkhanivṛttiṃ cecchati tasya tatsādhanamapekṣamāṇasya laukikeṣu sādhaneṣu pravṛttasya teṣāṃ nirayādihetubhūtānarthahetutvena tatparihārāyānarthahetutvarahitāḥ sukhādyupāyāḥ pratipādyante /
evaṃ kāmyakarmāṇi pāralaukikāni dṛṣṭajātīyatadadhikaphalārthatayā dṛṣṭānarthāvahasukhapravṛttipratibandhaupayikatvād hitānyeva rāgiṇām /
tathā aihalaukikānyapi citrādīni /
kārīryādīni tu jagaddhitānyapi /
abhicārakarmaṇopi hiṃsādiyuktasyāpi svarūpato nānarthahetutvam,tadaṅgapaśuhiṃsāderagnīṣomīyādivadvidhiprāptatvāt, api tu svasādhyenāprāptaviṣayavadhādinā /
tadapekṣayā cābhicāro niṣidhyate /
sopi hi kvacidavaśyakartavya eva, "ṣaṭsvanabhicaran patet" ityādidarśanāt /
ataśca mumukṣorapi rakṣakakṣatriyādyabhāve rākṣasādyabhibhave cātmarakṣaṇārthamabhicāraḥ kartavya eva, "sarvata evātmānaṃ gopāyet" iti śāstrāt, anyathā aharaharanuṣṭheyasyāprayāṇādanuvartanīyasya karmāderucchedaprasaṅgenopāyāniṣpattermokṣāsiddhiprasaṅgāt /
vṛṣṭyannādidṛṣṭārthāni ca sarvāṇyupāsananiṣpattyaupayikatayā tattadapekṣāyāmanuṣṭheyāni /
pāralaukikāni tu tatphalābhisaṃdhiviraheṇa karmayogānuṣṭhānadaśāyāṃ nityanaimittikairekīkṛtya kartavyāni /
naimittikāni hi sarvāṇi prasaktānarthaparihārārthatayā sarvahitānyeva /
evaṃ nityāni, uttarakarmādhikārārthatvādakaraṇanimittapratyavāyaparihārārthatvācca /
ataḥ śrutivihitaṃ svavarṇāśramocitaṃ sarvaṃ hitameva /
ata eva hi smaranti--- "śāstraṃ hi vatsalataraṃ mātāpitṛsahasrataḥ" iti /
evaṃ sthite pravāhānādisāmagrīcakravaśādaniyatasamayasamāgatasakalasaiddhāntikasamālambanīyasucar itaparipākanivṛttapratibandhaparamapuruṣakaṭākṣaviśeṣasamunmiṣitasattvasāmarthyena karatalāmalakavadālokitaheyopādeyavibhāgasyānādyanantabahuvidhadurviṣahaduḥkhānuṣaṅgadūṣitālpāsthirasāṃsārikasukhamayaviṣamadhuviraktasya samastaduritavargāpavargāyamāṇanityaniratiśayānandamukundacaraṇāravindasevāmakarandalampaṭasya yathāśakti varṇāśramocitanityanaimittikaniṣiddhaparihārasahakṛtaṃ darśanasamānākāradhruvānusmṛtirūpaṃ bhagavadupāsanaṃ hitatamaṃ vihitam /

children.translated_text: And that [meditation] is of many kinds — according to the distinctions of <s>Sadakṣara</s> (the six-syllabled [mantra]), <s>Nyāsa</s> (surrender), <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Bhūma</s>, <s>Dahara</s>, and so on — and is to be accomplished by those of the three higher <s>varṇas</s> in all <s>āśramas</s>.
And since it has the nature of unsurpassed love (<s>prīti</s>) directed toward a most exalted object, it is denoted by the word <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).

children.text: ayameva ca paramo yogastrayyantānuvidhāyiṣu sarveṣu mokṣaśāstreṣu pratipādyate; yathāha bhagavān parāśaraḥ--- "ātmaprayatnasāpekṣā viśiṣṭā yā manogatiḥ /
children.translated_text: And this supreme <s>yoga</s> is taught in all the treatises on liberation that follow the conclusion of the three <s>Vedas</s> (<s>trayyanta</s>); as the venerable <s>Parāśara</s> has said: "That distinguished mental movement (<s>manogati</s>) which depends on the self's own effort,
its conjunction with <s>Brahman</s> is called <s>Yoga</s>."

<s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, <s>Prameya</s> section 10. Now, here is another summary pertaining to practical engagement, being intimately connected with performance and avoidance. Thus: what is beneficial (<s>hita</s>) and what is harmful (<s>ahita</s>) is preeminently to be known.
Therein, for worldly benefit and harm, the <s>pramāṇas</s> are <s>Āyurveda</s> (medical science), <s>Nītiśāstra</s> (political science), and the like, [established] through agreement and difference; even these should be followed by a seeker of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) without contradicting <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and the like — for the purpose of protecting the body, which serves as an instrument for the practice of <s>yoga</s>.
But for supra-mundane benefit and harm, the <s>Vedas</s> are the <s>pramāṇa</s>. And <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇas</s> serve as supplements to them.
Whatever is enjoined by <s>Śruti</s> — all of that, according to one's eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>), is beneficial. And whatever is prohibited by it — all of that is harmful.
If one objects: how can sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>) and other rituals that cause harm, and desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) rituals that serve petty human goals, be beneficial? — [the answer is:] every injunction and prohibition is relative to a particular qualified person (<s>adhikārin</s>). As it has been stated: "The <s>Vedas</s> have the three <s>guṇas</s> as their domain."
For one who desires pleasure and cessation of pain, when he, depending on means to that end, has engaged in worldly means — since those [worldly means] cause misfortune as the cause of hell and the like — in order to avoid that, means to pleasure and the like that are free from being causes of misfortune are taught.
Thus, desire-motivated rituals pertaining to the next world, since they serve to obstruct engagement in pleasures that bring visible harm — by presenting results of the same type but superior to the desired [worldly] result — are indeed beneficial for those who have attachment.
Likewise, even worldly [rituals] such as <s>citra</s> (ornamental rites) and the like. And <s>kārīrya</s> and similar [rites] are beneficial for the world as well.
Even the sorcery ritual (<s>abhicāra</s>), though involving violence and the like, is not in its essential nature a cause of harm — because the animal violence that is its subsidiary element is scripturally sanctioned just as in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and similar [sacrifices]; rather, [it becomes harmful] through its intended effect of killing and the like, which targets a person not otherwise [legitimately] to be killed.
And it is with reference to that [illegitimate effect] that sorcery is prohibited.
Yet even it is absolutely obligatory in certain cases, as is seen from [the injunction] "in six [situations], one who does not perform <s>abhicāra</s> falls."
Therefore, even for a seeker of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), in the absence of a protecting <s>Kṣatriya</s> ruler and the like, and when overwhelmed by demons (<s>Rākṣasas</s>) and so forth, sorcery must indeed be performed for self-protection — based on the scriptural teaching "one should protect oneself by all means"; otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that the daily and other obligatory rituals to be performed until death would be cut off, resulting in the failure of the means [to liberation] and hence the failure of liberation itself.
And all [rituals] whose visible purposes are rain, food, and the like should be performed as needed, since they are conducive to the accomplishment of meditation (<s>upāsana</s>).
But supra-mundane [desire-motivated rituals] should be performed during the stage of practicing <s>Karmayoga</s>, unified with the obligatory and occasional rites, without aiming at their [specific] fruits.
For all occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) rites, being intended to avert impending misfortune, are beneficial for all.
Likewise the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) rites, since they serve as qualification for subsequent rituals and since they avert the adverse consequences of non-performance.
Therefore, everything enjoined by <s>Śruti</s> and appropriate to one's own <s>varṇa</s> (social class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) is entirely beneficial.
For this very reason it is remembered: "The scripture is more affectionate than a thousand mothers and fathers."
This being established, for one whose <s>sattva</s> capacity has been awakened by the special grace of the Supreme Person — [that grace being] the culmination of matured good conduct relied upon by all established authorities, arriving at an indeterminate time through the wheel of beginningless causal assemblages in a continuous flow — one who has thereby perceived, as clearly as a fruit in his palm, the distinction between what is to be rejected and what is to be embraced; who has become disenchanted with the worldly pleasure that is like poison-laced honey — tainted by the association with beginningless, endless, manifold, unbearable suffering, meager and unstable; who is ardently devoted to the lotus feet of <s>Mukunda</s> — whose service is like a jewel-box of eternal, unsurpassed bliss that effects liberation from the entire mass of sins — for such a one, the supremely beneficial thing enjoined is <s>bhagavad-upāsana</s> (meditation on the Lord), which has the form of steady recollection (<s>dhruvānusmṛti</s>) of the same nature as direct vision, assisted by the obligatory and occasional rites appropriate to one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, along with the avoidance of prohibited acts, all performed to the best of one's ability.
Thus.

children.text: smarati ca bhagavān śāṇḍilyarḥ--- "idṛśaḥ paramātmāyaṃ pratyagātmāva tathedṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the venerable <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> remembers: "Such is this <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), and such likewise is the individual self (<s>pratyagātman</s>);
the contemplation of their relationship is proclaimed as <s>Yoga</s>."

children.text:
iti /
tatra cidacidvivekādimātre sāṃkhyamupakurute /
yamaniyamādisamādhiparikaraśodhane yogaḥ /

children.translated_text: The <s>Karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritualistic portion of the Vedas) and the like [assist] in the specifics of what is to be done (<s>itikartavyatā</s>).
The <s>Pañcarātra</s> [assists] in all [aspects] everywhere.
Regarding the prohibited and desire-motivated classes [of action], and regarding those obligatory [duties] that are purposeless [when considered independently],
the injunction of <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the like does not contradict [their] performance elsewhere.

Thus.
Therein, <s>Sāṃkhya</s> assists with regard to the mere discrimination of sentient and insentient. <s>Yoga</s> [assists] in the purification of the auxiliaries to <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), such as <s>yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), and the like.

children.text: soyamevaṃvidhaḥ paramayogākhyo dharmaḥ "mayyeva mana ādhatsva" iti gīyate /
children.translated_text: This very <s>dharma</s> of such a nature, called the supreme <s>yoga</s>, is sung [in the <s>Gītā</s>]: "Fix your mind on Me alone."

children.text: tadaśaktasya, "atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram /
children.translated_text: For one who is incapable of that: "If you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me,
then seek to attain Me through the <s>yoga</s> of repeated practice (<s>abhyāsayoga</s>), O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.
If you are incapable even of practice, then be one whose supreme [devotion] is in performing actions for My sake."

children.text:
ityādinā pūrvaparvāṇi vidhīyante /
yaḥ prītipūrvabhagavadasādhāraṇakarmaṇyapi na samarthaḥ, tasya viṣayarasavaimukhyajananāya samastavaiṣayikasukhaśeṣitvena cirataramanusaṃhitasyāpi svātmanaḥ sāṃsārikasamastasukhasamadhikānandasvarūpamālokayitumāntaracakṣurvirodhitimirapaṭalapāṭanāya jñānakarmayogākhye dve bheṣaje /
tatrātmacintanarūpo jñānayogastadālokanentaraṅgabhūtaḥ /
tatrāpyasamarthasya tadadhikārasiddhyarthaṃ karmayogaḥ /
tena tatra siddhādhikārasyāpi śiṣṭatayā vyapadeśyasyāntargatātmajñānaḥ karmayoga eva kāryaḥ /

children.translated_text: Otherwise, even for such a person, <s>jñānayoga</s> too would be obstructed by the greater sin rooted in generating a distinction of understanding between the man of complete knowledge and the man of incomplete knowledge who is incapable of <s>jñānayoga</s>.

children.text: tādṛśenaiva ca karmayogena sukaratvādiguṇavatā cirataramanuṣṭhitena jñānayogavyavadhānamantareṇāpyātmāvalokanaṃ sidhyati /
children.translated_text: And by that very <s>karmayoga</s>, which possesses the merit of being easy to perform and so forth, when practiced for a long time, the vision of the Self is accomplished even without the intervention of <s>jñānayoga</s>.

children.text: karmayogepyasamarthastu vikalamapi karmayogamārabheta, "nehābhikramanāśosti pratyavāyo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: One who is incapable even of <s>karmayoga</s> should undertake even an incomplete <s>karmayoga</s> — 'In this [path] there is no loss of effort, nor is there any adverse consequence;
even a little of this <s>dharma</s> protects from great fear.'

Thus by such [passages], the preceding stages are enjoined. For one who is not even capable of performing the special acts of devotion preceded by love toward the Lord, two remedies called <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action) are prescribed — for generating aversion to sense-pleasures, and for removing the cataract of obstruction from the inner eye so as to behold one's own Self, whose essential nature is bliss equal to or surpassing all worldly pleasures, even though it has been for the longest time contemplated as subordinate to all sensory enjoyments. Of these, <s>jñānayoga</s>, which consists of contemplation of the Self, is the more proximate means to that [Self-]vision. And for one incapable even of that, <s>karmayoga</s> is prescribed for the attainment of qualification for it. Therefore, even for one whose qualification [for <s>jñānayoga</s>] has been established, <s>karmayoga</s> alone — with the knowledge of the Self included within it, and being fit to be designated as a disciplined person — is to be practiced.

children.text:
ityādibhirvaiṅkalyavicchedādisaṃbhavepi phalāvinābhāvādipratipādanāt /
prakramamātreṇāpi prasanno bhagavān pauṣkalyamāpādayati /
sarveṣu cāmīṣu parvasu tattatsāmagrīcakraghaṭanāya tattatphalapradānāya ca sa eva hi śaraṇamanusaraṇīyaḥ /
tathā cāmananti--- "sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ" iti /
sa eva paramapuruṣo vaśīkāryakāṣṭhā paramaprāpyaścetyarthaḥ /
"tasya ca vaśīkaraṇaṃ taccharaṇāgatireva" iti bhāṣyam /

children.translated_text: Thus, a mere indication of the most beneficial form of worship (<s>upāsana</s>) has been shown.
And the fruit, in the form of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), has been characterized earlier.

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tu dehavicchedamātrasahasrayuvatisaṃbhogasamastālīkaviṣayavijñānasaṃtānocchedavāsanātyantavirāmaviṣayoparāgavaidhuryanityordhvagamanasakalalokamastakopariniviṣṭasādhāraṇadehaviśeṣānupraveśanirāvaraṇatvasvānandānubhavasvātantryalābhaśivasārūpyaśivāpatticicchaktipariśeṣāvidyānivṛttyupādhinivṛttisakalavaiśeṣikaguṇocchedaprabhṛtayo niḥśreyasavikalpā dehādyatiriktātmasadbhāvabāhyārthapāramārthikatvatattadāgamāprāmāṇyabrahmanirvikāratvanirdeṣatvatajjñānānandanityatvādisamarthakaiḥ śārīrakaparyantaiḥ śāstraiḥ pratikṣepyā; iti tatra tatra vistaro draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the alternative conceptions of the highest good held by others — mere separation from the body, enjoyment of a thousand celestial maidens, cessation of the continuum of cognition of all illusory objects, complete and permanent cessation of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), freedom from attachment to objects, permanent upward ascent, entry into a special common body situated atop all worlds, attainment of freedom from obstruction, experience of one's own bliss, attainment of independence, attainment of <s>Śiva</s>'s form (<s>śivasārūpya</s>), becoming <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivāpatti</s>), power of will, cessation of residual <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), cessation of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), destruction of all the distinctive qualities [of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system], and so forth — these are to be refuted by the <s>Śārīraka</s> (Brahmasūtra) and other scriptures that establish the existence of a Self distinct from the body and so forth, the reality of external objects, the invalidity of the respective <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures) [of those schools], the immutability of <s>Brahman</s>, its being beyond defects, and the eternality of its knowledge and bliss. The detailed treatment is to be seen in the respective places.

children.text: iha tu pramāṇacintāyāḥ paramaprayojanaṃ darśayituṃ prameyasya saṃgrahoktiḥ, saparikarapramāṇamaryādāpratipādanaparatvānnyāyavistaraśāstrasya, iti //
children.translated_text: Here, however, for showing the supreme purpose of the investigation of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge), a summary statement of the <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge) [is given], since the <s>Nyāyavistara</s> science is devoted to establishing the bounds of the means of knowledge together with their auxiliaries.

Thus, by such statements establishing the unfailing connection with the fruit even when there is incompleteness, interruption, and so forth. By mere commencement alone, the Lord, being pleased, brings about fulfillment. And in all these stages, for the assemblage of the respective causal conditions and for the bestowal of the respective fruits, He alone is the refuge to be resorted to. Thus they declare — 'That is the supreme limit, that is the highest goal.' The meaning is: that Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>) alone is the limit of what is to be brought under control and the supreme object to be attained. 'And the means of bringing Him under control is taking refuge in Him (<s>śaraṇāgati</s>) alone' — thus the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary).

children.text: nyā. pa. prame. 11 svātantryeṇa mitaṃ sukhetaratayā yadbhāti jantoridaṃ sarvaṃ yasya vibhūtirivyavasitaṃ svādaṃ vyanakti svakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Nyā. Pa. Prame.</s> 11. May that Blessed Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), the ocean of infinite bliss, the Lord of the Self (<s>ātmeśvara</s>), Himself reveal Himself within the hearts of those like me who have anointed eyes [of devotion] — He whose glory is all this [universe], which by His sovereignty appears as independently existing, and which manifests, as it were, His own flavor [of being] through its appearance as pleasure and such to beings.

children.text: antaḥsvāntamanantanandathunidhirmedodṛśāṃ mādṛśā- māvirbhāvayatu svayaṃ sa bhagavānātmānamātmeśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: May He, of His own accord, manifest Himself within the hearts of those like me who have anointed eyes [of devotion], He who is the treasure-house of infinite bliss.

children.text: yatrodāsata jaiminiprabhṛtayaḥ śrutyarthacintāparāḥ yasyāṃ kandalayanti mandamatayaḥ pāriplavān viplavān /
children.translated_text: In the [domain of reasoning] where <s>Jaimini</s> and other authorities, devoted to the investigation of Vedic meaning, came to rest,

children.text: viśveṣāmiha veṅkaṭeśaviduṣā viśrāntaye vādināṃ prācī nītiṣu paryaśodhi saraṇiḥ pracchāyaniṣkaṇṭakā //
children.translated_text: and in which those of dull intellect generate tossing waves of confusion — here, by the wise <s>Veṅkaṭeśa</s>, for the repose of all disputants, the ancient path in matters of reasoning has been purified — a shady, thornless road.

children.text: śuddhiṃ bibhrati mādṛśāṃ bhaṇitayaścūḍānvaye kevalaṃ prānte miśramabhāṇi nītinipuṇaiḥ kiṃ teṣvamantavyatā /
children.translated_text: If my utterances bear purity only in the succession of [initial] crests, and toward the end something mixed was spoken — what of that, even for those skilled in reasoning? Is there anything that should not be considered?

children.text: yuktaṃ vargayuge vimṛśya saradhāpuṣpakramaṃ yauktikai- raṅgīkartumaśakyanihnavaguṇagrantho nibandho mama //
children.translated_text: Having deliberated upon the pair of groups [of topics] with the order of arrows and flowers, it is fitting [to accept] — my composition is a treatise of incontestable merit, incapable of being dismissed by the logically-minded.

When devotion settles upon <s>Brahman</s>, who is rooted in the threefold <s>Veda</s> (<s>Nigama</s>), who is the wish-fulfilling jewel (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) of all the worlds, who has attained [our] trust, who is the abode upon which contemplation rests,

children.text: ratiṃ bhajati bhāvanā layamivopayāti drutaṃ ramāvasumatīsahācaritadharmaṇi brahmaṇi //
children.translated_text: and who is accompanied by <s>Ramā</s> (Śrī) and <s>Vasumatī</s> (Earth) in His eternal nature — then contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) attains love, and quickly reaches absorption (<s>laya</s>).

children.text: iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu nyāyapariśuddhau prameyādhyāye dvitīyamāhnikam //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the works of <s>Śrī Kavitārkikasiṃha</s> (the lion among poets and logicians), <s>Sarvatantrasvatantra</s> (master of all systems), the blessed <s>Veṅkaṭanātha</s>, the <s>Vedāntācārya</s> — in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s>, in the chapter on <s>Prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge), the second session (<s>āhnika</s>).
And thus the fifth chapter is concluded.
And the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) is completely finished.
Salutation to the blessed <s>Nigamānta Mahādeśika</s>.
